Sports.title: Mikel Arteta swerves question on Max Dowman red card but Arsenal manager’s death stare said it all
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta swerves question on Max Dowman red card but Arsenal manager’s death stare said it all

Mikel Arteta refused to criticise Max Dowman for his red card during Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup exit.

The Gunners suffered one of the most humiliating nights in their history as they succumbed to a penalty shootout defeat to League Two Fleetwood Town.

6 Fans stormed the pitch at Highbury Stadium as Fleetwood produced one of the all-time shocks in the League Cup's history Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

6 Arsenal haven't won the competition since 1993 Credit: Getty

Bruno Guimaraes' spot-kick was saved by Fleetwood goalkeeper Jay Lynch, allowing Conor Haughey to fire in the decisive penalty to seal a famous result for the Cod Army.

Fleetwood took the lead when Aaron Loupalo-Bi rolled young Arsenal defender Marli Salmon before slotting past Illan Meslier.

The Premier League champions responded through Viktor Gyokeres' scrappy finish early in the second half and controlled possession throughout but were unable to find a winner.

Arsenal's task at getting over the line when Max Dowman was sent off for a kick out after a crunching challenge on him by Harrison Neal.

After trudging off the pitch, Arteta made a comment to the 16-year-old, who then made his way down the tunnel to digest his disappointment.

Arteta was also seen staring at his player intensely as he went for the tunnel.

The Arsenal boss didn't give any indication about what he said to Dowman during that exchange and also didn't point the finger of blame at him.

Arteta tight lipped on Dowman

"First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through in the next round in the manner that they've done it, the atmosphere they've created" Arteta told Sky Sports.

"A very sad day for us. I cannot fault the attitude of the players, I haven't seen anyone not do what is required at this level.

"We had so much of the ball, so many chances, so many shots and if you want the margins to be bigger then you need to capitalise and we didn't. Football is about that."

6 Dowman was dismissed after a petulant kick out during a confrontation Credit: Getty

6 It seems unlikely Arteta was saying 'unlucky mate' after Dowman was red carded Credit: Getty

"It's difficult to see on the cameras like that, I prefer to watch it back properly so I can assess the situation," Arteta said of the incident leading to Dowman's red.

"We will learn from everything, yeah," Arteta said when asked if Dowman will learn from his indiscretions.

Incredible night for Fleetwood

As for Fleetwood, they march onto the quarter-finals with the most famous result in their 118-year history.

The Lancashire-based outfit showed great composure as they slotted home five penalties, despite according to manager Matt Lawlor not practising their spot-kicks in the lead-up to the tie.

"I'm absolutely buzzing proud," Lawlor told talkSPORT. "I'm proud as anything. I'm really ecstatic for the club, I'm ecstatic for the players.

"We've got to the fourth round and we played Sheffield United in the last round, which was a massive mammoth task for us, obviously being League Two and going down a model of how we want to go down with young players and obviously being financially completely separate.

6 Fleetwood are only two points above safety in League Two but are in the last eight of the League Cup Credit: Getty

6 The appointment of Lawlor as Fleetwood boss in January has proven to be a masterstroke Credit: Getty

"Arsenal coming here, we were realistic but we have to believe.

"Obviously, I'm a very passionate human being. Those that will speak around me about me, I might lack certain bits but I'm very, very, very passionate.

"I know my pre-match speech was about passion and playing with passion, being proud and showing the town, the club and the nation about what we are.

"I think we did that in… listen, we're never going to dominate the ball against them players, are we?

"We had to show it in a different way and we pressed a little bit different. All the nonsense you hear in football these days, we pressed a little bit different, obviously, because we came up against the champions.

"There were tactical things on Sunday and Monday and it was more passion and a bit of rah-rah before the game."

Sports.title: Iconic European derby being shown live on free to air TV this weekend
Sports.content:
Iconic European derby being shown live on free to air TV this weekend

AC Milan's derby clash with bitter rivals Inter Milan will be broadcast on free to air TV in the UK this weekend.

The 247th edition of the Derby della Madonnina takes place on Saturday, with kick-off at 7:45pm GMT.

3 The Derby della Madonnina between Milan and Inter will be live on the BBC Credit: Getty

It sees two of this season's title contenders face off at the San Siro.

Both clubs are unbeaten after eight matches ahead of midweek clashes as Milan host Bologna and Inter visit Venezia on Wednesday.

For reigning champions Inter, they are dropped just two points so far this season with seven wins to their name, trailing Serie A leaders Lazio by three points with a game in hand.

As for Milan, Ruben Amorim's side are a further four points back in fifth after picking up five wins and three draws to date.

Milan Derby live on in the UK

Fans in the UK will be able to watch the match live on BBC Two and BBC iPlayer.

Coverage gets underway five minutes before kick-off at 7:40pm.

As well as being shown on BBC Two, the match will also be available to viewers on BBC iPlayer.

The BBC will provide coverage from the San Siro as part of their Serie A rights package.

This season will see 38 matches shown across BBC Alba and BBC Sport as part of the deal.

Whilst 19 fixtures are aired on BBC Alba with Gaelic and English co-commentary, a further 19 are live on BBC iPlayer with English commentary.

3 BBC Two will have live coverage from the San Siro on Saturday night Credit: Getty

A host of familiar names to Premier League fans could feature in the match, which is one of Europe's most iconic derbies.

They include England defender Fikayo Tomori and Nottingham Forest loanee Omari Hutchinson, who are both part of the current Milan side.

However, team-mate Ruben Loftus-Cheek will miss the match through injury.

As for Inter, their squad includes Three Lions trio John Stones, Djed Spence and Curtis Jones.

Recent Derby della Madonnina history

Ahead of Sunday's clash, Inter have the upper hand in the fixture, winning 91 of the previous 247 meetings to Milan's 84.

The Nerazzurri have not beaten their rivals since April 2024, a winless run stretching back seven matches.

3 The San Siro will host the 247th meeting between Milan and Inter Credit: AFP

AC Milan vs Inter Milan: Last five meetings March 2026: AC Milan 1-0 Inter Milan - Serie A November 2025: Inter Milan 0-1 AC Milan - Serie A April 2025: Inter Milan 0-3 AC Milan - Coppa Italia April 2025: AC Milan 1-1 Inter Milan - Coppa Italia February 2025: AC Milan 1-1 Inter Milan - Serie A

Those fixtures include three successive wins for Milan, including a 1-0 victory in this fixture last season thanks to Pervis Estupinan's first half goal.

Despite their league double over Inter last term, though, they were unable to prevent their city rivals from winning a 21st Serie A title.

Milan's current unbeaten run against Inter is their longest for 21 years.

The Rossoneri previously went 10 meetings without losing between November 2002 and April 2005.

Sports.title: Fans storm pitch as Arsenal stunned by League Two Fleetwood in iconic Cupset after Max Dowman red
Sports.content:
Fans storm pitch as Arsenal stunned by League Two Fleetwood in iconic Cupset after Max Dowman red

Arsenal suffered a shock Carabao Cup fourth-round exit as they were dumped out by League Two side Fleetwood on penalties.

After the match finished 1-1 at the end of normal time - which saw Max Dowman sent off for violent conduct - the Gunners lost the shootout 5-3 to give the fourth-tier outfit a famous win at Highbury.

7 Arsenal's players were left stunned at full-time as they suffered a shock upset

7 Fleetwood fans spilled onto the pitch at full-time to celebrate a famous night

Bruno Guimaraes missed the decisive penalty in the shootout, as he saw his effort saved by Jay Lynch in the Fleetwood goal.

Conor Haughey then showed total composure to fire home the winning spot-kick, sending Illan Meslier the wrong way to send his side into the Carabao Cup quarter-finals.

This sparked huge scenes of celebration, as Fleetwood fans piled onto the pitch to celebrate arguably their greatest-ever result.

It sees Arsenal suffer a huge upset, with the Premier League champions succumbing to League Two's 18th-placed side in the first-ever meeting between the two clubs.

Famous night for Fleetwood

The thrilling shootout came after the Gunners had initially avoided a giant-killing in normal time.

Aaron Loupalo-Bi gave Fleetwood a shock lead on 21 minutes, outmuscling young defender Marli Salmon before slotting the ball past Meslier to spark pandemonium among the home fans.

But the Gunners fought back, with Viktor Gyokeres bundling home a scrappy equaliser early into the second half.

As the game headed towards extra time, the game then took a turn as teenage sensation Max Dowman was shown a straight red card.

The 16-year-old was given his marching orders for his reaction to a heavy challenge from Fleetwood's Harrison Neal.

Dowman appeared to kick out at Neal prompting a straight red card, which drew a cold reaction from Arteta as he walked down the tunnel, before his side succumbed to an embarrassing exit on penalties.

7 Aaron Lupalo-Bi fired Fleetwood in front against Mikel Arteta's side Credit: Getty

7 Max Dowman was shown a first-ever senior red card in the huge upset Credit: Getty

7 Conor Haughey was mobbed by fans after his penalty sent Fleetwood through to the Carabao Cup quarter-finals Credit: Getty

For Gunners fans, this will bring back unwanted memories of their 2012 fourth round exit to Bradford, when they were also dumped out by League Two opposition on penalties.

The result ends Arsenal's hopes of League Cup glory for another year, having not tasted glory in the competition since 1993.

It marks a stark turnaround from last year, where Arteta's side made it all the way to the final before being beaten by Manchester City before ultimately pipping them to the Premier League title.

As for Fleetwood, their historic result means are now set for their first-ever quarter-final appearance in the competition.

The Cods will find out their quarter-final opponents when the draw takes place following the conclusion of Chelsea's game against Liverpool on Wednesday.

Arteta on 'sad' defeat and Dowman red card

Arsenal boss Arteta cut a disconsolate figure after his side's shock Carabao Cup exit, but insisted he couldn't fault his players' efforts.

7 Arteta now has one less competition to focus on after his side's Carabao Cup upset Credit: AFP

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Spaniard said: "First of all, congratulations to Fleetwood for going through to the next round in the manner they've done it.

"A really sad day for us. I cannot fault at all the attitude of the players, I haven't seen anybody not doing what is required at this level but we had so much of the ball, had so many chances, so many shots and if you want the margins to be bigger than going to penalties, you have to capitalise on that.

"We didn't and football is about that."

Meanwhile, Arteta opted to swerve questions about youngster Dowman's red card, despite appearing furious at the time.

As the teenager walked down towards the tunnel, the Gunners boss appeared to give him a death stare before dishing out a harsh telling off.

However, when asked about it, Arteta simply replied: “It’s difficult to see on the camera.

7 Arteta appeared to have some harsh words for Dowman after his sending off Credit: Getty

"I prefer to watch it back properly so I can assess the situation.”

Dowman's red card came after the starlet was handed the opportunity to impress from the start after his record-breaking display in the last round.

After scoring twice in a 4-2 away win over Ipswich Town, he was chosen to start in the No.10 role ahead of Eberechi Eze.

The decision followed Arsenal stars Adrian Clarke and Perry Groves backing Dowman to start in the position on talkSPORT's Inside Gooners, tipping him to edge ahead of Eze in the pecking order with a strong display.

However, Eze might just keep his nose in front after the 16-year-old brief loss of control summed up a miserable night at Fleetwood.

Sports.title: Fleetwood vs Arsenal stopped as drone flying over stadium sparks police intervention
Sports.content:
Fleetwood vs Arsenal stopped as drone flying over stadium sparks police intervention

Arsenal's Carabao Cup fourth round tie against Fleetwood Town was suspended for nine minutes after a drone flew over the stadium.

Referee Michael Salisbury stopped play inside two minutes of kick-off due to the incident.



3 The match was stopped after just two minutes by the referee Credit: Getty

The referee could be seen speaking to officials on the touchline following his decision to stop the action.

Both sets of players remained on the pitch at Highbury Stadium whilst the match was halted.

However, the pause in play lasted for several minutes, causing the players to begin passing balls between them to stay warm.



Supporters inside the stadium made their feelings known, meanwhile, booing as Salisbury spoke to the two managers.

Salisbury at one point ordered the players off the pitch, however, he reversed his decision after a conversation with a police officer pitchside having been assured the drone was safely away.



Following a delay of around eight minutes, the match resumed.

talkSPORT understands police had located the operator of the drone.

The last 16 clash had kicked off at 8pm, live on talkSPORT, with a place in the quarter-finals up for grabs.

Just 12 minutes after the match restarted, the home side grabbed a shock lead through striker Aaron Loupalo-Bi.



The on-loan Fulham man broke the deadlock after racing onto a ball in behind the Arsenal defence.

3 Play was suspended for around eight minutes at Highbury Stadium Credit: AFP

Once inside the penalty area, he evaded a challenge from Marli Salmon before slotting through the legs of Illan Meslier.

It is the 20-year-old's fourth goal since joining Fleetwood from the Cottagers in August.



Tonight's tie marks the first competitive meeting between the Gunners and their League Two opponents.

Meanwhile, this season marks the Cods' best Carabao Cup performance in their history.

After reaching the fourth round for the first time, Fleetwood are the lowest-ranked side left in the competition.

Matt Lawlor's side have beaten Chesterfield, Shrewsbury Town and Sheffield United to get this far.



3 Fleetwood took a shock first half lead against the Gunners Credit: AFP

In contrast, the Gunners are two-time winners of the League Cup, most recently in 1993.

Arsenal reached the final of the competition last season, losing 2-0 to Manchester City at Wembley Stadium.

Sports.title: New Max Dowman role could be bad news for £67m Arsenal star
Sports.content:
New Max Dowman role could be bad news for £67m Arsenal star

Eberechi Eze has been warned he may have to settle for a different Arsenal role if Max Dowman can make the most of his latest chance.

The teenage sensation has been handed a start in the No.10 role against Fleetwood Town in the Carabao Cup fourth round.

4 Dowman will start in the No.10 role for Arsenal against Fleetwood Credit: Getty

Arsenal head to Highbury Stadium to face the League Two side on Tuesday for a place in the quarter-finals, live on talkSPORT.

Dowman has once again been handed the opportunity to impress from the start after his record-breaking display in the last round.

The 16-year-old scored twice in a 4-2 away win over Ipswich Town.

With Martin Odegaard only on the bench, he has now been chosen ahead of Eze to start in the No.10 position.

Dowman's new Arsenal role

Former Arsenal stars Adrian Clarke and Perry Groves believe whilst it is an opportunity for Dowman, it could spell bad news for Eze.

The pair discussed the competition for places in that area of the pitch during the latest episode of talkSPORT's Inside Gooners alongside host Nick Bright.

Calling for Dowman to play centrally, Clarke explained: "Max Dowman at 10 for me.

"He was unbelievable, it was one of the best performances I’ve seen by anyone actually this season in the game against Ipswich.

"Dowman was outrageously good and I’d like to think he could do something similar against Fleetwood, who will try to make it a battle.

"But truth be told, we should be able to ‘out-football’ them and get the job done with a degree of comfort.

4 Eze missed out on the No.10 berth to Dowman on Tuesday night Credit: AFP

"It’s an important night for Max because with Bukayo Saka out now, he will be more in the manager’s thinking as an option to start Premier League games.

"What we need from him in this match is another eye-catching display."

Saka is set to be sidelined until at least the start of December with a quad injury.

His absence could open the door for Dowman, who has predominantly featured on the right for the Gunners.

However, the forward starred in the No.10 against Ipswich last month and now has the chance to do so again away to Fleetwood.

Eze warning

As for what this could mean for Eze, Groves was asked if the 28-year-old will have been wanting to play in that position on Tuesday night.

4 Dowman made history with two goals against Ipswich in the last round Credit: AFP

He replied: "It’s not a bad position to be in for Mikel Arteta when you’re talking about three No.10s who have that amount of quality.

"I think for Eze, he’s just got to concentrate on wherever he plays, and it looks like he’s going to get a run on the left-hand side, he’s got to make sure he reaches the levels like he did against Bayern Munich.

"I thought he looked sharper against Everton. He looked sharper on the ball. When he’s flowing, he’s got that sort of fluidity. He’s very graceful in his movement.

"He had about three or four shots from distance against Everton, where he had one thing in his mind to get the ball out of his feet and get a shot away.

"Whereas before, because he was lacking a little bit of confidence, he was playing very safe. He was going square, he was going back.

"I just think with Eberechi Eze, he’s not really in a position to go and knock on Mikel Arteta’s door and demand he wants to play in the 10 position."

4 Eze has been warned he may have to settle for playing on the left for Arsenal Credit: PA

Eze joined Arsenal from Crystal Palace for £67million last summer, penning a four-year deal at the Emirates Stadium.

However, the England midfielder has been afforded just five starts across all competitions this season.

Each of those outings have seen Eze deployed on the left-hand side of the front three, with his only appearances in the No.10 coming as a substitute.

Despite coming off the bench to score as an attacking midfielder against Bayern Munich last week, he returned to the wing from the start at the weekend.

The latest setback for Eze comes after he was warned he may have to settle for a cameo role at Arsenal.

He has completed 90 minutes just nine times, though, with only 41 starts to his name since his arrival in August 2025.

Sports.title: Harry Kane receives offer from Tottenham legend for help over lucrative lucrative new career after football
Sports.content:
Harry Kane receives offer from Tottenham legend for help over lucrative lucrative new career after football

Tottenham legend Clive Allen is ready to lend Harry Kane a helping hand in achieving his post-football aspirations.

The newly-crowned Ballon d’Or winner has never hidden his love for American football and in recent times has expressed an interest in one day becoming a kicker in the NFL.

5 Harry Kane scooped the Ballon d'Or award in London on Monday night Credit: AFP

"It all depends on what happens in my career over the next five or six years, the motivation and what I want to do," Kane said.

"The NFL is a lot more realistic, let's put it that way."

Few would bet against the England captain achieving yet another sporting feat if his recent achievements are anything to go by.

And if he does successfully make the switch to gridiron, then Allen, who actually played American football as a placekicker for the London Monarchs of NFL Europe, is ready to give the Bayern Munich striker a helping hand.

Allen is ready to assist Kane

Asked about the prospect of Kane becoming an NFL kicker, Allen told talkSPORT: "There's talk of it. I'll be happy to help him with that.

“I'm sure, the one thing I know he's got, he's got the leg to do it, that's for sure.

“And you have to have a really strong kicking leg and he will have the mentality to deal with it as well.

“So, yeah, that would be fun to see him try that."

Kane appears well primed for a future in kicking judging by his expertise in hitting the target.

The 33-year-old netted an impressive 73 goals in 65 matches for Bayern and England during the 2025/26 season.

5 Kane has eclipsed a host of goalscoring records during his time at Bayern Credit: Getty

5 Spurs legend Allen has offered his support to Kane Credit: Getty

His numbers played a huge role in Kane becoming the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001.

Since arriving in Germany, Kane has broken a glut of goalscoring records whilst firing the Bundesliga giants to two Bundesliga titles and a German Cup success.

But any potential move across the Atlantic will likely have to wait as Kane has agreed a contract extension at Bayern Munich until 2029.

The striker was also warned that the transition from striker to the idle role of kicker will not be an easy one.

Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Littler claims that while Kane boasts the physical talent and leg power to do it, he warned that the hardest part would be the cultural adjustment.

Little's words of caution

"It's just so different, sitting there on the sidelines the whole game," Little told The Associated Press.

5 Cam Little has highlighted the ket differences between being a striker and an NFL kicker Credit: Getty

5 Kane has been a regular at the NFL's international games Credit: Getty

"You're not going to get on the ball, and you don't have the same moxie, I guess, because he is a star striker for the team.

"So that moxie is just kind of put to the side. You've got to let everyone else do the big man's job, and then you're out there just to back everyone up basically."

"He's probably talented enough to do it. His technique in soccer is so good. But it's just such a different mental, I'd say, challenge than soccer.

"It'd be like him taking five set pieces a day. And he's got to deliver on all five set pieces, or you didn't do your job for the day."

However, Kane has been urged not to join the New York Jets should he get the opportunity in NFL.

"Do you know what's frustrating about that?," talkSPORT's Inside the NFL show host Jay Lawrence said.

"If Harry Kane were to genuinely want to give that a go, then I think it's getting to a point now where he will be too old. It will be a PR exercise for whatever team."

"You know what will happen, Woody Johnson will pay Harry Kane $20m just to get him in the Jets uniform and do some branding," Brian T Smith added.

"Then he ends up on a 3-14 team and is absolutely miserable."

Should Kane eventually make the leap, he wouldn't be the first to transition from football to the NFL.

Dallas Cowboys kicker Brandon Aubrey successfully made the switch to American football after playing in MLS and the USL.

Sports.title: Morgan Gibbs-White’s home burgled as fiancee issues vigilance warning
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White's home was recently burgled, the Nottingham Forest's fiancee revealed on social media.

The England midfielder's partner, Britney De Villiers, took to Instagram to share the news, describing the ordeal as 'unsettling'.



4 Gibbs-White serves as Nottingham Forest's team captain Credit: Getty

The South African model and influencer said on Tuesday that her and Gibbs-White's home had been burgled a 'few days ago'.

Fortunately, she confirmed that neither the couple or their two young children, Greyson and Hayes, were in the house when it was targeted.

However, Britney admitted the situation had left her feeling 'violated' and she urged others to be vigilant and to check their home security systems.



The content creator, who has more than 600k followers on TikTok, described the burglary as 'horrible'.

She wrote on her Instagram story: “I wasn’t going to publicly share this but our home was burgled a few days ago and after hearing about another one since, I feel it’s important to just warn others.



“It’s incredibly unsettling knowing that homes are being targeted.

“Please be extra vigilant, make sure your security systems are on whether you’re in the house or not and report anything suspicious.

“Thankfully, nobody was home when it happened and material things can be replaced but it’s a horrible feeling knowing someone has violated your home, especially when you have young children.



“Please stay safe and look out for one another.”

News of Gibbs-White's home burglary comes less than a week after Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes' home was targeted by a masked gang during his team's 4-1 defeat Como.

4 Britney De Villiers shared the upsetting news of the home burglary on Instagram

4 De Villiers recently posed on the pitch with Gibbs-White after he featured for England in the Autumn internationals Credit: Instagram / @britneydevilliers

The Portuguese midfielder's £4million mansion was broken into by three masked intruders whilst he was in Italy.



It is not clear whether Gibbs-White's home was targeted during Nottingham Forest's 1-1 draw with Ipswich on Friday night.

The Reds' winless run stretched to ten Premier League games in their last outing, with boss Oliver Glasner struggling to make his mark since joining the club on a £13million-per-year contract this summer.

Gibbs-White's personal life

Gibbs-White reportedly met partner Britney through a mutual friend in 2019, before getting engaged in June 2025.

Their eldest son Greyson was born in 2023, and they welcomed a second boy, Hayes, in August 2025.



The Forest star revealed after Hayes' arrival that Britney had suffered complications in her pregnancy, which played a part in his decision to stay at the City Ground in the 2025 summer transfer window.

4 Gibbs-White has earned 10 England caps since making his senior debut in 2024 Credit: Getty

The Englishman was at the centre of one of that summer's biggest transfer sagas, when he turned his back on a move to Tottenham after they thought they had activated his £60million release clause.

He later penned a new three-year deal with Forest, where he remains under contract until 2028.



Britney has continued to support Gibbs-White in his career since then, being a regular fixture in the stands as well as backing him online.

After he was initially left out of Thomas Tuchel’s England squad for the extended Autumn international break, she shared a statistic highlighting his chance creation in the Premier League.

And her wish was answered days later, when Gibbs-White received a late call-up following Cole Palmer's withdrawal.

Sports.title: Hulk Hogan's daughter rages after selling his $5.9M Florida mansion: 'Enjoy your dirty money'
Sports.content:
The daughter of late wrestling icon Hulk Hogan expressed her anger over the sale of her father's mansion.

After being listed in January for nearly $11 million, the 5,400sq ft beachfront mansion the 'Hulkster' owned in Clearwater Beach, Florida was recently sold for $5.9 million.

A guest cottage located next door to the mansion was also sold for $2.8 million.

In a rant on Instagram, Brooke Hogan accused close friends and family of trying to make money off her father.

Brooke, 38, shared an image of the property to her Instagram story with a big 'SOLD' sticker across it.

'The sick feeling is indescribable,' Brooke captioned the post.

Brooke Hogan, the daughter of late WWE icon Hulk Hogan, called out family and friends after her dad's Clearwater Beach properties were sold off for millions of dollars

The 5,400sq ft beachfront mansion the 'Hulkster' owned in Clearwater Beach sold for $5.9m

She wrote in her Instagram story rant: 'Enjoy your dirty money. You took my dad.'

Brooke continued her posts by speaking about the years she lived at the home with her father and Hulk's ex-wife Jennifer McDaniel, who was married to him from 2010 to 2021.

'We cooked, we watched Jerry Springer, we played music, we cried,' she continued.

'I walked in that garage every visit and hugged him right when he'd open the garage door. I'd sit next to him for hours in the chair he died in.'

Brooke revealed that she and McDaniel cared for Hulk for years during multiple health battles, including back surgeries and knee and hip replacements.

From there, she called out people who she believes took advantage of her father, born Terry Gene Bollea, after his passing.

'First Jen-who no one but me treated with respect. Then I was gone...the truth teller...I'm sure to everyone's delight,' she posted.

'And now it's all gone. Sold for profit. Just like him...used for f***ing everyone else's gain. Saddest ending I've ever seen. You know who TF you are.'

Further posts included another photo of the house with a pointed caption: 'Enjoy your dirty money. You took my dad.'

Brooke says she asked to be written out of her father's will to avoid fights over his estate

Brooke added that many people only showed up when they wanted something out of Hulk Hogan, not when he needed help.

'Apparently EVERYONE will show up at the end if you're famous enough and they can profit off your demise,' she wrote.

In a follow-up post, Brooke clarified that she wasn't calling out any WWE Wrestlers, rather specific friends and family who used Hogan's fame for their own benefit.

She told US Magazine: 'There’s something deeply unsettling about watching a person’s life and memories reduced to transactions.

'Some people see a home filled with history and love. Others simply see what it’s worth. I’ve learned that the way people move when there’s nothing left to gain from someone anymore can tell you everything about how they valued them when they were alive.'

Back in 2023, Hulk wrote Brooke out of his will, making her brother, Nick, Hulk's sole beneficiary. Brooke previously revealed that she asked to be removed from the will as she didn't want to be involved in any fights over money.

'I've had to hear everyone say I'm the jerk for stepping away from the toxic behavior and brainwashing, fake, greedy people… 'I should have been there.' 'Everyone else' was there till the end. NO. They were there AT the end. To collect,' she wrote.

Sports.title: Arsenal's defeat by Fleetwood is the greatest upset in the history of the Carabao Cup: Premier League champions sunk by League Two side on dismal night for Mikel Arteta, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Beside the tram tracks that run all the way down to Blackpool and the Pleasure Beach, just along from the hulking iron anchor embedded in the pavement at the start of Fisherman’s Walk, they were doing a brisk trade at The Eating Plaice as kick-off edged closer.

One of the ladies behind the counter upbraided a customer who was taking his plate of fish and chips through to the restaurant. ‘You’ve done yourself there, love,’ she said. ‘If you’d ordered in there, you could have had fish and chips, mushy peas, a brew and bread and butter for £10.95.’

There is a frontier feel about this town, a bit like Barrow-in-Furness on the other side of Morecambe Bay. Sea salt in the veins and a harbour that was once home to a flotilla of trawlers. The wind blows through it so hard it whisks away anything that is not nailed down. The Vintage Emporium and Odditorium advertises its wares near the seafront.

It feels like giant-killing country here. Especially on Tuesday evening when a gale blew through the ground, bending the corner flags and threatening to sweep laptops off the press tables and dislodge red and blue hats from the heads of the Cod Army regulars who filed into the stands and leaned against the crush barriers on the terraces behind the goals.

This was Highbury, but not as Arsenal know it. There is nothing Art Deco about any of the stands at Fleetwood Town’s delightful ground. The capacity is 5327. The trendy restaurants of Upper Street are not a short walk away down Holloway Road. This is a different kind of Highbury. A single-storey sports and social club sits behind the touchline opposite the main stand. A banner proclaiming ‘Up the Cods’ hung behind one of the goals.

Arsenal have been knocked out of the Carabao Cup on penalties by League Two Fleetwood

After taking the lead in the 21st minute, Arsenal scored through Viktor Gyokeres in the second half - but Fleetwood Town managed to hang on

It is more than 20 years since Arsenal – who brought 1100 fans north with them - played the final game at their Highbury but even though this Carabao Cup fourth round tie on the Fylde Coast only pitted them against a team that languishes two points outside the relegation zone in League Two, 85 places adrift of them in the pyramid, Mikel Arteta picked a strong side.

It is a million miles from the Ballon d’Or ceremony at the London Palladium, where Arteta had lost out to Luis de la Fuente in the manager of the year category, to this football outpost by the sea but the Arsenal boss gave every signal that he and his team were approaching the task with relish. His line-up included Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

They are not strangers to tricky trips like this. They negotiated a visit to Mansfield Town’s Field Mill ground in the FA Cup last season with aplomb. Teenagers Max Dowman and Marli Salmon started that game just as they started this one. Arteta also handed a debut to 18-year-old Ceadach O’Neill.

Arsenal were at Bayern Munich last week and now the champions were playing their part in the biggest game in Fleetwood’s history. The game even began with a rare curiosity – less than two minutes into the match, play was halted by the sight of a drone of unknown provenance hovering over the pitch.

The referee informed both managers of the issue and the players tried to keep warm in the hiatus. The teams were brought to the sidelines before play was resumed after a seven minute delay. The drone operator, apparently, was apprehended by police in a nearby park. Stick the whole episode in that Odditorium.

Midway through the half, there was some football drama, too. Aaron Loupalo-Bi ran on to a through ball and held off Salmon before turning him and rifling the ball through the legs of Ilhan Meslier. Never has Highbury celebrated a goal against Arsenal with such unbridled joy. The theme to Captain Pugwash, the Fleetwood goal music, carried across the ground on the breeze.

Fleetwood defended well and with great commitment but five minutes after the interval, with Martin Odegaard introduced to the fray, Arsenal were level. O’Neill swung a fine cross into the box and after a bit of pinball, Gyokeres forced it over the line. Five minutes later, Jay Lynch pulled off a last-ditch save to deny Havertz from close range.

Dowman was shown his marching orders for kicking Harrison Neal and a less-than-impressed Arteta appeared to say something to the youngster as he headed for the tunnel

Bruno Guimaraes hit an unconvincing fourth penalty for the Gunners which he saw saved

Odegaard changed the complexion of the game. Arsenal dominated midfield now and started to turn the screw. Havertz prodded into the side-netting, Lewis-Skelly skied an effort over the bar from the edge of the six-yard-box. ‘Champions of England, you’re having a laugh,’ the Cod Army sang.

Five minutes from the end, Dowman, who had been ineffectual, reacted to a challenge by Harrison Neal and kicked him while he was on the floor. Referee Michael Salisbury showed him a straight red card. Dowman is still only 16. As he trudged off the pitch, Arteta muttered something in his ear. The kid was doing his GCSEs last summer. This will be a valuable part of his football education.

Lynch saved brilliantly from Ben White in the dying seconds and the tie went straight to penalties. Arsenal, incredibly, blinked first. Bruno Guimaraes hit their fourth penalty to the keeper’s left and Lynch dived to push it out. Conor Haughey stepped up to take Fleetwood’s fifth and smashed it into the roof of the net.

Fleetwood were in the quarter-finals of the Carabao Cup after causing the greatest upset in the history of the competition. The Cod Army invaded the pitch at the end. Highbury had done its worst. Arsenal were out.

Sports.title: Steve Borthwick has finally put his England players on notice - now it's time they delivered if they want to be anywhere near the plane to the World Cup, writes ALEX BYWATER
Sports.content:
Steve Borthwick has finally put his England players on notice - now it's time they delivered if they want to be anywhere near the plane to the World Cup, writes ALEX BYWATER

Steve Borthwick has put his England stars on a World Cup countdown ahead of a crunch autumn – and revealed he hopes No10 Fin Smith will be fit for his team’s campaign opener.

Next month's Nations Championship clashes against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, before the finals weekend on November 27-29, take place less than a year out from the 2027 World Cup. Borthwick has admitted that means the onus is on his players to perform now or risk missing out on selection for the tournament Down Under.

Borthwick is sweating on the fitness of star playmaker Smith to face Australia a week on Sunday, as he continues to recover from a calf injury suffered in action for Northampton against Leicester.

‘We’ve got 12 Tests to the World Cup,’ Borthwick said. ‘There are 10 Tests until I name the 33-man squad. There are nine Tests until I name the World Cup training squad.

‘This series of games is the last opportunity we have playing southern hemisphere opposition before we’re at that World Cup. I’m looking forward to seeing players compete and perform against this calibre of opposition. You start looking at the squad and think people are fighting for places to be in that World Cup. I think the lads are excited by that.’

Borthwick oversaw the worst Six Nations campaign in England's history at the start of this year. A fifth-place finish heaped the pressure on the former second row, but he was backed by the RFU and his contract was extended to the 2028 Six Nations.

Steve Borthwick (left) has put his England players on notice with less than a year to go to the World Cup

Borthwick suffered a significant blow with an injury to first-choice fly-half Fin Smith (centre), who is in a race against time to be fit for Australia a week on Sunday

NATIONS CHAMPIONSHIP FIXTURES Nov 8 England v Australia , Twickenham Nov 14 England v Japan , Twickenham Nov 21 England v New Zealand , Twickenham Nov 27-29 Finals weekend , Twickenham

Too often these days, international rugby coaches are reticent to admit their teams have to win or that players must deliver to avoid being dropped. Instead, they blather on about being on a ‘journey’ where it is the level of ‘performance’ and not the result that matters.

Such rhetoric has become painful and unnecessary, and Borthwick's comments were a refreshing shot in the arm. The 47-year-old has effectively put his players on trial. The message was obvious – if you don’t perform now, you won’t be on the plane to Australia.

Hallelujah! That is exactly what this England team needs. For too long, the country’s leading players have been allowed to underperform as a collective without any real risk of jeopardy. That, thankfully, now seems to be at an end.

England’s stars need to know that failure to deliver must come with consequences. It might be a stretch to say England’s environment has become too comfortable, but the players will be all the better for being put on their toes. Borthwick’s messaging will also be music to the ears of the likes of Northampton’s George Hendy, who missed out on selection and must consider himself unlucky to do so.

Borthwick’s hopes for a fast autumn start haven’t been helped by the setback to Smith, who hasn’t trained with England this week. ‘He has made good progress over the past couple of days and we are hopeful of his availability for the Australia Test,’ Borthwick said of Smith.

‘But that remains unclear at this stage. With calf injuries in particular, you monitor those closely. I'll be assessing that right at the start of the week, but all the news we've got so far is very positive. If Fin’s not available for selection, we have some quality fly-halves in George Ford and Marcus Smith available also. So, we're in a positive position.’

Borthwick confirmed on Tuesday that Bath flanker Guy Pepper (ankle) and Bristol centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg (concussion) won’t play any part this autumn.

Wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso should be fit for Australia after a hamstring problem. Daily Mail Sport understands he is set to be involved for Exeter against Harlequins on Saturday.

Wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso should be fit for Australia after a hamstring problem

It's about time a head coach told things how they are - and now England's players must deliver

England beat a weaker New Zealand at Twickenham last year - it's more than feasible that they can repeat the trick this autumn

Pepper’s absence is a blow to Borthwick as the 23-year-old has established himself as a key member of the set-up. Bath were hit by a double blow on Tuesday as they also confirmed their Argentina full-back Santi Carreras will miss the rest of the season with a serious knee injury.

A defining autumn awaits Borthwick and his squad. England must beat Australia, regardless of whether Smith is fit or not, take down Japan and at the very least push New Zealand all the way. It is more than feasible for them to beat the All Blacks, as they did this time last year at Twickenham against a weaker touring side.

England might have fitness issues, but they can cover for Smith and Pepper. They have a strong squad with good depth. As Borthwick pointed out, even if Smith doesn’t make it for the Wallabies he has fine alternatives in namesake Marcus and George Ford. Henry Pollock or either Tom or Ben Curry can cover for Pepper.

It’s time England’s players delivered. Now, at last, Borthwick has admitted it too.

Sports.title: How Michael Carrick survived as Man United boss after 72 hours of drama: Why Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada were reluctant to pull the trigger and the signs he was keeping his job after being given stay of execution
Sports.content:
How Michael Carrick survived as Man United boss after 72 hours of drama: Why Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada were reluctant to pull the trigger and the signs he was keeping his job after being given stay of execution

At the end of a remarkable 72 hours of drama and mystery at Manchester United, Michael Carrick has survived as head coach. For now, at least.

Is it a fresh start or merely a stay of execution? Time will tell, but it feels as though Carrick won’t have long unless he can buck the trend of disastrous results and lifeless performances this season, starting at Chelsea on Saturday lunchtime.

It seemed unlikely that Carrick would even last until then when he left the pitch at Old Trafford on Sunday after a 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth with tears in his eyes and a wave of the right hand towards the Stretford End that looked suspiciously like a goodbye.

Carrick had the look of a broken man and admitted in his post-match press conference that he didn’t know whether he would be sacked.

Two men who would have a big say in that decision, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, had been down to the United dressing-room but did not stay long to chat with him.

That night, representatives from United were conspicuous by their absence from the Northern Football Writers’ awards dinner in Manchester – where David Moyes was honoured for a managerial career that included an all-too-brief spell at Old Trafford – perhaps realising that the club were about to go into crisis mode.

Michael Carrick will stay as Man United boss for now after appearing to be on the brink

Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox held crunch talks with Sir Jim Ratcliffe and co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer on Monday via conference calls

Discussions among the United hierarchy over Carrick’s future assumed even greater intensity in the wake of a defeat that left his team one point above the relegation zone.

Berrada and Wilcox arrived at the club’s Carrington training complex on Monday morning ready to hold conference calls with minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, as well as co-chairmen Joel and Avram Glazer once it was morning in America.

It would not have been lost on the two executives that their own positions could come under scrutiny if United decided to appoint a third head coach this year.

They were also in no doubt about the depth of feeling among United’s fanbase who threw their support behind Carrick on Sunday while rounding angrily on the Glazers, Ratcliffe, Wilcox and the players. Sacking the one man who is still popular with the fans was a big step.

Then there would be the process of agreeing on a replacement – Daily Mail Sport revealed that Wilcox favours a Premier League proven manager over Julian Nagelsmann, the preferred choice of director of recruitment Christopher Vivell – as well as the cost of making a change.

Carrick is only six months into a two-year contract and would be due a pay-off, although it’s unclear if there is a break clause at some point.

Meanwhile, Eddie Howe – the main rival to Nagelsmann – would cost United £3million in compensation even though he left Newcastle in the summer.

The players had a day off on Monday, but Carrick arrived at the training ground shortly before a behind-closed-doors game between United’s Under-21s and Hull City was due to kick off at 2pm.

He watched it with his No.2 Steve Holland and Under-18s coach Darren Fletcher before leaving three hours later with his son Jacey, still very much in the dark over his future.

The first signs that Carrick might beat the axe emerged on Monday night when sources hinted that it might not go the way everyone was expecting.

Then the 45-year-old returned to Carrington just before 8am on Tuesday morning dressed in his club tracksuit ready to take training as the players reported back still unsure over his fate.

Carrick was later pictured welcoming fans with life-limiting illnesses to the training ground along with captain Bruno Fernandes, Harry Maguire, Carlos Baleba and Kobbie Mainoo as part of a Dream Day organised by the Manchester United Foundation.

United fans turned on the players after the defeat by Bournemouth but supported Carrick

Carrick took training on Tuesday morning as his squad reported for duty after a planned day off

He will take charge of Saturday's trip to Chelsea but desperately needs an upturn in results

Shortly before noon as Carrick was leaving the training ground, it emerged that he was being given an opportunity to turn the season around and would be in charge for the trip to Stamford Bridge on Saturday.

‘I’m surprised but I’m happy because I was absolutely certain that what I witnessed on Sunday would be the end of Michael,’ his old teammate Gary Neville told Sky Sports.

‘I have no idea how it’s going to go in the next couple of weeks, but I hope he can somehow get those players to start playing for him again because they haven’t played for him for the last few weeks.’

There is sympathy among the United hierarchy that Carrick has been let down by largely the same group of players who only lost two of 17 games under him last season to finish third.

No-one more so than Fernandes who threw his head coach under the bus with his post-match comments in Como last week and was benched against Bournemouth as a result. Carrick must decide how to re-integrate his best player before it’s too late.

Former United assistant boss Mike Phelan, who worked with Carrick on the coaching staff under Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, said to Sky Sports: ‘The players all need to look at themselves and think, “are we doing the best we possibly can to support this manager?”.

‘He will expect them to turn up and be consistent and really play football. Stop talking. Play football.’

Carrick has been unlucky with a spate of injuries to key players this season, but it’s hoped that Mainoo will be available at Stamford Bridge for what feels like a huge game.

The comparisons with two of his predecessors, Erik ten Hag and Solskjaer, are intriguing.

Ten Hag appeared to be a dead man walking before the 2024 FA Cup Final as United interviewed candidates for his job, but won that game and survived for another five months.

Solskjaer was also on the brink after a 5-0 home defeat to Liverpool five years ago this week, and looked to have survived when he won at Tottenham the following week, but only lasted another three games.

Now it’s Carrick’s turn to see how long he can dodge the bullet.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta FUMES at Max Dowman after Arsenal star, 16, sent off in shock Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood as Gunners manager's angry reaction is caught on camera
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta FUMES at Max Dowman after Arsenal star, 16, sent off in shock Carabao Cup defeat by Fleetwood as Gunners manager's angry reaction is caught on camera

A furious Mikel Arteta appeared to scold Max Dowman after the 16-year-old was sent off in the latter stages of Arsenal's shock Carabao Cup defeat against Fleetwood Town.

The teenage winger was dismissed in the closing stages of the fourth round tie after reacting to a challenge from Harrison Neal.

Neal had slid into a challenge on Dowman, with the Arsenal star responding by appearing to try to kick out at the Fleetwood player, sparking a melee.

Dowman was shown a straight red card for the act, with Arsenal forced to play out the closing stages with 10-men.

As Dowman made his way off the pitch, Arteta was seen walking towards Dowman and appeared to be seen sternly addressing the youngster.

Former Arsenal star Paul Merson, speaking on Sky Sports, expressed his concerns over the incident at full-time.

Mikel Arteta appeared to scold Max Dowman after his red card in their shock cup defeat to Fleetwood Town

Dowman had reacted to a strong challenge from Harrison Neal and appeared to lash out

Dowman was shown a straight red card following the incident in the closing stages of the match

WHEN YOUNG STARS SEE RED Wayne Rooney – Everton vs Birmingham, December 2002 Rooney became the youngest player to be sent off in the Premier League after he saw red in the closing stages of Everton’s Boxing Day clash against Birmingham City. Aged 17 years and 63 days old at the time, Rooney’s aggression got the better of him as he was dismissed 15 minutes after coming on as a substitute. Rooney had miscontrolled the ball and responded with a late challenge on Steve Vickers, catching the defender on his ankle. Everton boss David Moyes suggested Rooney should have been shown a yellow card but Birmingham manager Steve Bruce stated post-match that Vickers had required eight stitches after the incident. Michael Owen – Liverpool vs Man United, April 1998 An 18-year-old Owen saw red as Liverpool drew 1-1 with rivals Manchester United in the Premier League. Owen had earlier equalised for Liverpool as the forward cancelled out a Ronny Johnsen opener. The two players were then involved in the incident that saw Owen’s match come to a premature end. The Liverpool star was shown a second yellow card for a late challenge on Johnsen, who was ultimately forced off on a stretcher. Man United boss Sir Alex Ferguson hit out at Owen post-match over a what he labelled a ‘terrible tackle’. Myles Lewis-Skelly – Arsenal vs Wolves, January 2025 The Arsenal youngster was controversially shown a straight red card for a foul on Matt Doherty during a 1-0 victory. Lewis-Skelly had caught Doherty on his ankle as the Wolves full back looked to break, with Arteta stating post-match that he was ‘absolutely fuming’ at the decision. Arsenal succeeded in overturning Lewis-Skelly’s three-match ban following an appeal. Lewis-Skelly was sent off for a second time just weeks later. Lionel Messi - Argentina vs Hungary, August 2005 Messi’s Argentina debut lasted just 47 seconds as the 18-year-old was sent off moments after coming off the bench in a friendly against Hungary. The Barcelona sensation had barely touched the ball before being pulled back by Hungary’s Vilmos Vanczak. Messi responded by swinging his arm back, hitting Vanczak in the face. Despite protestations from his Argentina team-mates, Messi was sent off for violent conduct by the referee.

'This didn't look good to me at all,' Merson said.

'For me, I didn't like that.'

Arteta provided little insight into what he told Dowman, with the Arsenal boss telling the BBC he said 'Something that we discussed already before the match.'

When asked by Sky Sports, Arteta added on the red card: It's difficult to see on the cameras like that, so I prefer to watch it back properly and then I can assess the situation.'

When asked whether Dowman would learn from the incident, Arteta responded: 'Yeah, we'll learn from everything.'

The straight red card came on a dismal night for Arsenal as the reigning English champions stunningly crashed out of the competition on penalties to their League Two opponents.

Arsenal had fallen behind in the first half to Aaron Loupalo-Bi, before Viktor Gyokeres drew Arteta's side level in the second half.

Bruno Guimaraes crucially missed from the spot in the shootout as Fleetwood scored all five of their penalties to remarkably book their place in the quarter-finals.

Sports.title: Peter Schmeichel accuses Erik ten Hag of 'stirring the pot' with his attack on Man United's owners - and tells former Red Devils boss to look in the mirror: 'How DARE he go out and say that!'
Sports.content:
Peter Schmeichel has slammed former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag for 'stirring the pot' amid yet another turbulent period for the club. Ten Hag conducted a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic last week in which he criticised Cristiano Ronaldo for 'letting the team down', as well as hitting out at the club's hierarchy for contributing to a 'toxic culture'. The Dutchman, who joined United at the end of the 2021-22 season before being sacked in October 2024, also revealed that he pleaded with the club to buy Harry Kane and Declan Rice during his tenure. In his first summer at United, after a move for the Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong fell through, Ten Hag asked about the possibility of signing Rice, but West Ham did not want to sell their captain. 'I think we could have done more to test. They tried but I don’t know how the process went,' he said. The interview has come amid a tricky spell for United, with manager Michael Carrick feeling the heat after recording eight matches without a win in all competitions, as well as inflammatory interviews from captain Bruno Fernandes and defender Lisandro Martinez in the media. Speaking on The Overlap Daily, former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said: 'What really annoys me in everything that has happened in the past two weeks is Ten Hag coming out and saying that he wanted Declan Rice and Harry Kane, like he was a god. 'It's so ridiculous. He brought (Lisandro) Martinez in, (Matthijs) de Ligt. I mean he brought players in that are still there, how dare he go out and say that. 'Everybody knew we should sign Harry Kane. Everyone knows we should have signed Declan Rice, that's no secret. I don't know why we didn't do that. Schmeichel has slammed former Man United manager Erik ten Hag for 'stirring the pot' with his recent comments that criticised the club (Source: overlapdaily/YouTube) Ten Hag conducted a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic last week in which he hit out at the club's hierarchy for contributing to a 'toxic culture'

Your browser does not support iframes.

Your browser does not support iframes.

'But you have now people stirring the pot where they should just keep calm and not talk and maybe talk about what they did for this football club themselves, or what they didn't do. 'He wasn't a success at Manchester United. Why does he feel the need to come out and say that? 'What he's saying is "I was let down by the club" and there might be an element of truth in that but he wasn't good enough. And then he went to Bayer Leverkusen, a team who had just won the Bundesliga, and then he got sacked within, what, three games? 'Maybe just take a step back and don't put yourself in that because then you will end up with someone like me criticising him, and there's no need for that. We don't need it in the narrative.' Ten Hag was sacked by United in October 2024 after a string of poor results left the team 14th in the Premier League. His future had been in doubt after he led United to a disappointing eighth-placed finish in the top flight a couple of months earlier, but victory in the FA Cup final over rivals Manchester City contributed to the club's decision to give him a contract extension in the summer after crunch talks in Ibiza. He went on to replace Xabi Alonso at Bundesliga side Bayer Leverkusen the following season, but was sacked after just three games in charge, and he criticised the club's board for this 'unprecedented' decision. Meanwhile, United confirmed today that under-fire boss Michael Carrick will be given the chance to turn the club's season around.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Carrick will remain in charge for Saturday's trip to Chelsea after Old Trafford bosses decided not to sack him with United in 16th place in the Premier League table, one point clear of the relegation zone. The 45-year-old still faces a battle to improve results and performances and convince his employers that he remains the right man for the job. Like Schmeichel, many former players have been vocal about the club's current situation, with Gary Neville accusing the squad of being 'unprofessional' in an eviscerating attack following the weekend's defeat to Bournemouth. 'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned him for a few months. They've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast. 'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though. He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players. 'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them. 'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should. 'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.' United travel to Stamford Bridge on Saturday, where Carrick will be desperately hoping that his players can finally pick up their first three points since Ipswich at the end of August.

Sports.title: Sky Sports issue FOUR apologies after Fleetwood Town star's hilarious X-rated interview following shock win over Arsenal in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
Sky Sports were forced to repeatedly apologise after a hilarious X-rated interview with Fleetwood Town's victorious EFL Cup stars. The League Two side pulled off one of the biggest upsets in the competition's history after defeating Premier League champions Arsenal on penalties following a 1-1 draw in normal time. The Cod Army scored all of their five spot kicks, and Jay Lynch saved Bruno Guimaraes' penalty to ensure they progressed. Lynch was then joined by Conor Haughey, who scored the match-winning effort, in a wholesome but hilarious post-match interview with Sky Sports. When asked what was going through his head before the decisive moment, Haughey had a slip of the tongue as he said: 'I don't know. 'Pick my spot, hit top corner and run like f***. It's just mental. The boys, I'm so proud of them. It just shows how good the team are.' Sky Sports were forced to repeatedly apologise after a hilarious X-rated interview with Fleetwood Town star Conor Haughey Haughey (L) scored the winning penalty on the greatest night in the League Two side's history Touchline reporter Juliette Ferrington immediately apologised for the language, before she did so again at the end of the interview as Haughey awkwardly looked at her and the camera. When the coverage went back to the studio, Sky Sports then apologised two more times for the language, leaving some fans confused. Meanwhile, in the pitchside interview, Lynch, who also made several key saves in normal time, tried to put into words what the victory meant to him and his team-mates. 'My voice has gone from organising the defence,' he said. 'The whole team throughout the game was magnificent. To beat the English champions - credit to these lads. 'We took heart from Grimsby beating Man Utd last year. We kind of compared it. 'It was a typical night in Fleetwood. We were expecting a storm, we knew the conditions would be horrible, so we thought it might go in our favour. 'It's amazing for the club and the town. Honestly it means everything to everyone.'
