Sports.title: Antonelli will automatically become champion if F1 cancels another race | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli is virtually guaranteed to win the world championship at the Mexican Grand Prix this weekend.

Carlos Sainz Jnr last weekend expressed doubt over whether the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix could go ahead due to the ongoing war between Iran and the USA. The war has already forced the cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix and the relocation of the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia.

This reduced the number of rounds this season from 24 to 23. A further reduction remains possible, and should that happen none of Antonelli’s rivals will be able to prevent him taking the championship.

F1 has indicated it is prepared to hold an alternative final race at Imola in Italy if necessary. However if both races in the Middle East are cancelled and only one replacement event is arranged, the total number of championship points available over the remainder of the season will be reduced.

With 125 points currently remaining, George Russell needs to out-score his team mate by 124 to take the title. Lewis Hamilton needs to beat Antonelli by 125 points.

Both scenarios are extremely unlikely as they would essentially involve the championship leader failing to score any points over the remaining five rounds. But another race cancellation with no replacement, reducing the total points available to 100, would make it impossible for Antonelli to be beaten.

The Moto GP series is due to hold its rescheduled Qatar round on the weekend after the Mexican Grand Prix. However many riders are demanding reassurances from the event promoters about their security, safety and compensation in the event of any last-minute changes.

Only a few F1 world championship titles have not been decided by the result of a grand prix. Max Verstappen won the 2023 world championship in a sprint race, coincidentally held in Qatar. In 1987 Nelson Piquet clinched the title when team mate Nigel Mansell withdrew from the Japanese Grand Prix after injuring his back in a crash during practice.

Sports.title: Keyshawn Davis Ducks $6 Million Question After Richardson Hitchins Says Fight Is Off
Sports.content:
Keyshawn Davis fired back against claims that he priced himself out of facing Richardson Hitchins, yet his heated response sidestepped the actual financial dispute. Davis stated he signed a bout contract back in August and insists Hitchins is the opponent he targets next. He never touched the alleged $6 million purse demand that Hitchins claimed blew up the deal.

Hitchins ignited the dispute on October 23, declaring the contest dead across social media while revealing the financial rift:

“Keyshawn Out Priced himself to fight me Like i said i been agreed to the fight going on 2 months i was wondering what was the hold up but He was asking for 6ms to fight me And mind you boy never even made more than a M in boxing #FIGHTOFF son a clown.”

Taking to social media, Davis focused heavily on personal bravery, flashing his Olympic pedigree to shut down talk that he backs down from rivals. That approach silences people questioning his heart. It does nothing to explain how two fighters calling each other out still managed to stall negotiations.

“Back in August, before he even started doing the interviews, I DM’d him saying, ‘The ink is dry. Did you sign your contract?’ He said, ‘Business will get handled soon.’ … Now he’s saying I overpriced myself. So he never got back with me that he signed,” Davis stated.

That reported interaction gives Davis his firmest talking point. If accurate, he told Hitchins his paperwork was locked down well before this public spat erupted, establishing a distinct timeline that challenges the opposing narrative.

The mystery sits inside whatever document he inked. Davis omitted the purse figures, skipped any special clauses, and avoided confirming if Hitchins held matching conditions. Putting ink to paper does not prove the final terms worked for both camps.

Davis shifted quickly from quoting direct messages to guessing at his rival status. He assumed Hitchins probably avoided signing altogether, claiming that explained sudden talk about Brian Norman. The gap in knowledge counts. Davis can vouch for his own side of the table; he cannot verify the paperwork across the divide.

Hitchins brought up an exorbitant asking price, highlighting that Davis never collected a $ 1 million purse in his career. Davis countered with his readiness to trade punches. Both boxers can crave the contest while remaining completely split on compensation. Neither has established the pay-per-view drawing power required to justify an eight-figure event budget.

Davis has every right to secure his worth. Silencing accusations that excessive demands derailed the bout requires clear numbers: his requested purse, the promoter counteroffer, and the actual status of that proposal. A medal collection cannot clarify a balance sheet.

The talk surrounding Devin Haney clearly touched a nerve. Davis brought up Haney multiple times, batting away claims of fear while refusing to detail the actual business negotiations. Running into another collapsed deal gives detractors more ammunition, and repeating how fearless he feels will not convince skeptics.

“I want my next fight to be you. I don’t want nobody else,” Davis told Hitchins directly.

He told fans to flood the comment sections and prod his rival into accepting the contest. Shifting the heat onto an opponent plays well to an audience, yet it expects spectators to assign blame without seeing a single page of the paperwork.

Davis gave the boxing world a specific claim to chase by pointing to an August signature. The real challenge comes down to whether those terms back up his stance on the purse. Until he addresses the numbers behind that signature, he delivers pure theatrical heat without resolving the financial facts.

Sports.title: Andy Cruz Loses His Zero, Keeps His Problem
Sports.content:
Andy Cruz’s first professional defeat did little to boost his appeal to lightweight’s marquee names. Raymond Muratalla edged him in a grueling encounter that reinforced how dangerous Cruz remains. He surrendered his spotless record, yet none of the elite skill that makes him a nightmare opponent disappeared.

Cruz still demands top-tier competition. “William Zepeda. I’m coming for you,” he told reporters, singling out the WBC champion. Calling out the division’s best is simple enough. Persuading a champion to share a ring with him when safer, lucrative options exist is the real hurdle.

Muratalla earned respect for meeting Cruz head-on to retain his IBF belt. He brought steady pressure, landed big shots, and took home a majority decision. The scorecards of 114–114, 116–112, and 118–110 painted wildly divergent pictures of the bout. The Ring’s post-fight analysis favored Muratalla’s aggression while raising eyebrows at the wide 118–110 total.

The outcome proved Cruz could be outpointed at championship level. It offered zero comfort to rivals expecting an easy night. Muratalla worked relentlessly for all 12 rounds against a challenger who kept landing sharp counters. The loss revealed technical adjustments Cruz must make, yet his durability and ring IQ stayed intact.

Cruz answered in July by halting Abraham Montoya inside three rounds. That stoppage lifted his record to 7–1 with four knockouts, keeping his name in the mix. Steamrolling Montoya could not erase the tactical questions from the Muratalla clash. Facing another elite technician will reveal much more.

Landing that test remains the obstacle. Muratalla vacated his 135-pound strap to chase opportunities above, joined by Shakur Stevenson, who also left the division behind. Their exits put Zepeda and Abdullah Mason atop The Ring’s lightweight rankings, keeping Cruz hovering in the contender pack.

Mason recently floated Zepeda and Joe Cordina as potential targets. A clash with Zepeda brings a unification, while Cordina offers a credible defense. Cruz sat completely outside those discussions, despite loudly hunting Zepeda himself. That reality highlights his dilemma. Rival champions are not necessarily running scared, but they are looking elsewhere.

Cruz risks watching this cycle repeat. Elite fighters can chase unification paydays or fan-friendly matchups while he bides his time. Technical wizardry gives him an edge in any ring, but skill alone provides little financial incentive for rivals to take the risk.

The IBF’s mandate ordering Cruz to fight Artur Subkhankulov for the vacant lightweight crown provides an answer. Grabbing that strap would hand Cruz real leverage, giving unifications a genuine prize to dangle.

Even then, deals require willing partners. Cruz understands the gap between deserving a shot and securing one. His immediate test is capturing the title. Finding out if holding gold finally forces the division’s biggest stars to answer his call comes next.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster Shows His Brilliance Against Emanuel Navarrete
Sports.content:
San Antonio, Texas – O’Shaquie “Ice Water” Foster demonstrated his technical boxing skills Saturday night by boxing brilliantly to defeat Emanuel “Vaquero” Navarrete by unanimous decision (115-111, 118-108×2). He outpointed him by putting on a masterclass. He was offensively sharp and defensively elusive.

Scoring a pair of knockdowns in the twelfth round and holding him to career lows in both total punches landed (99) and connect rate (18.8 %), Vaquero struggled offensively, not being able to land anything of significance, finding it difficult to find the target all night. His connect rate was anemic, landing in the single digits for 8 of the 12 rounds (Compubox).

With the win Foster (26-3, 12 KOs) captured the vacant Ring Magazine super featherweight championship and unified the WBO, IBF, and WBC titles. He now becomes the frontrunner for the fighter of the year award, having earned victories over Raymond Ford and Navarrete (40-3- 1, 33 KOs).

After the win, Foster told the media at the post-fight scrum, “I feel like it was a great performance. I finished strong man. I put him down twice at the end. I feel like there was a lot of people raving saying that I didn’t have no power and that I wasn’t going to be able to keep him off of me. I feel like I showed them tonight that I’m an all-around fighter.”

Many boxing experts believed this fight to be a 50-50 fight where either fighter could have come out victorious. O’Shaquie proved Saturday he is an elite fighter, having defeated another top fighter.

Since having lost controversially to Robson Conceicao in July of 2024, he’s showed significant improvement since then. Earning his revenge in the rematch against Conceicao, then defeating Stephen Fulton convincingly, followed by his most recent performances against Ford and Navarrete.

Vasiliy Lomachenko seems poised to come out of retirement and make an undisputed run in the 130-pound division, stating this is his normal weight and that he wants to become undisputed again.

Foster has his eyes set on becoming undisputed champion and made it known to the media that this is his immediate goal and does not want to deviate from this by entertaining a fight with Shakur Stevenson or Lomachenko; for now, he wants to become undisputed.

The other divisional titleholder is WBA super featherweight champion Anthony Cacace, who is set to defend his title next against Nick Ball on December 19. O’Shaquie has every intent of pursuing a fight against the winner.

He did say he would be willing to fight Lomachenko afterwards, “I want Loma to get a tune-up fight or something cuz when I beat him I don’t want any excuses, man. He been retired.” With the return of Loma and Foster on the verge of becoming undisputed, it’s becoming one of the must-watch divisions.

Sports.title: Keith Thurman Can’t Talk Away The Fundora Loss
Sports.content:
Keith Thurman’s dismissal of Sebastian Fundora’s power makes his own performance harder to explain. If the punches were only “medium,” as Thurman insists, the unanswered question is why he couldn’t produce enough offense to keep the referee out of their fight.

“Medium. Medium, bro,” Thurman said to Brian Custer. “Like, I mean, come on. He never knocked me down.” Thurman’s defense of his performance rests heavily on that distinction: Fundora stopped him, but never put him on the floor.

Thurman rejected Fundora’s comment, relayed by Brian, that the referee had saved him from further punishment. He said a second-round counter pushed him downward because of Fundora’s height, rather than buckling his legs, and maintained that he could handle the punches.

“I’ve been in the ring with a lot of punchers, you know? I mean, at welterweight, Manny Pacquiao, Danny Garcia,” Thurman said. “It was medium. I could take that all day.”

That comparison draws on Thurman’s championship past, but his experience against established punchers cannot settle whether he was defending himself effectively against Fundora. His own description of the fight supplies a more revealing explanation than the power rating.

Thurman said Fundora’s height and reach were more difficult to deal with than he expected. Tall sparring partners had not fully prepared him for the distance he encountered, and he was still adjusting when the referee intervened.

Fundora did not need every punch to hurt Thurman badly if his reach and output kept Thurman occupied with protecting himself.

Thurman wanted more time, saying he had moved toward the middle of the ring and was beginning to feel comfortable defensively. He believed the decision should have remained with him and his corner.

“I just wish the ref would have used his eyes a little bit more and let me and my team make the decision, man,” Thurman said. “Like, if we get into the eighth round and it’s not getting any better, so be it. But I was determined to take the young man’s punches. It wasn’t really my night. My hands were not going.”

Thurman weakens his own argument by admitting he wasn’t throwing back. Being able to take Fundora’s punches wasn’t enough. He needed to answer them, and the referee didn’t have to wait for a knockdown to intervene.

Thurman also blamed an awkward weight cut and acknowledged a poor performance. Those explanations might account for his struggles, but they don’t explain why he believes more rounds would have changed anything.

Thurman had more to say when he discussed Fundora’s height, reach, and punch output. He admitted he couldn’t get comfortable against them. Calling Fundora’s power “medium” does nothing to explain why he couldn’t get past those advantages and land his own shots.

That version of the Fundora loss gives Golden Boy and DAZN something to sell: Thurman was still adjusting, his chin held up, and the referee denied him a chance to turn things around. It makes Ortiz sound like he’s facing a dangerous veteran whose right hand could punish a mistake. The harder sell is explaining how Thurman will land that punch after admitting he couldn’t get his offense going against Fundora.

Sports.title: Jaime Munguia Buys Time, But Bektemir Melikuziev Isn’t Going Away
Sports.content:
Jaime Munguia secured room to maneuver around an overdue mandatory defense, clearing a route to meet Nikita Zon on October 31 with his WBA super middleweight belt intact. Bektemir Melikuziev receives a firmer pledge for what follows, though Munguia reaps the instant reward.

This reported step aside setup introduces clear barriers against future stalls. Guardrails like these are important given that the WBA had already formally mandated the title bout. Melikuziev is asked to sit and wait on a fight the WBA deemed past due.

The sanctioning body ordered Munguia against Melikuziev back on September 21, granting both corners until October 21 to finalize terms. Official notices indicated the champion’s mandatory window actually lapsed on August 30. The champion stood obligated to face his top challenger right then.

According to a Team Munguia dispatch circulated by Cesar Seda, this new deal triggers an additional 30-day negotiating window right after October 31.

Such an extension merely sets up another round of talks instead of placing Melikuziev directly under the arena lights. No date or site was attached to that mandatory meeting. Munguia’s chosen bout holds a firm calendar spot; the actual title challenger must still wait on one.

Zanfer operations head Guillermo Brito confirmed a mutual pact exists, while leaving ultimate ratification in sanctioning hands.

“We have an arrangement, but the WBA still has to determine it,” Brito explained via Izquierdazo.

That boundary stops Munguia’s side from claiming a private deal equals formal sanctioning consent. The missing piece remains legitimate organizational approval.

The sharpest terms target what Munguia cannot pursue going forward. His camp pledges he will steer clear of any intervening bouts, including unifications, prior to squaring off with Melikuziev. The terms also rule out procedural challenges that could stall the defense, alongside a promise not to petition for WBA super champion standing.

These limits aim to shut down bypass options. A unification clash often provides an appealing detour. Seeking an elevated title tier might spark fresh bureaucratic wrangling. The paperwork aims to settle these hurdles before they fuel further delays.

Melikuziev’s camp earns points for locking down explicit pledges. Still, their worth comes down entirely to accountability. Ink on paper means little to a top contender if the next detour merely sparks another cycle of waiting.

With no money figures made public, there is zero evidence Melikuziev took a payout or parted with his title opportunity for cash.

Munguia collects his bout with Zon; Melikuziev collects signed guarantees for the future. The WBA faces the challenge of transforming those guarantees into an actual title fight with a fixed date once October 31 wraps up.

Kicking the can down the road to take on Zon buys Munguia a brief reprieve, but it does not erase the problem waiting in the wings. Melikuziev is not going to politely fade into the background, and the WBA is eventually going to run out of patience for stall tactics. Melikuziev is a legitimate puncher who brings real risk to anyone trying to play it safe at 168 pounds.

Holding a belt means taking on the top contenders when their turn arrives. If Munguia wants the prestige, the marketing power, and the leverage of being a recognized champion, he has to earn it in the ring against the rightful mandatory. If he prefers softer touches and exhibition-style tune-ups, the honorable move is to vacate the strap and let the hungry contenders fight for it. Sitting on a title while dodging a live wire like Bektemir just holds up the division.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Arrest Complicates Zuffa’s Rebuilding Job
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga’s reported arrest puts Zuffa Boxing in a difficult spot with a headliner whose competitive standing was already under scrutiny.

Stopping Steven Butler in seven rounds on July 26 at Madison Square Garden’s Theater gave Dana White’s outfit a clean knockout for the highlight reel, but surviving an early knockdown against a fringe operator did little to prove Berlanga belongs near the elite bracket at 168 pounds.

That sporting reality turns this legal situation into a genuine commercial problem. Berlanga needed his next fight announcement to drive the narrative and validate his position as a marquee attraction following his 2024 points loss to Saul Canelo Alvarez. Instead, public focus has abruptly shifted to serious criminal allegations while the competitive value of the Butler victory remains thin.

Lakeland Police arrested Berlanga on October 26 in Polk County, Florida, regarding an incident alleged to have occurred October 18, according to an Uncrowned report published by Yahoo Sports. Court records cite first-degree misdemeanor battery alongside a second-degree felony count of aggravated battery.

A judge set combined bail at $16,000 during an October 27 court appearance at Bartow Courthouse. His formal arraignment is set for November 17 at 8:45 a.m., where he will enter a plea. These charges remain strictly allegations, and Berlanga retains the presumption of innocence under the law.

Zuffa invested heavily in Berlanga to anchor its boxing venture, banking on his recognizable name to draw viewers. Yet his competitive trajectory required careful handling even before police became involved. Butler offered a recognizable target Berlanga could eventually wear down, but trading knockdowns with a fragile contender exposed defensive flaws that better super middleweights would punish. A win of that level cannot carry an entire promotional campaign.

Matchmakers now face frozen options. Staging another contest against lower-tier opposition might produce another finish, but it will do nothing to answer doubts about Berlanga’s ceiling against genuine contenders. Booking a significant step up in class would give his rebuilding phase real credibility, yet it carries the immediate danger of another defeat.

The legal process clouds the entire calendar. With arraignment running into late November, assembling a meaningful training camp or booking a major date becomes an expensive risk. While no upcoming bout has been formally scrapped and Zuffa has announced no disciplinary action, sponsors and broadcasters inevitably pull back when headline talent faces felony assault claims.

The real issue involves promotional credibility. Zuffa must prove that Berlanga’s performances inside the ropes warrant the attention he receives. The Butler stoppage offered a modest rebound, but it never answered the larger questions about his true ability. Now, with serious legal dates taking precedence over fight negotiations, convincing the public to take Berlanga seriously as a top contender just became far more difficult.

Promoters tolerate outside chaos for fighters who deliver elite pay-per-view numbers or dominant championship runs, but Berlanga brings neither of those things to the table.

Zuffa signed him expecting a turnkey attraction who could headline cards on name recognition alone. Instead, they inherited an expensive puzzle. His early sixteen-fight knockout streak built an inflated reputation, yet the moment Top Rank put him in with actual durable pros, the power vanished, and the technical limitations showed.

Surviving a knockdown against Steven Butler just to score a mid-tier stoppage did not convince anyone that Berlanga could hang with the monsters at super middleweight. Taking on punchers like Christian Mbilli, Osleys Iglesias, or Diego Pacheco would likely end his run as a viable headliner overnight.

That leaves Zuffa holding a contract on an expensive fighter they have to baby through soft touches, all while paying him marquee money. If Dana White and his team were already realizing that Berlanga’s ceiling is strictly as a domestic-level gatekeeper rather than an elite world champion, an aggravated battery felony arrest gives them the ultimate clean exit.

Contracts at this level always carry standard morals and conduct clauses. Invoking that language allows a promotion to walk away without paying out a severance or having to fulfill dates for a fighter who became more trouble than he is worth. If Zuffa wanted an off-ramp from the Berlanga business, the legal system just handed them one on a silver platter.

Sports.title: Dmitry Bivol Has Zero Reason To Grant Anthony Yarde An Unearned Shot
Sports.content:
Anthony Yarde is eyeing Dmitry Bivol before hanging up the gloves, but calling out the division elite after almost a year out of action leaves him in a tough spot. To turn that target into reality, the British light heavyweight must snap his inactivity, build momentum, and take down legitimate contenders.

Yarde has been sidelined for 11 months following his seventh-round stoppage loss to David Benavidez in November 2025. Coming off an extended break plus a stoppage defeat, there is little incentive for Bivol to grant him an unearned shot.

Still, the 35-year-old insists Bivol is the missing name on his resume. Having shared the squared circle with Sergey Kovalev, Artur Beterbiev, and Benavidez, he is eager to complete his personal sweep of the era’s best.

“A fight for me that I would have to make in my career would be Bivol, just for my own personal thing, because I fought all the best people and he’s definitely one of the best people,” Yarde told Sky Sports News. “Partly my character, partly you can call it a screw loose, I want to fight the best people in my generation.”

Nobody questions Yarde courage. He proved his grit by traveling to Russia against Kovalev, and pushed Beterbiev to the brink before being halted. The problem is that none of those valiant attempts brought home a world championship, and falling to Benavidez set him back considerably.

That leaves Bivol with virtually no motive to pick Yarde. Without a headline victory to his name recently, the Londoner cannot offer the kind of leverage or massive payday that would lure the champion into a voluntary defense. Short of capturing a mandatory slot, he has no way to force Bivol’s hand.

Father Time is ticking as well. At 35, Yarde cannot afford to sit idle waiting around for a lottery ticket. He needs activity, consistency, and meaningful wins against top 175-pound contenders to build real leverage.

Fortunately, he sees an alternate avenue. Yarde is keeping a close watch on the vacant WBC light heavyweight title rematch between Joshua Buatsi and Willy Hutchinson. Backing Buatsi to win, Yarde recognizes that an all-British grudge match would generate serious domestic buzz, while snagging that green belt would give him the exact negotiating chip he needs to tempt Bivol.

Meanwhile, Bivol is scheduled to meet Callum Smith on December 12 in Russia. Yarde believes Smith has a strong shot at an upset given his championship pedigree at 168 pounds.

Should Bivol handle business as expected, his masterclass footwork, sharp hand speed, and distance control would give Yarde fits. Before worrying about that stylistic nightmare, however, Yarde must get back to work and give the division king a real reason to pick up the phone.

Sports.title: Canelo Walking Into A Trap Against Christian Mbilli In Riyadh
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez might regret his calculations for Christian Mbilli. Trainer Marc Ramsay insists Canelo treats the challenger like a basic pressure slugger. Mbilli intends to show far more variety on Saturday in Riyadh, which could turn this into a grueling night for the champion.

Canelo picked Mbilli, believing he had the tools to handle him. The danger is that his camp looked at Mbilli pushing forward and assumed his attack would remain simple to disarm. At 36 years old, Canelo lacks the foot movement he once possessed. His tank drains faster now.

Ramsay explained that his fighter brings surprises. He stated in French that Mbilli possesses more tools than Canelo expects. The trainer stressed that they plan to demonstrate those adjustments on fight night.

The bout takes place on October 31 in Saudi Arabia. Mbilli respects the Mexican star yet sees slipping reflexes. He noted that Canelo is more beatable than ever, calling this the ideal moment to strike.

Ramsay’s theory faces reality the second Canelo sets his base to fire counters. Mbilli cannot wade inside throwing wild hooks. He must utilize an active jab. He must target the ribs. He has to disguise his punches so the veteran cannot read his timing.

Sustaining the assault matters just as much. Canelo thrives whenever fighters pause to admire their work. Mbilli has to limit those rests. He must drag Alvarez into sustained exchanges before the veteran catches his breath.

Canelo solved aggressive tactics before. He turned back Jaime Munguia two years ago through precision counterpunching. Mbilli cannot rely on raw volume if Canelo connects with the cleaner blows.

Still, Canelo’s stamina issues remain visible in recent outings. Mbilli needs to turn every round into a physical grind. That does not call for reckless charges. It demands persistent pressure when Canelo searches for lulls.

Mbilli spent four years chasing this opportunity while protecting his top ranking. Now he must prove that his gym form holds up against an elite master.

Canelo remains dangerous across twelve rounds. If he took Mbilli lightly, this matchup could slip out of his hands.

Ghana News.title: Woman killed by Tema-Afienya train as residents demand footbridge
Ghana News.content:
An unidentified woman has been killed after being struck by a passenger train on the Tema-Afienya railway line at Mataheko-Sebrepo, prompting residents to renew calls for a footbridge to provide a safer crossing between communities in the area.

The incident occurred on Tuesday night, leaving residents at the scene grappling with the aftermath as they waited for the police to arrive.

Witnesses said they heard the train sound its horn shortly before the collision, followed by an unusual noise that alerted people to the incident.

The impact reportedly left the woman’s body severely mutilated, with her head thrown into a nearby gutter. Some residents and bystanders searched the area to locate it.

Residents raise concerns over safety

Residents said the incident had revived longstanding concerns about the difficulty of crossing the railway line and the need for a dedicated pedestrian crossing to connect communities in the enclave.

They are calling on the relevant authorities to construct a footbridge to reduce the risk of pedestrians being struck by trains.

The residents believe such a facility would provide a safer route across the railway and help prevent similar tragedies.

According to accounts from people at the scene, several emergency calls were made after the incident, but assistance had not arrived by the time some residents began taking steps to preserve the body.

When a news crew arrived at about 9:30 p.m., residents said they had made repeated calls for help.

The body was subsequently conveyed by officers of the Afienya-Mataheko Police for the necessary procedures.

The identity of the deceased had not been established at the time of reporting, and further details about the circumstances of the incident were not immediately available.

Ghana News.title: AMA clears Achimota bus stop to make way for Ayalolo buses
Ghana News.content:
The Accra Metropolitan Assembly (AMA) has stepped up efforts to reclaim public spaces in the capital, clearing unauthorised structures around the Achimota New Overhead Ayalolo bus stop to improve access for commercial buses and their passengers.

The operation, led by the Accra Mayor, Michael Kpakpo Allotey, on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, targeted structures and trading activities obstructing the bus stop, where Ayalolo and other commercial buses are expected to pick up and drop off passengers.

The clearance is intended to provide buses with adequate space to operate, reduce obstructions and improve traffic movement around the busy transport point.

The exercise forms part of a broader campaign by the AMA and the Okaikwei North Municipal Assembly to remove unauthorised structures and trading activities from public spaces.

Bus stops targeted

The assemblies say the operation is aimed at restoring bus stops to their intended purpose and preventing trading activities from interfering with public transport services.

The presence of structures and traders around loading and offloading points can restrict access for buses, disrupt passenger movement and contribute to congestion, particularly at busy transport locations.

By clearing the area around the Achimota interchange, the authorities hope to enable commercial vehicles, especially Ayalolo buses, to serve commuters without having to navigate obstructions at the designated stop.

Broader public-space enforcement

The collaboration between the AMA and the Okaikwei North Municipal Assembly is intended to extend the removal of unauthorised structures and trading activities beyond the Achimota bus stop to other areas where public spaces have been occupied.

The authorities are seeking to ensure that bus stops remain accessible to public transport operators and commuters, while discouraging trading and other activities that obstruct their use.

The clearance forms part of wider efforts to restore order in the city’s transport corridors and improve the movement of people and vehicles.

The assemblies are expected to continue addressing the occupation of unauthorised spaces as part of their traffic management and public-space regulation measures.

Ghana News.title: Dr. Bawumia engages TUC leadership on youth employment, rising living costs and labour welfare
Ghana News.content:
Former Vice President and NPP presidential candidate, Dr. Mahamudu Bawumia, has taken his broad-based stakeholder engagement to Organised Labour, meeting with the leadership of the Trades Union Congress (TUC) at the Hall of Trade Unions in Accra Tuesday.

The meeting, held as part of Dr. Bawumia's ongoing national consultations, brought together top executives of the TUC, the umbrella body representing thousands of Ghanaian workers across both the public and private sectors.

Sources close to the meeting describe the atmosphere as cordial, frank and solution-oriented, with both sides demonstrating a commitment to addressing Ghana's current labour concerns.

At the centre of the discussions were bread-and-butter issues affecting workers, including the biting cost of living that has eroded disposable incomes, the long-standing demand for a sustainable living wage that goes beyond the minimum wage, and the growing anxiety over youth unemployment.

Other critical matters raised were the need to reform and enhance the pensions regime to guarantee dignity in retirement, and the imperative of ensuring workplaces are truly inclusive for persons with disabilities.

Beyond immediate welfare issues, the meeting also delved into strategic economic policy, with both sides exploring the idea of creating a resilient economy strong enough to absorb external shocks that affect exchange rates, inflation, commodity prices and supply chains.

Dr. Bawumia, who has consistently advocated strong economic fundamentals to withstand global economic shocks, is said to have listened attentively to the concerns and proposals put forward by the TUC leaders, assuring them that their inputs would form part of his broader economic vision.

The engagement with the TUC follows similar consultations Dr. Bawumia has held in recent weeks with traders, professional bodies, faith-based organisations, youth groups and private sector players, as he continues to gather diverse perspectives on building a more resilient and inclusive Ghanaian economy.

Both sides are expected to hold follow-up meetings to drill down into concrete policy proposals.

Ghana News.title: CDD-Ghana urges NDC to crack down on vote-buying
Ghana News.content:
The Centre for Democratic Development Ghana (CDD-Ghana) has urged the National Democratic Congress (NDC) to introduce clear rules and stronger monitoring systems to address allegations of vote-buying in its internal elections.

Programme Officer of CDD-Ghana, Vera Abena Addo, said the party needed to move beyond discussions about guidelines and demonstrate a commitment to tackling the practice before its forthcoming regional and national executive elections.

She warned that incidents at the constituency level could set expectations for subsequent contests, potentially increasing pressure on candidates to offer money or gifts to delegates seeking to elect party executives.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 27, Ms Addo said the party should establish regulations governing its internal elections, even in the absence of specific laws addressing the conduct of such contests.

“Even without the laws regulating the internal election, I think that the party needs to have some regulation,” she said.

She expressed concern that the development of guidelines appeared to be taking too long, given the party’s electoral calendar.

“I think it's taking long, and I'm hoping that even before we move into the next level of elections [it would be implemented],” she said, referring to the regional and national polls that will follow the constituency contests.

Concerns over future contests

Ms Addo said allegations of vote-buying at the constituency level raised questions about what might happen when the party moved to elections involving regional and national delegates.

“If at a constituency level we see this kind of activity happening, then how much more at the regional level?” she asked.

She suggested that the distribution of money or gifts during constituency elections could create expectations among delegates contesting or participating in subsequent rounds of internal elections.

“We expect that if we have given something at the constituency level, then they equally would want to expect something at the regional level and then at the national level,” she said.

Ms Addo said the party needed to take the concerns seriously and act before the next stages of its internal electoral process.

Referring to previous concerns about vote-buying, including the Ayawaso incident, she said she had expected concrete action rather than continued efforts to formulate guidelines.

“From the incident at Ayawasu up to now, I would have thought that we could see some action taken, that it wouldn't just be another—the guidelines, still parties still trying to get a guideline,” she said.

Calls for stronger monitoring

Ms Addo also called for a more structured approach to monitoring internal elections, saying the party should ensure that its field officers and monitoring committees had clear responsibilities and systems for reporting suspected breaches.

Responding to comments by NDC National Deputy General Secretary Rashid Tanko, who referred to officers deployed to monitor the elections, she said the party's monitoring arrangements needed to be sufficiently organised to establish what happened during the polls.

She noted that CDD-Ghana's assessment was partly dependent on media reports from areas its officers could not visit.

Ms Addo said the party should therefore strengthen its own monitoring mechanisms to ensure that concerns about vote-buying were properly documented and investigated.

Ghana News.title: Stop using money to manipulate elections — Inusah Fuseini warns vote-buying politicians
Ghana News.content:
Former Tamale Central Member of Parliament Inusah Fuseini has cautioned against the growing use of money to influence internal party elections, saying financial inducements threaten electoral integrity even when they fail to determine the eventual winner.

He said the presence of vote-buying in the recent National Democratic Congress (NDC) constituency executive elections was troubling in itself, warning that political parties risk undermining democratic values when candidates use cash to court delegates.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, October 27, the former member of Parliament’s Constitutional and Legal Affairs Committee said the outcome of the elections showed that spending more money did not necessarily translate into electoral victory.

“When we produced our report, we said that we did not believe that the influence of the use of money would influence voters to cast their vote one way or the other. But the fact that it was present was bad in itself,” he said.

Mr Fuseini said voters could still exercise independent judgement despite attempts to influence their choices, adding that the experience should serve as a warning to politicians who believe money can secure electoral success.

He welcomed comments by a person who had spoken against the practice, saying such a position could discourage candidates from relying on financial inducements to win votes.

He said the central concern was not simply whether a candidate who spent heavily won or lost, but whether the use of money had the potential to distort the electoral process.

“What we are concerned with is the undue influence that has the potential to corrupt the outcome of elections that affects the integrity of elections,” he said.

Mr Fuseini warned that the increasing reliance on money in internal party contests risked shifting attention away from the candidates’ competence, ideas and commitment to public service.

He said such a trend could also exclude candidates who lacked the financial resources to compete, regardless of their leadership qualities or support among party members.

Voters’ conscience

To illustrate his point, Mr Fuseini referred to the election results, arguing that some candidates who reportedly distributed more money than others did not win.

He mentioned Babar and Jamal while discussing the results, saying the outcome challenged the assumption that the candidate who spent the most would necessarily emerge victorious.

He also cited the case of a candidate who received only one vote and, according to his account, had not given money to voters.

“And again I go back to also there was one person who got only one vote, and that person never gave anything,” he said.

Mr Fuseini questioned whether the candidate’s failure to distribute money explained the result, while suggesting that voters retained the ability to make their own choices.

“Is it because that person never gave anything that he got one vote, and who was this person who voted? That person was a voter of conscience who received but decided that he would act one way or the other and not be influenced by what he had received?” he said.

His comments highlight the distinction between the presence of financial inducements and their actual influence on voting decisions. Even where voters reject attempts to influence them, he suggested, the practice remains damaging to the credibility of elections.

Safeguarding internal democracy

The debate over vote-buying raises broader questions about the conduct of internal party elections and the ability of candidates without substantial financial resources to compete fairly.

Although Mr Fuseini said money might not always determine the outcome, he warned that its presence could compromise the integrity of the process and weaken confidence in party democracy.

His remarks come at a time when political parties face recurring concerns about the role of cash and other inducements in contests for internal leadership positions.

Ensuring transparent elections, enforcing party rules and encouraging delegates to assess candidates on their leadership records and ideas are among the measures that can help strengthen internal democracy.

Ghana News.title: Northern Ashanti Mines challenges Minerals Commission over Konongo takeover, disputes $8.3m debt
Ghana News.content:
Northern Ashanti Mines Limited (NAML) has challenged the Minerals Commission’s justification for taking over its Konongo premises, accusing the regulator of making false claims about its debt and mining activities.

In a statement responding to the Commission’s defence of the takeover, the company described the regulator’s account as containing “falsehoods, untruths and half-truths”.

NAML said it had invested more than US$100 million in developing the mine since taking it over in 2019. It accused the Commission of acting in bad faith and seeking to undermine a Ghanaian-owned business.

The company disputed the Commission’s assertion that it had met the requirements of Section 68 of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703).

According to NAML, it received no notice identifying a statutory breach before the revocation of its mining lease and prospecting licence.

It said the only correspondence received was a letter dated April 30, 2026, communicating the revocation. Although that letter referred to an earlier notice, the company maintained that it had not received such a notice.

“The Company finds the claim and actions of the Minerals Commission perplexing and in complete bad faith,” the statement said.

NAML also challenged the Commission’s claim that the revocation related to debts of US$8,332,000 and US$49,000 associated with its mining lease and prospecting licence, respectively.

The company said an audit communication from the Commission in May 2026 put its debt at approximately US$2.4 million.

It argued that this was separate from a legacy debt of about US$8.3 million attributed to the mine’s previous operator.

NAML said it had paid more than US$1 million towards reducing its outstanding balance.

The company said it had requested time to settle its obligations because it was still developing the mine, including constructing a processing plant, and had not begun producing gold or earning revenue.

“The Minerals Commission has at no point expressed any disagreement to this proposal,” it said.

NAML rejected the claim that it had undertaken no meaningful mining operations on the concession for more than two years.

It argued that mine development and investment in processing infrastructure are essential to responsible mining.

The company said the Commission had issued permits for projects, including a new processing plant and mining activities to stockpile ore ahead of full production.

It cited two permits issued on February 7 and February 17, 2026, both due to expire on December 31, 2026.

NAML maintained that it was carrying out mining activities under those permits.

The company said it had turned to the courts to protect its investment and its ambition to build an indigenous mining business.

It also alleged an emerging pattern of “horrible, unlawful takeovers” of Ghanaian-owned mining assets, which it accused the Commission of instigating or facilitating.

Despite the dispute, NAML said it remained open to dialogue and a resolution that would protect confidence in Ghana’s mining investment environment.

Ghana News.title: Cenpower clears 600 tonnes of waste from Sega Beach
Ghana News.content:
Cenpower Generation Ltd says it removed 600 tonnes of waste from Sega Beach during the fourth edition of its annual KIPP Clean Project, highlighting the scale of shoreline pollution.

The exercise brought together employees, Kpone residents, the Kpone Katamanso Municipal Assembly, and waste management partners to clean the beach in the Tema Industrial enclave.

Cenpower, which owns the Kpone Independent Power Plant (KIPP), launched the project in September 2023 to tackle coastal pollution, protect marine ecosystems and encourage responsible waste disposal.

This year’s exercise involved Cenpower Operations (Cenops) and Excelior Solution Services, which supported shoreline cleaning, waste collection, sorting and safe disposal.

Cenpower’s Chief Executive, Theophilus Sackey, said protecting the environment required collective action beyond individual businesses' operations.

He warned that waste dumped into the ocean could wash back onto beaches, creating recurring pollution problems for coastal communities. He called for clean-up exercises to be supported by responsible disposal practices and sustained public participation.

The Director of Environmental Services at the Kpone Katamanso Municipal Assembly, Freeman George, commended Cenpower for maintaining the initiative.

Speaking on behalf of the Municipal Chief Executive, he urged businesses, institutions, and residents to help keep the municipality clean. He stressed that lasting improvements would depend on changes in everyday waste disposal habits.

He said environmental cleanliness should be a daily responsibility rather than an activity reserved for organised clean-up exercises.

Community members welcomed the initiative and called for continued collaboration to prevent waste from accumulating along the shoreline.

Cenops Plant Manager Darlington Ahuble said employee participation helped reinforce environmental awareness and responsible practices.

He explained that environmental compliance and cleanliness formed part of the company’s operational responsibilities. He urged employees, partners and neighbouring communities to sustain those efforts beyond the annual exercise.

Cenpower’s Director of Legal and Corporate Affairs, Elizabeth Akin-Taylor, also called for greater community involvement in coastal protection.

She said local participation could strengthen ownership of environmental initiatives and encourage residents to prevent littering.

According to her, the project’s value extended beyond the volume of waste collected. It also offered an opportunity to promote responsible environmental practices and strengthen cooperation among stakeholders.

The initiative aligns with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 14, which focuses on conserving oceans, seas and marine resources.

Ghana News.title: Vote-buying: NDC weighs rules to distinguish transport payments from electoral inducement
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) is weighing rules to determine when money given to delegates for transport becomes an electoral inducement.

Former Tamale Central MP Inusah Fuseini says proposed constitutional changes must address payments that exceed reasonable travel costs, even when candidates describe them as transport support.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, he said the party needed clear standards for acceptable payments.

“How much money can we say is appropriate in the circumstances? If somebody gives a delegate GH¢200, is it an inducement or what is it?”

His comments follow reports of widespread alleged vote-buying during the NDC’s latest constituency executive elections.

Mr Fuseini said declaring the purpose of a payment did not resolve the question. The amount could still exceed what a delegate reasonably needed for transportation.

The committee reviewing the party’s constitution is examining how to handle such cases. It must also establish which party body can investigate complaints and impose sanctions.

“So we need a framework.”

Mr Fuseini said the committee had recognised the need for sanctions after acknowledging that inducement had occurred in the elections.

But it found “there was no legal mechanism in our constitution to deal with that”.

He explained that this gap could expose disciplinary decisions to challenges. The party needed rules that define misconduct and give its institutions authority to act.

One option is to empower constituency councils of elders to handle cases locally. Another is referring offenders to the national headquarters, where the Functional Executive Committee would act.

The party would further review the proposals before presenting them to a special congress for constitutional amendment.

“So yes, it's a work in progress.”

Mr Fuseini also warned that the growing financial demands of politics were excluding women, young people and people with integrity.

Some potential candidates lacked the resources to compete. Others were withdrawing from politics because of the sums involved.

He said heavy spending also pressured politicians to recoup their money after winning office.

“A politician is not an NGO, and so when people spend that amount of money, they expect to recoup that, and that fuels corruption on a national scale.”

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
