“Without having that security anchor to ensure that whatever comes from wherever to invest, the investments are safe, it becomes very difficult for us to do anything.”

He said the partnership would provide a platform to approach prospective investors with security arrangements designed to protect their investments.

Also speaking, the Managing Director of MOFI, Dr Armstrong Takang, said: “Nigeria needed to make better use of its land, water resources and people to produce sufficient food for households and industries, while generating additional supplies for export.”

He said the partnership would focus on developing bankable agribusiness opportunities capable of attracting public and private investment. On his part, DAPCO Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, Aliyu Abdulhameed, said: “The defence establishment’s role was to ensure that financing reached agricultural opportunities in rural areas under secure and properly structured arrangements.”

He added that surrounding communities would be involved in projects established in their areas, while serving military personnel and veterans would also be considered.

Ogunseinde said: “An estimated 30 million to 35 million hectares of land could be available for farming, providing considerable scope for expanding large-scale agricultural production.”

He added that the partners had identified several opportunities and expected at least one project to break ground before year-end, although he did not identify the project or specify a commencement date.

The Group Managing Director of Defence Holding Company Limited, Air Vice Marshal A.V. Ndache, said: “The memorandum of understanding signed by the institutions was a broad agreement covering agriculture, hospitality and other investment areas.”

World.title: Cooking gas supply rises 18% to 4.5m litres daily — NMDPRA
World.content:
gas

By Ediri Ejoh

Domestic supply of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG), popularly known as cooking gas, rose by 17.78 per cent year-on-year, YoY, to 4.5 million litres per day in September 2026, from 3.7 million litres per day in September 2025.

The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority, NMDPRA, disclosed this in its latest data obtained by Vanguard.

On a month-on-month, MoM, basis, supply increased by 33.33 per cent from 4.5 million litres per day in August 2026.

Meanwhile, the price of cooking gas rose by 7.14 per cent to N1,400 per kg in October 2026, from N1,300 per kg in September.

Reacting, former National President of the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers, NALPGAM, Mr. Oladapo Olatunbosun, attributed the increase to improved local production but called for sustained investment and government support to prevent shortages.

He said: “Local production has increased, which is the reason for the result. However, there is much to be done by both the government and stakeholders to drive the development required to harness the potential of LPG.”

Olatunbosun urged the government to encourage indigenous operators and support major domestic producers, including Dangote Petroleum Refinery, to boost output and stabilise the energy market.

“The government should continue to encourage indigenous operators, and they should see it as being a partner in bringing stability to energy,” he said.

He also called for affordable supplies to surrounding communities, adding that increased investment in production and distribution would improve availability.

“The market is wide and large, and the more we get people investing in the production and distribution of LPG, the more available the product will be,” he said.

Similarly, National President of the Oil and Gas Services Providers Association of Nigeria, OGSPAN, Mazi Colman Obasi, described the supply growth as positive but stressed that consumers must benefit through improved access and affordability.

“The growth in supply is a positive development because availability is fundamental to the expansion of LPG consumption. However, the real test is whether consumers are seeing improved access and more affordable prices,” he said.

Obasi cautioned that increased supply would not automatically reduce retail prices, citing transportation, logistics, exchange-rate movements and other costs.

He said efficient distribution was essential to ensure additional volumes reach consumers and encourage more households to switch to LPG.

World.title: 2027: NDC campaign DG urges Atiku to join Obi-Kwankwaso
World.content:
The Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Presidential Campaign Council, Ibrahim Abdulkarim, has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and other opposition leaders to join the alliance backing Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election.

Abdulkarim said the opposition needed to unite behind a common platform to improve its chances of defeating the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in the election.

Speaking on Arise News, he said the coalition was already taking shape within the NDC, with Obi emerging as its presidential candidate and Kwankwaso agreeing to work with him.

“The opposition has to come together for us to win. The opposition have already come together. Nobody said the coalition must happen on ADC. It can happen in NDC, and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso has already dropped his ambition,” he said.

Abdulkarim said Atiku and other opposition figures were welcome to join the alliance to broaden its national reach.

“What we are asking for is for other people to join us, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, to join all of us, so at least we will have the spread that they think they can add,” he added.

The NDC campaign chief also dismissed criticism of the party’s campaign structures, arguing that its organisation should not be compared with the Obidient movement and other support groups backing Obi.

“How can you compare a party with a support group? We don’t have any problem. They’re all part of the NDC party. We have more than a thousand support groups like that,” he said.

On concerns about electoral fraud, Abdulkarim urged Nigerians who feared their votes might not count to support the NDC, promising that the party had developed measures to protect votes during the 2027 elections.

He said the party would campaign peacefully across the country and mobilise voters who had lost confidence in the electoral process.

“We are going to do our campaign peacefully. We are going to go into every corner,” he said.

Abdulkarim added that the party would reassure voters before the election that their votes would be protected.

“I can promise anybody, anybody that feels he wants his vote to count, we have a very, very unique and serious programme that we have put in place,” he said.

World.title: MultiChoice Unveils New DStv, GOtv Packages Ahead of November 5 Rollout
World.content:
Mmachi Okafor

MultiChoice Nigeria, a CANAL+ company, has unveiled a simplified package ‘ Expect More’ lineup for DStv and GOtv subscribers, with the new structure scheduled to take effect on November 5, 2026.

The announcement was made at a press briefing held at the company’s headquarters in Victoria Island, Lagos, where executives outlined changes aimed at giving subscribers more choice and better value through packages tailored to their viewing preferences.

Under the new structure, DStv subscribers will choose from four packages: Starter, Select, Sports and Premium, while GOtv customers will have Easy, Starter, Select and Sports. The restructuring forms part of CANAL+’s broader strategy to develop a more unified, customer-focused portfolio following MultiChoice’s integration into the group.

Chief Executive Officer of MultiChoice Nigeria, Kemi Omotosho, said the changes were driven by customer feedback and shifts in how audiences consume entertainment across television sets, smartphones, tablets and laptops.

“Our focus is on giving subscribers better value and access to the entertainment they love,” Omotosho stated during her keynote presentation. “The strength of our platform is the combination of African entertainment, leading international content, and unrivalled live sports in one place. We’ve reimagined our packages to better reflect how customers watch today, with tailored options specifically for general entertainment and sports fans.”

During the executive media question-and-answer session, Omotosho explained that the restructuring was intended to reduce package confusion and help subscribers choose options that better match their interests and budgets. She added that, despite the company’s integration into CANAL+, pricing, channel packaging and day-to-day operations remained locally driven, with content tailored to Nigerian consumer demand and economic conditions.



During a product presentation led by Senior Vice President of Communications, Tope Oshunkeye, the executive team outlined the prices and content available across the new DStv packages.

The entry-level DStv Starter package, priced at N6,000 monthly, will introduce two new channels: SuperSport KICKOFF, which will broadcast the Premier League Match of the Week and selected UEFA Champions League fixtures, and Africa Magic+, a destination for local and international entertainment.

DStv Select, priced at N11,000 monthly, is designed for family viewing, combining movies, local and international series, selected football and other sports, children’s programming and Africa Magic Showcase.

For sports enthusiasts, DStv Sports will cost N21,000 monthly and offer every Premier League and UEFA Champions League match, alongside WWE, UFC, the Europa League and ESPN content, including the NBA. The package will also include all general entertainment channels available on the Select tier.

DStv Premium priced at N44,500 will remain the flagship package, offering all the content available on the Sports tier, alongside motorsport competitions such as Formula 1 and MotoGP, Grand Slam tennis, major golf tournaments and first-run international series on M-Net.

Alongside the package changes, MultiChoice announced a refresh of its movie offerings through the introduction of M-Net Movies+, M-Net Stars and M-Net Legends. The company said the changes were intended to provide faster access to new releases and reduce repetitions.

For customers who prefer streaming, DStv Stream will be available as a standalone service from N6,000 monthly. The application will allow subscribers to watch content on compatible smart TVs, tablets and mobile devices without requiring a physical decoder or satellite dish. MultiChoice also announced a decoder promotion offering a complete kit, including a dish and one-month entry-level subscription, for N15,000 across both DStv and GOtv platforms.

Addressing the transition for existing subscribers, Vice President of Customer Value Management, Onyinye Ezenwa, said active accounts on legacy packages would be automatically mapped to new tiers offering equivalent or greater content selection. She assured customers with advance multi-month subscriptions that they would retain their full prepaid duration without losing service time or experiencing interruptions.

Executives also responded to questions about future technological developments, including artificial intelligence and regional content expansion. They said these areas remained under internal consideration as the company continued to assess emerging AI regulations and their implications for content quality and platform integrity.

World.title: Knight Frank Nigeria to Host Second Golf Classic at Ikoyi Club 1938
World.content:
Knight Frank Nigeria will host the second edition of the Knight Frank Golf Classic in Lagos on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at the Golf Section of Ikoyi Club 1938, bringing together a select gathering of clients, business leaders, associates and golf enthusiasts for a day of sporting excellence, relationship-building and celebration.

The Golf Classic forms part of Knight Frank Nigeria’s ongoing commitment to nurturing enduring relationships with clients and partners through meaningful experiences beyond the workplace.

Head of Marketing and Corporate Communications, Knight Frank Nigeria, Mr Lanre Sonubi, confirmed in a statement released to the media that Tatum Bank has been onboarded as a sponsor of this second edition of the tournament as tee off will start from 6:30am, while a reception and trophy presentation ceremony will commence from 2:00pm.

The inaugural edition of the Knight Frank Golf Classic was held on June 20, 2025 at Ikoyi Club 1938 as part of the firm’s 60th anniversary celebrations in Nigeria.

Building on that first event, Knight Frank plans to establish the Golf Classic as an annual fixture, creating a consistent platform for clients, associates and partners to connect through their shared interest in golf.

Knight Frank Nigeria is a member of Knight Frank LLP, the leading independent global property consultancy, serving as our clients’ partners in property for over 128 years globally, and 60 years in Nigeria. Headquartered in London, Knight Frank has more than 20,000 people operating from 384 offices across 51 territories.

The Group advises clients ranging from individual owners and buyers to major developers, investors and corporate tenants.

World.title: Tinubu: Why I Signed SEDC Bill Into Law
World.content:
*Says South East region of enterprise

President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has said that his decision to sign the South East Development Commission (SEDC), Bill into law was driven by his conviction that the prosperity of the South East region is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria.

The President made the disclosure at the the South East Gas Pipeline Infrastructure Investment Ceremony in Enugu on Tuesday.

It will be recalled that the President assented to the bill in July, 2024

Represented at the event by the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, President Tinubu said the Commission was created to provide sustained institutional attention to the region’s reconstruction, rehabilitation and long-term development.

He said: “Our responsibility is to build upon that legacy. I have always believed that the prosperity of the South East is inseparable from the prosperity of Nigeria. When Aba’s industries thrive, when Nnewi’s factories expand, and when commerce flourishes in Onitsha, the entire Nigerian economy benefits. Nigeria cannot achieve its full economic potential while any region operates below its productive capacity. This conviction is central to our Renewed Hope Agenda. It informed my decision to assent to the legislation establishing the South East Development Commission in July 2024”.

The President further said the SEDC was established to be an institution of delivery and not just another bureaucracy.

“The Commission was established to provide sustained institutional attention to the region’s reconstruction, rehabilitation and long-term development.

“I established the South East Development Commission to be an institution of delivery. We must measure its success by the investments it mobilises, the infrastructure it enables, the opportunities it creates, and the lives it improves”, he said.

He commended the Chairman of the Commission, Dr. Emeka Wogu, the Board, and Management of the Commission led by its Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer, Mr. Mark Okoye, for advancing what he described as an important initiative, noting that the South East Vision 2050 process, supported by the Federal Government and the Governors of the region, provides an important foundation for coordinated development.

President Tinubu also disclosed that he has approved the South East Investment Company, explaining that his administration is adopting a model that leverages public resources to unlock private capital.

“We must use public resources strategically to unlock much larger pools of private investment. This is the model I expect from our development institutions: identify strategic economic opportunities, prepare credible projects, commit public resources responsibly and mobilise private capital at a scale government budgets alone cannot achieve,” he said.

Reassuring the people of the South East, the President said his administration remains committed to delivering critical infrastructure that will drive trade and create jobs in the region.

“My dear people of the South East, we recognise the importance of modern roads, rail connections, reliable energy and efficient access to markets. Our administration continues to advance critical transport infrastructure, including the Enugu–Onitsha and Enugu–Port Harcourt corridors, the supporting infrastructure around the Second Niger Bridge and the Eastern railway corridor. We know that much remains to be done. Our commitment is not simply to award contracts, but to deliver infrastructure that reduces costs, expands trade and creates jobs”, he said.

The President added that the reforms introduced in the electricity sector are opening new opportunities for states and private investors to strengthen power supply in the region and across the country.

Speaking on the gas infrastructure, President Tinubu said that the proposed South East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project will help develop a regional gas distribution network that will serve industrial and commercial users across the five eastern States.

“But today, our attention is on another vital foundation of industrial competitiveness: Natural gas. Nigeria possesses substantial gas resources. Yet we must not measure those resources only by what lies beneath our soil. The true value of our gas is in the factories it powers, the jobs it creates and the prosperity it brings to our people.

“With the Assa North–Ohaji South gas processing project in Imo State achieving first gas earlier this year, we have an important opportunity to connect domestic gas resources to productive industries. The proposed South East Gas Distribution Pipeline Project seeks to do precisely that.

“It aims to develop a regional gas distribution network serving industrial and commercial users across Imo, Abia, Anambra, Enugu and Ebonyi States.

“Consider what this could mean: More competitive manufacturing in Aba. Stronger industrial clusters in Nnewi and Onitsha. New investment and productive enterprises in Enugu. Greater opportunities for agro-processing and manufacturing in Ebonyi. A stronger connection between Imo’s gas resources and the wider regional economy. These are not five separate economies. They are parts of one interconnected economic region.

“Gas infrastructure must therefore serve industries and markets, not stop at political boundaries. That is the economic logic of regional integration”, he said.

President Tinubu also encouraged the governors from the South East region to sustain the spirit of cooperation amongst themselves, saying that the zone is a region of enterprise.

He also charged the SEDC and its partners to produce tangible results that will impact the region positively, promising the government will always strive to create the enabling environment for businesses to thrive.

“Your Excellencies, the Governors of the South East, I encourage you to sustain the spirit of cooperation that has brought us to this point. No single state can realise the full benefits of regional infrastructure on its own.

“The Federal Government will continue to provide the enabling environment. But states, investors and the private sector must work together to convert these opportunities into productive investments.

“To our investors, I say: the South East is a region of enterprise, talent and enormous industrial potential. Look beyond today’s ceremony. Examine the opportunities. Bring your capital, expertise, and long-term commitment. To our manufacturers and entrepreneurs, we recognise your resilience. Our responsibility is to create an environment in which your competitiveness depends less on endurance and more on productivity.

“To the young people of the South East, this initiative is ultimately about your future. A future where your skills have value, your businesses can grow, and a lack of opportunity does not limit your ambitions.

“I expect the South East Development Commission and its partners to move beyond today’s ceremony with a clear implementation plan, defined milestones and measurable results.

“Let this project be remembered not for the agreements signed today, but for the factories it powers, the investments it attracts and the jobs it creates. For generations, the people of the South East have built successful businesses despite inadequate infrastructure. Our responsibility is to help build an economy in which they can succeed because of the infrastructure we provide”, the President assured.

World.title: Tinubu Seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn Loans, Atiku, ADC Raise the Alarm
World.content:
• President cites infrastructure deficit, economic growth, security, agriculture, healthcare, education as priorities

•Requests NASS approval for N269.4bn promissory notes to clear FG’s debts

• Atiku alleges proposed borrowing may serve as campaign slush fund, demands project-by-project disclosure

•ADC PCC says president mortgaging Nigeria’s future, warns of economic recolonisation

• Senate refers supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report

Chuks Okocha, Sunday Aborisade and Juliet Akoje in Abuja





President Bola Tinubu yesterday asked the National Assembly to approve a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance projects and programmes across critical sectors of the economy, a move that has drawn criticism from former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC).

While the President said the proposed facilities would address Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit, accelerate economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, Atiku alleged that the borrowing request vindicated his earlier warning about a loan plan of up to $20 billion and raised concerns about the possible use of public funds for political purposes.

The ADC-PCC, in a separate reaction, condemned the proposed borrowing, describing it as reckless, warning that excessive dependence on foreign loans could mortgage Nigeria’s future and set the stage for economic recolonisation.

The controversy comes as President Tinubu has also sought the National Assembly’s approval for the establishment and expansion of the federal government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities amounting to N269.44 billon.

Tinubu Seeks Approval for $20.5bn, €1.04bn External Loans

Tinubu, in a letter read by Senate President Godswill Akpabio at plenary yesterday, urged the National Assembly to approve the supplementary external borrowing plan for 2026–2027 to enable the federal government to implement its projects and programmes without delay.

He said the proposed borrowing plan covered infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security, employment generation and financial management reforms, among other sectors.

Tinubu said, “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others.”

Explaining the rationale for the request, the President said the need to sustain economic growth following the implementation of his administration’s reforms had made additional external financing necessary.

“In light of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643,” he said.

He added that the projects and programmes covered by the plan had undergone technical and economic assessments to establish their potential contributions to national development.

“I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” Tinubu said.

According to him, the proposed interventions are expected to stimulate economic activities, create jobs, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security.

“These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child,” he said.

The President disclosed that most of the projects and programmes would be implemented across the 36 states of the federation and the Federal Capital Territory, underscoring the nationwide scope of the proposed investments.

“The majority of these projects and programmes will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory,” he said.

Tinubu added that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure needs and the financial resources required to address them had made broader external borrowing necessary to bridge the funding gap.

“In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” he said.

He said the funds would be channeled primarily into critical infrastructure, particularly power, transportation and healthcare, while other sectors would also benefit from the proposed financing arrangement.

“These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the President said.

Tinubu urged the Senate and the House of Representatives to give the proposal urgent consideration, arguing that prompt approval would facilitate timely disbursement and effective implementation of the projects.

The President said, “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.

“This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.”

He maintained that the proposed financing would support the implementation of development programmes and help address the country’s infrastructure funding shortfall.

The letter, however, did not provide, in the material presented to the Senate, a project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the individual financing terms or the allocation of the funds among the beneficiary sectors.

The proposed borrowing plan comes as the federal government seeks additional resources to finance infrastructure and development programmes amid competing demands on public finances. Its implementation will depend on the National Assembly’s consideration of the proposal and the details of the projects to be financed under the plan.

Following the presentation of the letter, Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for consideration and directed it to report back to the chamber within one week.

The committee is expected to undertake the initial legislative review of the proposal, with possible collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees.

The request will require legislative scrutiny before the proposed external financing can proceed.

Tinubu Seeks Approval for N269.4bn Promissory Notes to Clear FG Debts

In a separate legislative request, Tinubu sought the National Assembly’s approval for the establishment and expansion of the federal government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities amounting to N269.44 billion.

The request was conveyed in a letter from the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), Senator George Akume, which was read during plenary at the House of Representatives in Abuja yesterday.

The proposed programme is intended to address outstanding contractual commitments, project-related debts and other financial obligations owed by the Federal Government to various categories of creditors.

In the letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume disclosed that the outstanding liabilities totaled N269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review conducted by relevant ministries, departments and agencies of the Federal Government.

He stated that Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations.

According to the letter, the initiative is intended to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for clearing the outstanding debts while ensuring that only claims that have been properly verified and validated are accommodated under the arrangement.

The request also seeks legislative approval for the inclusion of the identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the appropriate government agencies.

Tinubu further requested that the National Assembly empower the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, working with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme.

Akume explained that the proposal was designed to reduce the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial charges arising from the unpaid obligations.

He added that the arrangement would provide relief to affected creditors and reinforce confidence in the federal government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual agreements and other financial responsibilities.

The SGF noted that the Federal Government had previously deployed the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited domestic debts and contractual obligations, following approval by the Federal Executive Council and subsequent authorisation by the National Assembly.

He said the proposed arrangement was expected to enable the government settle the outstanding liabilities in an orderly manner without creating an immediate and disproportionate demand on its cash flow.

According to the letter, the programme would also improve fiscal planning by allowing repayment obligations to be spread over an appropriate period, consistent with prudent debt management principles.

Akume appealed to the House of Representatives to give the request urgent consideration, citing the substantial size of the outstanding liabilities, the length of time some of the debts had remained unpaid and the risk of further increases in interest and related costs.

He said prompt legislative approval would allow the Federal Government to begin the necessary procedures for issuing the promissory notes and bringing the affected liabilities to a close.

The detailed schedule of the outstanding obligations, containing the relevant categories, beneficiaries, amounts and supporting documents, was also forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration.

Atiku Says Loan Request Vindicates His Warning

Former Vice President and ADC presidential candidate, Atiku, said Tinubu’s request for approval to borrow $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion vindicates his October 12 warning about a loan plan of up to $20 billion.

Atiku said the President’s failure to identify the specific projects the loans would fund raises serious concerns that borrowed public money could be channeled through the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, now rerouted inland, to political campaigners and favoured contractors.

In a statement issued by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku was quoted to have said: “On October 12, I warned Nigerians that President Tinubu was reportedly preparing to borrow up to $20 billion in connection with the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway. I asked him to confirm or deny the plan and publish the accounts.

“He did neither. Today, he has asked the Senate to approve $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external loans. My warning has been vindicated.

“The President has listed broad sectors but has not provided a project-by-project account of what this enormous borrowing will fund. Nigerians have not been given clear project details, costs, locations or contractors to scrutinise.

“That silence is especially troubling given the highway’s inland rerouting. Nigerians have every right to ask whether it is becoming a pipeline for borrowed money to reach Tinubu’s campaigners and favoured contractors.

“Barely 12 weeks before an election, how can the President ask lawmakers to saddle Nigerians with more than $20 billion and €1 billion in debt without identifying the projects and their costs? Is this a development plan for Nigerians or a campaign financing scheme dressed up as infrastructure?

“You cannot continue taking frivolous loans on the eve of your departure from office. Let it be on record that one of the first responsibilities I will undertake as President is to scrutinise and investigate every kobo borrowed, especially loans taken in the final year of your tenure. Nigerians will ask questions, and we will find the answers by every lawful means.

“I put local and international lenders on notice: any loan granted to this winding down administration must meet all constitutional, statutory and due process requirements. Upon assumption of office, I will scrutinise every such loan. Any borrowing found to have been obtained without proper authorisation or process will be challenged and will not be allowed to stand.

“The National Assembly must not approve a single dollar until the President publishes every project, contract, cost, contractor, loan term and repayment obligation. No public money should be borrowed in the dark, and no lawmaker should sign a blank cheque against Nigeria’s future.”

Atiku said the burden was on Tinubu to prove that the borrowing would serve the country, not his political interests. He urged lawmakers to publish the proposal and supporting documents and subject them to rigorous scrutiny before any decision.

He added that families already struggling with a cost-of-living crisis should not be made to carry debts they did not approve.

“The woman fighting to keep her business alive and the worker spending their income just to feed deserve to know where the money is going, who will benefit and who will pay,” he said.

Atiku further said that Nigerians would have the opportunity at the ballot box to reject a government that borrows against their future while taking their sacrifices for granted.

ADC-PCC Warns of Economic Recolonisation

The ADC-PCC also condemned Tinubu’s request to the National Assembly for approval to borrow an additional $20 billion and £1 billion, describing the move as reckless, unconscionable and a dangerous step towards Nigeria’s economic recolonisation.

In a statement by the Director of Media and Publicity of the ADC-PCC, Kola Ologbondiyan, the council expressed concern that the administration continued to pursue aggressive borrowing without providing Nigerians with a transparent and convincing account of how previous loans and savings from subsidy removal had been utilised.

The ADC-PCC said the fresh borrowing request came at a time when Nigerians were still struggling with the devastating consequences of the administration’s economic policies, including soaring living costs, increased taxation and the removal of fuel subsidies, with millions of citizens facing worsening economic hardship.

Ologbondiyan said it was alarming that the Tinubu administration was seeking additional foreign loans despite the enormous economic burden already imposed on Nigerians.

“What exactly is President Tinubu borrowing all this money for?” he asked.

He further queried: “Where are the roads, the electricity, the hospitals, the jobs and the critical infrastructure that should justify this relentless accumulation of debt? Nigerians deserve answers.

“Where is the money saved from fuel subsidy removal? What happened to the previous loans? And why must the government return to the international credit market with another $20 billion and £1 billion when millions of Nigerians are struggling to survive?”

Ologbondiyan said the development raised serious questions about the administration’s fiscal priorities, economic direction and commitment to accountability.

According to him, “This is not a sustainable path to national development. It is a dangerous attempt to mortgage the future of Nigeria and generations yet unborn. A country cannot continue to accumulate foreign debt without a clear, measurable and transparent account of the benefits accruing to its citizens.

“President Tinubu cannot continue to impose painful economic sacrifices on Nigerians, claim the benefits of subsidy removal and, at the same time, seek enormous additional loans without adequately explaining how the resources already available to his government have been spent.”

The ADC-PCC argued that an economic strategy built primarily on borrowing and increased taxation, without corresponding improvements in productivity, infrastructure, employment and citizens’ welfare, risked pushing the country deeper into a debt trap.

It warned that excessive dependence on foreign creditors could expose Nigeria to mounting debt-servicing obligations, constrain future governments’ policy choices and undermine the country’s economic sovereignty.

The council further observed that the administration must demonstrate how the proposed borrowing would contribute to productive investment, economic growth and improved living standards rather than impose additional liabilities on future generations.

“The sovereignty of Nigeria must not be compromised by fiscal recklessness. Our national assets, economic independence and the welfare of future generations must not become casualties of an endless borrowing spree,” Ologbondiyan said.

The ADC-PCC therefore called on the National Assembly to subject the proposed borrowing to rigorous scrutiny and reject it unless the Federal Government provided compelling evidence of its necessity, sustainability and tangible benefits to the Nigerian people.

It also demanded that Tinubu publish a comprehensive account of all domestic and foreign borrowing undertaken since May 29, 2023, alongside a detailed breakdown of the revenue realised from subsidy removal and how the funds had been applied.

The council further called for full disclosure of the proposed loans’ purposes, interest rates, repayment periods, associated fees, conditionalities and any collateral or guarantees attached to the facilities.

It insisted that Nigerians had a constitutional and democratic right to know the obligations being incurred in their name and the implications for the country’s fiscal future.

“Nigeria cannot borrow its way out of poor economic management. Borrowing must be tied to clearly defined national priorities, transparent expenditure and measurable outcomes. Anything less is an injustice to the Nigerian people.

“The National Assembly must not abdicate its oversight responsibilities. It must insist on accountability and ensure that no borrowing arrangement places the country’s future at unacceptable risk.

“Nigerians must not be compelled to pay indefinitely for loans whose purposes, terms and benefits remain unclear. Our country must not mortgage its future through opaque and unsustainable borrowing,” the ADC-PCC stated.

World.title: Leadership Names Obaigbena, Rabiu Persons of Year 2026
World.content:
• Cites businessmen’s contributions to innovation, job creation, others

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





Leadership Newspapers has named the Chairman of THISDAY Group and founder of Arise News, Prince Nduka Obaigbena, and the Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, as its Persons of the Year 2026.

The newspaper announced the recognition, while citing the businessmen’s contributions to institution-building, talent development, innovation, investment, job creation and philanthropy.

According to Leadership, the duo are being honoured for “building influential institutions, nurturing talent, challenging convention, and breaking new ground” in their respective fields.

Also yesterday, Leadership Newspapers presented the formal notification of Obaigbena as Person of the Year 2026 at the Ikoyi Offices of Arise News Channel in Lagos.

Present at the event were: Ombudsman, Kayode Komolafe; Leadership Newspapers Vice Chairman & Editor in Chief, Azu Ishiekwene; Leadership Newspapers Chairman, Mrs Zainab Sam Nda Isaiah; THISDAY Managing Director, Eniola Bello and Arise News Director of Politics, Akin Osuntokun.

Obaigbena was recognised for his contributions to Nigeria’s media industry, particularly his role in expanding the country’s media landscape and launching the Leekelee social media platform in February 2026.

Rabiu, on his part, was recognised for BUA Group’s investments in manufacturing and local production, as well as its contributions to job creation, infrastructure development and shareholder value.

The newspaper also highlighted the philanthropic activities of both businessmen, noting their contributions to strengthening confidence in Nigeria’s future.

It described the recognition as an acknowledgement of their influence and impact on the country’s economic and social development.

Earlier, the newspaper said Obaigbena had built influential media organisations, nurtured generations of journalists and expanded the reach of Nigerian and African media through investments spanning newspapers, magazines, television, fashion and digital platforms.

It cited his founding of ThisWeek magazine in 1986 and THISDAY newspaper in 1995 as defining milestones in his career, noting that both publications introduced new approaches to journalism and newspaper production in Nigeria.

Obaigbena founded ThisWeek at the age of 27, establishing a publication that covered politics, economics, international affairs, art and culture. The magazine also became a platform for talented journalists, many of whom went on to occupy prominent positions in the media industry and public life.

His entry into newspaper publishing with THISDAY further expanded his influence, with the publication introducing innovations in presentation, editorial content and the commercial positioning of Nigerian newspapers.

Leadership noted that THISDAY began operations without Obaigbena owning a printing press, while highlighting its adoption of colour production, the elevation of the back page as a platform for prominent columnists and the publication of the full table of daily transactions at the Nigerian Stock Exchange.

Beyond newspaper publishing, Obaigbena, it said, extended his entrepreneurial interests into broadcasting, fashion and entertainment, establishing platforms designed to promote African talent and connect the continent’s creative industry with international audiences.

These included ARISE Magazine, the THISDAY Music and Fashion Festivals, and ARISE Fashion Week, which provided platforms for Nigerian and other African creatives to showcase their work to wider audiences.

In 2013, he launched ARISE News, an international television news platform with an African focus and global outlook, aimed at strengthening African perspectives in international news coverage.

Leadership described the launch of LekeeLekee, a social media platform developed by ARISE Broadcast and THISDAY Media Group in February 2026, as another significant step in Obaigbena’s efforts to expand Africa’s presence in the digital media landscape.

The newspaper said the platform had recorded more than 100,000 downloads within about six months, describing its launch as evidence of his continued interest in exploring new frontiers in media and technology.

It added that Obaigbena’s career had been marked by a willingness to take risks, assemble exceptional talent and build institutions despite economic constraints, technological disruption and the challenges confronting traditional journalism.

It noted that his media organisations had navigated changing governments, economic recessions and the pressures of digital transformation, while continuing to seek new ways of remaining commercially viable and relevant to society.

Born on July 14, 1959, in Ibadan, Oyo State, Obaigbena attended Edo College, Benin City, before obtaining an honours degree in Creative Arts from the University of Benin. He began his media career in 1978 at the Nigerian Observer, where he developed his skills in writing, satire and cartooning.

He subsequently became coordinating editor of The Dawn magazine and worked as a Special Section Representative for Newsweek. His professional experience also included work with Time magazine on special surveys and country sections covering Nigeria, Kenya, Morocco and Zimbabwe.

Obaigbena also participated in public affairs, serving on a sub-committee of the Technical Committee on Privatisation and Commercialisation in 1990. He contested for a seat in the Senate in 1991 and became a member of the 1994 Constitutional Conference.

His contributions to the media profession have earned him several honours and leadership responsibilities. He received the Fellowship of the Nigerian Guild of Editors in 1998 and served two terms as president of the Newspaper Proprietors’ Association of Nigeria (NPAN). He also chaired the Nigerian Press Organisation (NPO).

In 2022, the federal government conferred on him the national honour of Commander of the Order of the Niger (CON). The following year, he received the Lifetime Achievement Award from the Diamond Awards for Media Excellence (DAME) in recognition of his contributions to journalism and society.

Leadership said Obaigbena’s enduring significance lay in the institutions he had established, the conventions he had challenged and the opportunities he had created for successive generations of media professionals.

It described him as an institution-builder whose career demonstrated that African media organisations could pursue global ambitions while retaining their roots and perspectives.

The newspaper said his recognition reflected a career built on the conviction that ambitious ideas, supported by talent, execution and perseverance, could overcome the constraints often associated with operating in Nigeria’s media environment.

World.title: IPO: Dangote Refinery Sets Record with Interest from 119 Nations, Faces Allocation Dilemma
World.content:
• Landmark offer achieves 100% African participation, reaches all six continents

• Aliko: Africa has shown it can finance, build and own its industrial future

• Refinery to reap over $60m in annual gross operational benefits from AI deployment

Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja





The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has attracted investors from 119 countries, setting up a potential allocation squeeze as demand from Nigerian, African and international investors may likely exceed the shares available for sale.

The offer has secured between $1.5 billion and $1.6 billion in fully funded commitments from domestic and retail investors alone, effectively meeting its fundraising target before accounting for additional demand from overseas investors, according to a Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the transaction.

The development underscores the scale of international interest in the equity offering by Africa’s largest refinery, valued at nearly $50 billion, and raises the prospect that some investors may not receive the allocations they seek.

The company is expected to exercise an additional 30 per cent overallotment option, which could increase the total amount raised to approximately $2.1 billion and create room for more international investors. However, demand could still exceed the available shares even if the option is fully exercised, the report said.

The IPO attracted applications from investors in all 54 African countries for the first time, while the total number of countries represented in the offering had reached 119 at the time of the report.

The breadth of participation reflects efforts by Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, to widen ownership of the refinery beyond Nigeria and encourage greater participation by African investors in the continent’s industrial assets.

Dangote extended the closing date for applications by two weeks to October 27, allowing his team to engage investors across Africa and put structures in place to broaden participation beyond the Nigerian market.

“We have more than reached our target,” Dangote said in Gaborone, Botswana, on October 14, adding that the refinery had attracted interest of “more than three times or four times what we are looking for.”

The offer includes nominee structures involving Standard Bank Group for investors in Egypt and Ethiopia, as well as global depository receipts being sold through stock exchanges in Kenya and Botswana.

The transaction is being closely watched as a test of the capacity of African capital markets to mobilise substantial domestic and regional funds for large-scale industrial projects without relying primarily on international financial centres such as London and New York.

If demand significantly exceeds the shares available, Dangote could consider selling part of his personal stake to investors who fail to secure sufficient allocations through the IPO. However, people familiar with the process said no decision had been made on a secondary sale, which would depend on the final order book.

The offering provides investors with an opportunity to take stakes in one of Africa’s most strategically significant industrial assets, whose scale has the potential to reshape petroleum product supply across Nigeria and the wider region.

Beyond the equity offering, the refinery is also deploying advanced digital technology in an effort to improve operating efficiency and profitability, with industrial technology company Honeywell announcing the introduction of an artificial intelligence platform projected to generate more than $60 million in annual gross operational benefits at full capacity.

The platform, known as Forge Plant Cognition, combines Honeywell’s industrial expertise with artificial intelligence and accelerated computing capabilities from NVIDIA and AI infrastructure from Dell Technologies.

According to Honeywell, preliminary estimates indicate that the technology could deliver operational benefits exceeding $0.29 per barrel processed at the refinery. The company cautioned, however, that the projections are based on preliminary data and are not guaranteed.

The system is designed to combine real-time operating data, engineering knowledge and physics-based models to help operators identify constraints, anticipate potential problems and improve plant performance.

Unlike conventional AI applications that primarily analyse data and generate recommendations, Honeywell said the platform integrates industrial automation and process technology expertise with AI-driven analysis to support operational decisions.

“Industrial plants are among the most complex operating environments in the world, with enormous potential to realise greater performance and value using digital technologies and connected solutions,” said President of Honeywell Technologies, Rajesh Gattupalli.

The deployment is also expected to strengthen the capabilities of the refinery’s local engineering and operations teams, as Dangote Industries pursues a major expansion of its refining operations in Nigeria and elsewhere in Africa.

In November 2025, Dangote Industries partnered with Honeywell to support plans to increase the Lagos refinery’s nameplate capacity from 650,000 barrels per day to 1.4 million barrels per day by 2028.

The proposed expansion would more than double the facility’s original design capacity and increase its potential to supply petroleum products to Nigeria and international markets.

The refinery’s processing capacity reached 700,000 barrels per day in June 2026, marking a further step towards the expansion target.

Dangote’s engagement with Honeywell also extends beyond Nigeria. In September 2026, the industrial group selected the technology company to provide engineering services, licensing and equipment for its proposed 700,000-barrel-per-day refinery in Lamu County, Kenya.

Separately, the refinery yesterday said that the IPO achieved 100 per cent geographical coverage of Africa, stressing that more than a conventional fundraising exercise, the offer has emerged as a landmark in financial inclusion, demonstrating how digital technology, coordinated financial institutions and innovative distribution channels can connect millions of potential investors to opportunities previously dominated by institutional and high-net-worth participants.

It said the transaction was supported by an extensive network of commercial banks, stockbroking firms, fintech platforms, capital market institutions and distribution partners, whose collaboration expanded access to the offer across national boundaries and created new pathways for retail participation.

President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, Aliko Dangote, described the outcome as a powerful affirmation of African confidence, enterprise and the continent’s ability to mobilise its own resources for development.

“When we set out to build this refinery, many doubted that a project of this scale could be delivered by Africans. We proved that Africa could build it. Today, through this historic IPO, we have demonstrated something equally important: Africans are ready to own and participate in the prosperity created by their own industries.

“To have investor applications from all 54 African countries is deeply significant to me. It tells us that our people do not simply want to consume what Africa produces; they want to invest in it, own it and share in its future. This is the Africa we have always believed in,” he said.

“We did not undertake this IPO simply because we needed to raise capital. We wanted to open the doors of ownership, give ordinary Africans an opportunity to participate in an enterprise of global significance and establish a new culture of shared prosperity. The refinery was built in Africa, by African determination, and its future must create opportunities for Africans. Today, we have made history together.

“But the greater achievement will be the generation of African investors, entrepreneurs and industrialists that this transaction inspires. Our ambition is not merely to build successful businesses. It is to help build a prosperous, self-reliant Africa whose people are participants in its economic destiny.

“As we advance our expansion programme and Vision 2030 strategy, we remain committed to strengthening our operational performance, deepening our contribution to Africa’s energy security and building an enterprise that rewards the confidence placed in it,” he stated.

Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals, David Bird, said the international response reflected confidence in the refinery’s operating capabilities, industrial scale and long-term growth prospects.

“The successful conclusion of this IPO is a remarkable milestone for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals. Investor applications spanning 120 countries demonstrate the extraordinary international interest in our business and the confidence that investors are placing in the future of this refinery.

“We have built one of the world’s most significant refining and petrochemical complexes, and our focus remains on translating that industrial scale into operational excellence, sustainable growth and long-term shareholder value,” he said.

The refinery’s IPO opened on September 14, 2026, offering 4.1 billion ordinary shares at N525 per share, representing a proposed capital raise of approximately N2.15 trillion. Initially scheduled to close on October 13, the offer was extended to October 27 following approval by the Securities and Exchange Commission, allowing additional time for investors across Africa and other international markets to participate.

Group Chief Financial Officer, Dangote Industries Limited, Murat Erden, speaking on the execution and wider significance of the offering, said the transaction had established an important precedent for the continent’s capital markets.

“The Dangote Refinery People’s IPO represents much more than a landmark capital-raising exercise. It marks a defining moment in the evolution of African capital markets, demonstrating our continent’s ability to mobilise domestic savings, connect investors across borders and broaden ownership of strategic industrial assets.

“Reaching investors in 120 countries, including all 54 African nations, is an extraordinary achievement and a powerful testament to the growing investment appetite across our continent. By bringing together banks, capital market institutions, stockbrokers, fintech platforms and innovative digital distribution channels, we have demonstrated that African capital markets can transcend national boundaries and connect millions of people to investment opportunities previously beyond their reach,” he said.

World.title: FG, WAHO Seek Regional Plan to Retain Health Workers, Tackle Japa Syndrome
World.content:
Onyebuchi Ezigbo in Abuja

The federal government has canvassed stronger regional cooperation and practical measures to address migration of health workers and improve healthcare delivery across West Africa.

The government’s position came just as the West African Health Organisation (WAHO) said that Africa accounts for 24 percent of global disease burden but only three percent of global health workforce.

Quoting 2025 UK report, WAHO said that 85,000 to 90,000 Nigerian-trained doctors and nurses were registered in UK.

The further organization projected that additional 4.2 million workers will be needed by 2030,

Minister of State for Health, Dr. Adekunle Salako, while declaring open a meeting to review the regional work plan for motivation and retention of health workers in ECOWAS member countries said there are lans to grow the number of health workers in Africa.

The meeting, organised by West African Health Organisation (WAHO), seeks to develop strategies for retaining skilled professionals, improving workforce planning and strengthening health systems across the sub-region.

Salako, represented by Dr. Ovuoraye John, Director and Head of Department of Health Planning, Research and Statistics, said regional plan will complement continental initiative targeting two million community health workers across Africa by 2028.

He said meeting coincided with 50th anniversary activities of West African College of Physicians and high-level African Union forum on community health workforce scheduled for Abuja from October 28 to 30.

According to him, simultaneous meetings reflect growing recognition that health workforce challenge requires coordinated action at national, regional and continental levels.

“We now know that we cannot do it alone in silos. We need every resource available to us as a country to get it right. The health workforce is the challenge that we are facing on our continent,” Salako said.

He expressed satisfaction that three initiatives were taking place in Nigeria at same time, describing convergence as opportunity to align regional and continental priorities.

On public health security, Salako urged participants to observe Nigeria’s Ebola prevention protocols, saying country had continued to allow public gatherings despite recording a confirmed case.

He said no additional cases have been recorded since initial confirmation, with contact tracing expanded to 53 persons as of Sunday, all monitored and those at risk tested negative.

He said index patient was recovering though evacuated to Switzerland earlier in day.

Representative of West African College of Surgeons, Prof. Foluso Owoeye, said success of healthcare systems depends not only on infrastructure but on competence, motivation and availability of health workers.

He described migration of health professionals, commonly called brain drain or japa, as major threat to sustainability and quality of healthcare in West Africa, warning those huge investments in training will have limited value if countries fail to create conditions for retention.

He urged that work plans contain practical measures, measurable targets, realistic timelines and clear responsibilities, with stronger links between training and retention, including mentorship, research and career advancement.

WAHO Director General, Prof. Palokinam Pitch, represented by Director of Public Health and Research, Prof. Joseph Olorunda, said Authority of Heads of State had directed that the document be completed to guide retention planning for next 5, 10, 15 and 20 years before presentation to Assembly of Health Ministers.

Pitch said work had begun on harmonising training curricula, with 58 curricula developed to ease mobility of professionals across ECOWAS states.

He said region needs long-term planning to address departure of professionals amid growing challenges including non-communicable diseases and climate change.

WAHO said that Africa accounts for 24 percent of global disease burden but only three percent of health workforce, with projection of additional 4.2 million workers needed by 2030, while 2025 UK report showed 85,000 to 90,000 Nigerian-trained doctors and nurses registered in UK.

The proposed framework is expected to promote improved remuneration, supportive working environment, career development and evidence-based staffing for underserved communities.

World.title: Fayemi Mourns Bishop Ajakaye’s Mother, Extols Her Legacy of Faith and Discipline
World.content:
Gbenga Sodeinde in Ado-Ekiti

A former governor of Ekiti State, Dr. Kayode Fayemi, has commiserated with the Catholic Bishop of Ekiti Diocese, Most Rev. Felix Femi Ajakaye, over the death of his mother, Mama Florence Funmilayo Ajakaye, describing her as a woman whose enduring values were reflected in the exemplary life and ministry of her son.

In a condolence message dated October 26, 2026, Fayemi expressed deep sadness over the passing of the matriarch and extended his heartfelt sympathies to Bishop Ajakaye, the entire Ajakaye family, and the Catholic faithful in Ekiti State and beyond.

The former governor noted that although the death of a mother creates an irreplaceable void, the memories of her love, sacrifices and moral upbringing would continue to serve as a source of strength and comfort for the bereaved family.

Fayemi said the late Mama Ajakaye’s virtues could be seen in the life of the Catholic Bishop, whom he described as a model of faith, humility, discipline, selfless service and commitment to the physical and spiritual well-being of others.

According to Fayemi, whose condolence message was conveyed on behalf of hmself, his wife, Bisi, and the entire Fayemi family, the bishop’s outstanding character and dedication to the service of God stood as a testament to the quality of upbringing and enduring values instilled in him by his late mother.

“The character of a child often bears testimony to the life and values of the parent. The virtues you exemplify are a fitting testament to a mother whose life must have been marked by diligence, dedication, selflessness and an unwavering commitment to raising her children in the fear of God and in the enduring principles of integrity and discipline,” Fayemi stated.

While praying God to grant Bishop Ajakaye, the Ajakaye family and all who mourn Mama Florence Funmilayo Ajakaye the strength to bear the painful loss, Fayemi also prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased, saying her legacy of sacrifice, faith and virtue would continue to inspire generations.

World.title: Ouaddou calls Orlando Pirates players selfish despite 3-0 win
World.content:
Orlando Pirates head coach Abdeslam Ouaddou was not happy despite his team thrashing Milford 3-0 on Tuesday evening.

The Buccaneers are into the last eight of the Carling Knockout Cup after another impressive win.

Ouaddou called his players selfish having gone 3-0 up in the first half. Although they controlled the game, Pirates failed to add more goals in the second half.



“Thank you very much, the positive point I think is the win, I think I will only retain this victory because I was not happy about how we played, we didn’t have the control, we had a lot of precipitation, we were selfish, a lot of players were selfish, instead of giving the ball to the teammate to score -and they are not in a bad position and they shoot,” Ouaddou told SuperSport TV.

Ouaddou not happy with Pirates players

Ouaddou said if the team continues continues with the current path, they might end up without silverware this season.

“A lot of wrong decision making, the positive point is this three goals and clean-sheet, but to be honest if we want to dream bigger when I say dream bigger, is to win the Betway, win the Champions League.

“I think if we continue like that, we’re going to win nothing, and we have to be honest. So, I was not happy about the game so the positive point we go to the next stage, but there are a lot of players they need really to wake up,” he added.

Ouaddou will now turn attention to this weekend’s Soweto derby as Pirates look to go top of the Betway Premiership.

World.title: Eastern Cape floods leave roads underwater as damage mounts
World.content:
Heavy rainfall has flooded roads and bridges in parts of the Eastern Cape, disrupting travel and damaging infrastructure. Image: X via @tndaba

Heavy rainfall has flooded roads and bridges across parts of the Eastern Cape, disrupting travel and damaging electricity infrastructure.

The OR Tambo District Municipality has deployed disaster management teams to assess the damage and identify communities that need assistance.

According to SABC News, Several areas, including Mqanduli, Ngqeleni, Port St Johns, Qumbu and Tsolo, have experienced flooding and travel disruptions.



Which roads and bridges are affected?

Floodwater has affected several crossings in the OR Tambo District, including the Mqanduli Bridge south of Mthatha and the Buntingville Bridge near Ngqeleni.

The municipality has also warned residents against crossing the Ngwevana Bridge as officials monitor rising water levels.

In Mqanduli, an overflowing bridge has disrupted travel, while authorities have identified roads near affected crossings for closure.

However, authorities have not yet confirmed which of these routes remain closed on Wednesday, 28 October.

Motorists should check local traffic updates before travelling.

Heavy rain damages electricity infrastructure

Eskom has confirmed that severe weather damaged electricity infrastructure across several parts of the Eastern Cape.



The affected areas include OR Tambo, Alfred Nzo, Amathole and Chris Hani district municipalities, as well as Buffalo City.

#EskomEasternCape #EasternCapeOutages



Electricity Supply Interruptions Following Severe Weather



Eskom teams are attending to widespread outages caused by heavy rainfall and strong winds affecting parts of the Eastern Cape. The most severely affected areas include: Alfred Nzo,… — Eskom Hld SOC Ltd (@Eskom_SA) October 27, 2026

The damage includes broken conductors, damaged electricity poles and other network components.

Eskom said difficult road conditions have prevented some repair teams from reaching affected infrastructure, delaying restoration efforts.

The flooding has also raised concerns about learners travelling to school, particularly those writing examinations.

The Department of Education’s Coastal District has urged school principals and parents to prioritise safety and make alternative arrangements for examinations where necessary.

Education officials in coastal and inland districts have also received alerts about the risks posed by the weather.

Will the weather improve?

The South African Weather Service has not issued an impact-based warning for the Eastern Cape for Wednesday, 28 October, according to the latest published forecast.

Residents should avoid crossing flooded bridges, use alternative routes where possible and continue monitoring official updates.

World.title: Beware: Fake driver scam targeting tourists at Cape Town airport
World.content:
Travellers arriving at Cape Town International Airport have been warned about fake e-hailing drivers. Image: X @AfricaFactsZone

A Cape Town International Airport scam is costing some tourists thousands of rands for a single trip.

The scammers pose as e-hailing drivers. They look the part, with reflective vests and fake identification.

But by the time travellers notice the charge, they’ve already been dropped off.



According to an Airports Company South Africa (ACSA) contractor who also works as an e-hailing driver, a syndicate of fake drivers is targeting foreign tourists at the airport, adding extra digits to turn a fare of about R250 into R25 000.

He claimed that he regularly hears complaints from tourists who’ve been overcharged.

HOW THE CAPE TOWN AIRPORT SCAM WORKS

According to the latest reports, the fake drivers:



Wear reflective vests and carry fake cards designed to look like official e-hailing driver identification

and carry fake cards designed to look like official e-hailing driver identification Wait near the airport exits, targeting passengers who’ve just landed, often after long-haul flights

targeting passengers who’ve just landed, often after long-haul flights Lie about where official e-hailing pickup points are, and convince travellers to cancel trips they’ve already booked through the app

and convince travellers to cancel trips they’ve already booked through the app Drive passengers safely to their destination, but then charge their cards far more than the trip should cost

SCAMMERS REMOVING WARNING SIGNS

ACSA has put up signs at the airport warning travellers not to accept transport offers from people approaching them.

However, many of the signs have since been removed by the scammers, according to the latest reports.

EARLIER WARNINGS

The scam isn’t new.

In early October, crime watchdogs and a local improvement district warned visitors about fake drivers offering trips from the airport for between R10 000 and R25 000, the Weekend Argus reported.



In one case, a visitor was allegedly charged R25 000 for a trip to Green Point.

ACSA told the newspaper that touting is a criminal offence, and that it had responded with more warning signs, messages on terminal screens and visible security staff.

In February, the US Embassy in South Africa also warned American travellers about people posing as e-hailing drivers at the airport, without a confirmed booking.



HOW TO AVOID THE SCAM

Book through the official app only, and never accept a lift from someone who approaches you in the terminal

and never accept a lift from someone who approaches you in the terminal Check the driver’s name, number plate and car against the details in the app before you get in

against the details in the app before you get in Never cancel an app booking because someone tells you to

because someone tells you to Don’t let anyone look at your phone to see your booking

to see your booking Use official pickup points, or arrange transport through an authorised kiosk inside the terminal

or arrange transport through an authorised kiosk inside the terminal Pre-book an airport transfer with a reputable operator, if you’d prefer not to use an app

WHAT TO DO IF YOU’VE BEEN SCAMMED

Contact your bank immediately to dispute the charge

to dispute the charge Report it to airport security or ACSA

or ACSA Open a case with the South African Police Service (SAPS)
