KENYA · LISTED COMPANY

Key Facts — The country Kenya is an East African democracy of over 50 million people, and Safaricom is its largest company.

— What happened Safaricom dismissed 118 employees in a fraud crackdown in the year to March 2026, up from 113, Business Daily reported on 27 October 2026.

— The source The figures come from Safaricom’s 2026 Sustainable Business Report, which also lists 14 cases referred to law enforcement, up from 7.

— The recovery The company recovered KSh953 million (about US$7.3 million) linked to inflated agent commissions, through monitoring and data analytics.

— The owners Vodacom of South Africa holds 55% of Safaricom, and Vodafone, which controls Vodacom, has receipts that trade on Nasdaq.

— What it means for you M-Pesa moved KSh41.7 trillion (about US$321 billion) in the year, so internal fraud controls matter to investors and to US firms that rely on it.

— Still open The report does not say how much money the dismissed staff took, or which of the 118 cases ended in court.

Safaricom, Kenya’s biggest company and the operator of the M-Pesa mobile-money service, dismissed 118 employees in a fraud crackdown in the year to March 2026. That is up from 113 the year before, Business Daily reported on Tuesday 27 October 2026.

For American investors and firms that do business through M-Pesa, the number shows a company policing its own staff as the platform grows. The fraud crackdown also brought back KSh953 million (about US$7.3 million) tied to inflated agent commissions.

What the Safaricom Report Shows

Safaricom published the figures in its 2026 Sustainable Business Report, which covers the financial year that ended in March 2026. Business Daily, a Nairobi newspaper owned by Nation Media Group, says the number of fraud dismissals has now risen for four years in a row.

Alongside the 118 dismissals, the report records 3 disciplinary warnings, where the year before it recorded none. It also lists 14 cases passed to law enforcement, double the 7 of the previous year, TechMoran reported.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Kenya markets Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Where the Money Was Lost

The largest recovery came from inflated agent commissions. Agents are the small shops that take cash in and pay it out for M-Pesa customers, and they earn a fee on each transaction.

Safaricom says monitoring and analytics helped it recover KSh953 million (about US$7.3 million) linked to that fraud. TechMoran notes the report does not tie the full amount to staff misconduct.

How the Fraud Crackdown Works

The report says Safaricom recovered 46% of reported fraud losses, and that fraud incidents fell 82% against a target of 90%. Staff misconduct that Kenyan outlets have listed in past years includes SIM-swap help, leaking customer data and breaching company procedures.

Fraud was the most common concern raised through the company’s ethics hotline, and the fraud crackdown sits on top of an ethics programme. That programme reached 98% of employees, the same share as the year before.

The Scale of M-Pesa

M-Pesa handled about 46.4 billion transactions worth KSh41.7 trillion (about US$321 billion) in the year, with 41.7 million customers active in the last 30 days. That scale is why the fraud crackdown matters.

Social engineering, where criminals trick customers into handing over codes or money, was the leading threat to customers, the report says. The company also names fraud powered by artificial intelligence as a growing challenge.

Who Owns Safaricom

Safaricom is listed on the Nairobi Securities Exchange, and South Africa’s Vodacom holds 55% after buying a 15% state stake. An appeal over that sale is still pending, as the Rio Times reported in its earlier story on the Vodacom stake.

Readers can find the company’s share data and background in the Rio Times Safaricom profile. Safaricom also launched a new overdraft for small traders on Thursday 22 October, covered in the Rio Times report on Fuliza Ya Pochi.

What It Means for US Readers

Vodafone, which controls Vodacom and therefore Safaricom, has American depositary receipts that trade on Nasdaq, so Safaricom’s governance reaches US portfolios. A rising count of dismissals can signal tighter controls or wider abuse, and the report does not settle which.

US companies that sell goods or services in Kenya often take payment through M-Pesa, which makes the platform’s integrity a business risk. Travelers who use M-Pesa should treat unexpected calls asking for codes as fraud, because social engineering is the main threat the company names.

What Is Not Known

Safaricom has not said how much money the 118 dismissed employees took, or how many of them face criminal charges. The report gives 14 referrals to law enforcement but no list of cases or outcomes.

It is also unclear how much of the KSh953 million (about US$7.3 million) recovered came from staff and how much from outside agents. The company has not said whether the fraud crackdown will shrink the number of dismissals next year.

More: Kenya news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How many Safaricom employees were dismissed for fraud?

Safaricom dismissed 118 employees over fraud in the financial year to March 2026. That is up from 113 the year before.

How much money did Safaricom recover?

Safaricom recovered KSh953 million (about US$7.3 million) linked to inflated agent commissions. The report also says it recovered 46% of reported fraud losses.

What is M-Pesa?

M-Pesa is Safaricom’s mobile-money service, which lets people in Kenya send money, pay bills and shop from a phone. It handled about KSh41.7 trillion (about US$321 billion) in the year to March 2026.

Who owns Safaricom?

Vodacom, a South African mobile group, holds 55% of Safaricom after buying a stake from the Kenyan government. Vodacom is controlled by Britain’s Vodafone.

Does this affect US investors?

Vodafone’s receipts trade on Nasdaq, so Safaricom’s results and governance reach US holders indirectly. The dismissals show active controls, but the report gives no loss total.

World.title: Panama Thanks US for Quake Help
World.content:
PANAMA · DIPLOMACY

Key Facts — What is happening Panama’s President José Raúl Mulino thanked US Secretary of State Marco Rubio by phone on Tuesday, 27 October for help after the 9 October earthquake.

— Why it matters The call shows Washington staying close to Panama during its recovery, and it put the race to lead the United Nations on the table.

— The numbers President Donald Trump approved an initial US$5 million, and 20 US specialists helped check buildings. The quake measured 7.7 on the US Geological Survey scale.

— Who is who Mulino is Panama’s president; Rubio is the top US diplomat; António Guterres, the UN secretary-general, leaves office on 31 December.

— What to watch Panama plans 2,700 new houses after the quake, and the UN must pick a successor to Guterres who starts on 1 January 2027.

— Power Index Panama ranks 11th of 14 in Panama ranks 11th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 34.2 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you US aid to Panama is continuing, and travellers should check local advisories before visiting the four quake-hit provinces.

Panama’s president thanked the US for earthquake help in a call with Rubio. He also asked that the next UN chief come from Latin America.

Panama’s president thanked US Secretary of State Marco Rubio by phone on Tuesday, 27 October, for help after the 9 October quake. President José Raúl Mulino also discussed who should lead the United Nations from 2027, the foreign ministry says.

It matters to US readers because Washington is helping this Central American ally recover from the quake. More is in the Rio Times Panama hub.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Panama ranks 11th of 14 with 34.2 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (64); weakest: military means (11). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

What the Call Covered

The foreign ministry says Mulino thanked the United States for humanitarian aid and for staff who checked buildings for structural damage. It calls that help “enormous” for the reconstruction now under way.

A second ministry note says Rubio sent a message of solidarity from the American people and promised support through the whole rebuilding. The first note adds that the two discussed the state of democracy in the region.

The ministry says both men agreed that the next UN chief needs broad consensus. Neither ministry note mentions the Panama Canal.

What the United States Has Sent

US Ambassador Kevin Marino Cabrera said in mid-October that President Donald Trump approved US$5 million, which he called only the initial help. The United States also provided 20 specialists to assess damage to schools, churches and hospitals.

Cabrera said Washington was weighing more engineers and had brought in Black Hawk helicopters through US Southern Command, its regional military arm. The ministry says aid including food, water and communications systems arrived within 24 hours.

The Quake and Panama’s Rebuilding

The US Geological Survey, the US government’s earth-science agency, recorded a magnitude 7.7 quake on 9 October. Panamanian reports have used 7.5, and the government declared a national emergency.

The worst-hit areas are the provinces of Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas and Coclé. Earlier coverage is in the Rio Times report on the first quake victim.

On the same Tuesday, Mulino ordered 1,400 more houses on top of 1,300 already started, after a cabinet meeting. The cabinet also let a state-bank trust fund builders, and a resolution allows up to US$100 million for special emergency contracts.

The Rio Times has also covered a US$310 million credit line for quake-hit firms and a telethon for quake homes. Both show the cost of recovery.

Why the UN Chief Matters

Guterres, a Portuguese former prime minister, ends his term on 31 December. His successor starts on 1 January 2027.

Mulino argued that the unwritten rule of regional rotation should give the post to Latin America or the Caribbean. The ministry says Rubio and Mulino agreed that the choice needs broad consensus.

What It Means for US Readers

US aid in Panama is ongoing, and the ambassador says more may follow. Charities, companies and Panamanian families in the United States can expect continued coordination between the two governments.

Travellers should check local advisories for Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas and Coclé before visiting, since reconstruction continues. Neither ministry note mentions the Panama Canal.

What Is Not Known

No official US total for the aid was found, only the US$5 million initial sum. The full US readout of the call was not found, and the ministry notes name no candidate for UN chief.

The final death toll and total damage bill were not in the sources reviewed. It is also unclear whether the US plans to add funds beyond the US$5 million Trump approved.

What Comes Next

The first 1,300 houses are under construction, with 1,400 more ordered. Mulino says the money will be there, and Rio Times will track whether builders meet the pace.

The UN will pick Guterres’s successor before 1 January 2027, though no vote date appears in the notes. The call does not mean Washington has backed a Latin American candidate.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did Rubio call Panama’s president?

Panama’s ministry says Rubio called to review recovery after the 9 October earthquake and to discuss the next UN secretary-general. Mulino thanked the United States for its help.

How much has the United States given Panama?

President Trump approved an initial US$5 million, which Ambassador Cabrera called only a first sum. No full official US total was found.

What did Mulino ask about the UN?

He asked that the next secretary-general come from Latin America or the Caribbean, citing regional rotation. Both men agreed on seeking broad consensus.

How strong was the Panama earthquake?

The US Geological Survey recorded magnitude 7.7 on 9 October, while Panamanian reports used 7.5. The worst damage was in Herrera, Los Santos, Veraguas and Coclé.

Does this affect the Panama Canal?

Neither ministry note mentions the canal. Nothing in them points to a change in canal policy.

World.content:

BOTSWANA · MARKETS

Key Facts — The country Botswana is a landlocked diamond-producing country of about 2.5 million people in Southern Africa, with a small stock exchange in the capital, Gaborone.

— What happened Access Bank Botswana is offering receipts, each equal to one Dangote refinery share, and the Sunday Standard wrote on 25 October that the window was closing.

— The company Access Bank Botswana Limited is the local arm of Nigeria’s Access Bank, which completed a 78.15% purchase in October 2021.

— The size Mmegi, citing its own sources, put the Gaborone offer at US$500 million (P6.9 billion) of the refinery’s US$1.6 billion sale.

— The ticket Ten shares at the main offer’s ₦525 (about US$0.39) would cost about ₦5,250 (about US$3.88, or about P55); the receipt price is unpublished.

— The reach The Botswana Stock Exchange is the trading hub for 14 members of the regional Committee of SADC Stock Exchanges.

— Still open The pula price of each receipt, the Botswana allocation limits and the final subscription total have not been published.

Access Bank Botswana is offering local investors a stake in the Dangote refinery share sale, Africa’s largest, through receipts that are to list in Gaborone. The Sunday Standard, a Gaborone weekly, wrote on 25 October that the window to join was in its final days.

For US readers, the deal shows a Nigerian bank and a small Southern African exchange routing regional savings into a US$1.6 billion refinery. The main offer in Nigeria was scheduled to close on Tuesday 27 October 2026.

What Access Bank Botswana Is Selling

Access Bank Botswana Limited is the Gaborone unit of Nigeria’s Access Bank, which bought a 78.15% stake in the Botswana lender in 2021. It is issuing Botswana Depository Receipts, or BDRs, that stand in for Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals shares.

Each receipt equals one refinery share, and the bank has secured a block of offer shares to back them. The Mmegi newspaper calls this an unsponsored structure, meaning Dangote did not set the shares aside and the bank went into the offer itself.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Botswana markets Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the Receipts Reach Ordinary Savers

Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest businessman, owns the group behind the refinery near Lagos. The company is selling 4.1 billion new shares at ₦525 (about US$0.39) each, which would raise about ₦2.15 trillion (about US$1.59 billion).

Mmegi reported that investors can start with ten shares, unlike most share sales that ask for blocks of thousands. Access Bank Botswana’s managing director, Sheperd Aisam, called it a people’s IPO aimed at ordinary, low-income retail investors.

Why Gaborone Became the Regional Hub

The Dangote Group chose the Botswana Stock Exchange to host the platform, and the Committee of Southern African Stock Exchanges lobbied for Gaborone. Mmegi said the committee’s 14 members can reach the receipts through the exchange’s existing systems.

Mmegi’s BusinessWeek section, citing its own sources, put the size of the offer hosted on the exchange at US$500 million (P6.9 billion). Zimbabwe’s Financial Securities Exchange is taking applications through the same Botswana-based programme, and its window ran to 21 October, Billionaires Africa reported.

Pension Money Drives the Interest

Botswana’s pension funds held more than P176 billion (about US$12.5 billion) at the end of June, Mmegi reported. Fund managers and pension funds pressed Dangote for local access when he visited Gaborone.

Thato Norman, chief executive of the Debswana Pension Fund, which holds more than P12 billion (about US$850 million), spoke to Dangote at that meeting. Minerals and energy minister Bogolo Kenewendo welcomed the receipts platform on Wednesday 14 October as a way for Africans to own African assets.

Price, Dates and Trading

Zimbabwe’s exchange quoted an indicative price of 40 US cents per receipt, and BusinessDay reported that trading is expected to begin on Monday 14 December. No pula price for the Botswana receipts has been published.

Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission pushed the main offer’s closing date from 13 October to 27 October. Zimbabwe’s exchange closed its window earlier than Lagos to leave time for application checks, exchange-control paperwork and transfers, Billionaires Africa reported.

What It Means for US Readers

The offer is aimed at investors in Botswana and the participating Southern African markets, and no route for US investors has been reported. A strong take-up would back Dangote’s plan, reported by Mmegi, to lift refinery output from about 650,000 to 1.4 million barrels a day by 2030.

American suppliers and fuel traders who deal with West African refiners should watch the outcome, because new equity could ease the refinery’s funding. The Rio Times covered the refinery’s valuation after its nine-month results and the subscriptions from more than 90 countries.

What Is Not Known

Neither Access Bank Botswana nor the exchange has published the pula price of one receipt. Mmegi noted that the limits on the receipts have not been made public.

The final amount raised through Gaborone will only be clear after Nigeria closes the books. The date when the receipts first trade has been reported only as an expectation.

Whether Nigeria closed its offer on 27 October as scheduled was not confirmed in the Botswana reports. Readers should check current terms with the Botswana Stock Exchange or Access Bank Botswana.

More: Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Access Bank Botswana offering?

Access Bank Botswana is offering Botswana Depository Receipts, each equal to one share of the Dangote refinery. They are to be listed on the Botswana Stock Exchange in Gaborone.

How much can Access Bank Botswana raise?

Mmegi, citing its own sources, put the Botswana offer at US$500 million, about P6.9 billion. That would be close to a third of the refinery’s US$1.6 billion share sale.

What is the smallest purchase?

Mmegi reported that investors can start with ten shares. At the ₦525 (about US$0.39) offer price in Nigeria that is about ₦5,250 (about US$3.88).

When does the offer close?

Nigeria’s main offer was scheduled to close on Tuesday 27 October 2026. Zimbabwe’s window closed earlier, on 21 October.

Who owns Access Bank Botswana?

It is the Botswana unit of Nigeria’s Access Bank, which completed its purchase of a 78.15% stake in October 2021. Its profile is in the Rio Times company directory.

Can US investors buy the receipts?

The offer is aimed at investors in Botswana and the participating Southern African markets. No route for US investors has been reported.

Sources: Mmegi, Botswana to host regional Dangote IPO hub, 19 October 2026; Mmegi, Why local pension funds billions are chasing Dangote, 21 September 2026; Sunday Standard, the people’s IPO gains momentum (introduction only, paywalled), 25 October 2026; Billionaires Africa, Zimbabweans have until Oct. 21 to buy Dangote refinery stock (citing The Herald and BusinessDay), 19 October 2026; Access Holdings, completion of Botswana acquisition, 11 October 2021.

World.title: Costa Rica Arrests Suspect in US Man’s Death
World.content:
COSTA RICA · SECURITY

Key Facts — What is happening Costa Rica’s judicial police (the OIJ) arrested a 22-year-old woman on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, in Alajuelita, near San José, as the main suspect in the killing of US citizen Marc Fleming.

— Why it matters Fleming was an American killed in a beach condominium in Guanacaste, Costa Rica’s north-western beach province, and the case drew wide attention in international media.

— The numbers Fleming died on 27 September, the suspect evaded a raid on 16 October and stayed at large for almost two weeks, and his age is variously stated as 67, 72 or 74.

— Who is who The OIJ is the judicial police; the suspect is known only by the surname Ortiz, and a second woman, surnamed Zeledón Abarca, was detained on 16 October on suspicion of helping her.

— What to watch Prosecutors must now decide which pretrial measures to ask a judge for, such as preventive detention, and no hearing date or formal charge has been announced.

— Power Index Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 in Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 36.5 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you The US State Department advises Americans to exercise increased caution in Costa Rica because of crime; no US Embassy statement on this case has been found.

Costa Rica has arrested the woman investigators call the main suspect in the death of an American at a beach condominium. She is accused, not convicted, and no court has ruled.

Costa Rica arrests suspect in the killing of an American man at a Pacific-coast condominium, ending a hunt of almost two weeks. The OIJ, the country’s judicial police, detained a 22-year-old woman on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, in Alajuelita, south of San José.

The victim, US citizen Marc Fleming, died on Sunday, 27 September, in a Playas del Coco condominium apartment. The woman is a suspect only, and no court has tested the evidence.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 with 36.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (75); weakest: military means (0). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

In Plain English OIJ: the Organismo de Investigación Judicial, Costa Rica’s judicial police, which investigates crimes and carries out raids.

the Organismo de Investigación Judicial, Costa Rica’s judicial police, which investigates crimes and carries out raids. Public prosecutors (Ministerio Público): the state office that decides on charges and asks judges for pretrial measures.

the state office that decides on charges and asks judges for pretrial measures. Preventive detention: jail ordered by a judge while a case is investigated, before any trial or verdict.

jail ordered by a judge while a case is investigated, before any trial or verdict. Guanacaste: Costa Rica’s north-western Pacific province, known for beach towns such as Playas del Coco.

Costa Rica’s north-western Pacific province, known for beach towns such as Playas del Coco. Alajuelita: a district just south of San José, the capital, where the arrest took place.

The Arrest in Alajuelita

OIJ agents detained the woman on Tuesday in San Felipe, a neighbourhood of Alajuelita, the agency confirmed. She is identified only by the surname Ortiz, and she is 22 years old.

She had been wanted since Friday, 16 October, when agents raided a home in La Capri, Desamparados, and missed her. She stayed out of reach for almost two weeks.

Reports differ on the arrest itself. One says she was detained on a public road, another that she was found at a relative’s home in a housing complex.

Some media have given her a nickname based on clothing seen in security video. It is not used here, because she is a suspect and no court has ruled.

Free download · Expat checklist Get the free checklist as PDF Moving to Costa Rica 2026: the step-by-step checklist. This guide condensed into 3 printable pages with tick boxes and the key official links. Email address Get the PDF Free. We send a confirmation link first, and the same address then receives The Rio Times Brief, our daily briefing. Unsubscribe with one click at any time; see our privacy policy. Your checklist is ready. Download the PDF checklist

What Investigators Say Happened in Playas del Coco

Fleming, a US citizen reported to be from California, died on Sunday, 27 September, in a Playas del Coco condominium apartment. Reports give his age as 67, 72 or 74.

Security cameras show him entering the building at about 4:50 p.m. with a young woman, who later left alone. He was found with multiple head wounds.

Investigators’ main hypothesis is that the attack was carried out with the glass jar of a kitchen blender. No motive has been stated.

How Investigators Traced the Suspects

Investigators say Fleming’s foreign bank cards were used after the killing in Playas del Coco, Brasilito, Flamingo and Abangares. Footage from shops and a cash machine helped trace a route towards the Central Valley.

On 16 October the OIJ detained a second woman, surnamed Zeledón Abarca, in San Miguel de Desamparados. Investigators say she picked up the main suspect in Guanacaste and drove her to San José.

The OIJ released images of the main suspect in a white top and denim shorts and asked the public for tips. Whether the cards were taken, and by whom, is still being examined.

Earlier coverage reported the first arrest on 16 October in this case. The Costa Rica country page follows security and justice news across the country.

What It Means for US Readers

The US State Department’s Costa Rica advisory tells Americans to exercise increased caution because of crime. It says petty crime is the main threat to tourists, but that violent crime, including armed robbery and homicide, occurs.

The advisory adds that the Costa Rican government provides extra security resources in areas that tourists frequent. It is general guidance and does not mention this case.

No US Embassy or State Department statement on the arrest has been found. Related security news includes Costa Rica’s 478 US deportees and a US extradition request for a suspected money launderer.

For background, see who holds power in Costa Rica and the San José city page for visitors based in the capital. Neither changes the advisory, which applies to the whole country.

What Is Not Known

No formal charge, court hearing or detention order for the main suspect has been reported. The motive, how the two met and the exact cause of death have not been stated by the OIJ.

The victim’s age is reported as 67, 72 and 74, and his first name appears as both Marc and Mark. Reports also differ on how long the woman stayed in the apartment and where she was arrested.

The OIJ had not posted a release on its news page when this article was written. The account therefore rests on the agency’s statements as relayed by Costa Rican media, and allegations against both women remain unproven.

What Comes Next

Prosecutors must decide which pretrial measures to request from a judge, and a hearing before a judge would be the next step. No date has been announced.

The investigation will keep testing the card records and camera footage. A hearing or a measure does not mean guilt.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who has been arrested in Costa Rica?

The OIJ, Costa Rica’s judicial police, arrested a 22-year-old woman surnamed Ortiz on Tuesday, 27 October 2026. She is the main suspect in the killing of US citizen Marc Fleming.

Where and when did the killing happen?

Fleming died on Sunday, 27 September 2026, in a condominium apartment in Playas del Coco, a beach town in Guanacaste. Security cameras show him entering at about 4:50 p.m. with a woman.

Has anyone been charged or convicted?

No formal charge, hearing or verdict has been reported. Both women held in the case are suspects, and prosecutors must decide which pretrial measures to seek.

Who is the second woman detained?

A woman surnamed Zeledón Abarca was detained on Friday, 16 October, in San Miguel de Desamparados. Investigators say she picked up the main suspect after the killing and drove her to San José.

Is Costa Rica safe for American visitors?

The US State Department tells Americans to exercise increased caution in Costa Rica because of crime. It says petty crime is the main threat to tourists, but violent crime, including homicide, occurs.

Sources: Organismo de Investigación Judicial (OIJ), news and police notices; US State Department, Costa Rica travel advisory (accessed 28 October 2026).

World.title: Chile Tests Primera B Disaffiliation Rules
World.content:
File photo, 2019. Headquarters of the ANFP in Peñalolén, Santiago, the seat of the association whose disciplinary tribunal ruled on San Marcos de Arica. (Photo: Carlos Figueroa Rojas, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

CHILE · FOOTBALL

Key Facts The country Chile is a South American country whose professional football runs in three tiers under one body, the Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional (ANFP). Promotion and relegation are settled on the pitch unless the ANFP’s own courts step in.

Why it matters The rules show how a second-division club can lose its league membership over paperwork filed with the league’s own financial control unit. There is no direct US link, but the case matters to readers who follow Chilean football or club governance in Latin America.

Why now On Tuesday 27 October the ANFP disciplinary tribunal voted 6-1 to disaffiliate the Primera B club San Marcos de Arica. The league’s final round is scheduled from Friday 30 October to Sunday 1 November.

What happened The tribunal’s first chamber imposed disaffiliation on San Marcos de Arica and rejected a separate complaint against Deportes Puerto Montt the same day. The written sentence is still to come, so the appeal clock has not started.

What it means for you Nothing changes for US travellers or investors. For fans, the rules decide how the final table is read and which clubs go up or down.

Still open Which rule the majority applied, whether the 3-0 defeat rule changes the table, and whether an appeal or a court order reverses the sanction.

Power Index Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in Chile ranks 3rd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 63.6 points (October 2026 edition).

In Plain English The ANFP is the clubs’ own governing association, a corporation that stages the three professional leagues and operates its own courts. Primera B is its second tier, listed on the ANFP site as the Liga de Ascenso. The Tribunal de Disciplina is the ANFP’s disciplinary court, with a seven-judge first chamber (Primera Sala) and a five-judge second chamber (Segunda Sala) that hears appeals. The Consejo de Presidentes de Clubes is the assembly of club presidents that votes on some disaffiliations. Desafiliación, or disaffiliation, means loss of membership in the ANFP. Chilean outlets call a result decided in a tribunal office instead of on the pitch an escritoriazo, a colloquial word.

Chile’s Primera B disaffiliation rules were put to a live test on Tuesday 27 October, when the disciplinary tribunal of the Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional (ANFP) voted 6-1 to disaffiliate the club San Marcos de Arica. Primera B is the second division, and disaffiliation ends a club’s membership in the body that runs Chilean professional football.

The verdict is not final: San Marcos can still appeal to a second chamber, and the clock starts only when the written sentence arrives, expected on Friday 30 October. A separate report covers the ruling against San Marcos de Arica, while this article explains the rules, the gaps and the precedents.

How the Primera B Disaffiliation Rules Work

The grounds sit in article 10 of the ANFP regulation, in force since 1 January 2026, and range from refusing to play to handing the association false documents. Several carry a fine first and disaffiliation only for repeat offenders, but false documents bring disaffiliation outright, while adulterated ones bring relegation at the end of the season.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Chile ranks 3rd of 14 with 63.6 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (86); weakest: diplomatic & cultural influence (38). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

La Tercera wrote that the club allegedly filed sworn financial statements that did not match its later audited accounts, and ADN reported that the ANFP asked for disaffiliation or, if the papers were adulterated rather than false, relegation. The tribunal has not yet published which rule its majority applied.

Disaffiliation is normally decided by the Council of Club Presidents with four fifths of the votes, but for the document grounds the tribunal can impose it directly (article 10.2). The dissenting judge wanted the file sent to the Council, citing the earlier regulation in force when the facts occurred.

A disaffiliated club may return only by earning promotion to the lowest professional division, and the ANFP retains the broadcast and other shared revenue due to the club for the rest of the season to meet its own obligations, with any remainder passing to the other clubs (articles 10.3 and 10.6). Loss of membership does not cancel the club’s debts to the association or to other members.

Where Primera B Sits in Chilean Football

The ANFP organizes three professional tiers: the Primera División (branded Liga de Primera), Primera B and the Segunda División. The 2026 league rules give them 16, 16 and 14 clubs respectively.

Each Primera B club plays 30 matches, and the champion goes up at once while the clubs placed second to eighth enter a playoff for a second promotion place. The bottom club is relegated directly to the Segunda División.

File photo, 2025. Interior of the Estadio Zorros del Desierto in Calama, Cobreloa’s home ground, where Cobreloa is scheduled to host Deportes Puerto Montt in the Primera B final round on 31 October. (Photo: Andre el gigante, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons, cropped)

What Happens to Results and the Table

Article 87 of the 2026 Primera B rules treats a club sanctioned with loss of category during the season as last in the table, with every played and remaining match counted as a 3-0 defeat unless the opponent won by more. The published verdict mentions that article only in a note by one member of the six-judge majority.

BioBioChile projected that Cobreloa and San Luis would each gain three points, reaching 57, while La Tercera wrote that the points are not handed to opponents and the table does not move. Cooperativa applied the 3-0 rule, and primerabchile.cl argued that the public verdict does not show the majority ordering a recalculation.

The ANFP documents consulted, including the verdict and the regulations it cites, say nothing about the club’s players, contracts or youth teams. The national outlets did not report an answer either.

The Appeal Ladder and the Clock

Sanctions on clubs are always appealable to the second chamber, and the appeal is filed with the first chamber within five days of notification of the sentence (articles 47 and 51 of the Code of Procedure and Penalties). Day counts in that code are business days, so weekends and public holidays do not count (article 2).

Tribunal secretary Simón Marín said the written sentence is expected on Friday, as Cooperativa quoted him, and the outlet counted a deadline of Wednesday 4 November. Five business days from a Friday 30 October notification would end on Friday 6 November, which fits ADN’s reference to five business days and the club’s own statement.

Appealing does not by itself suspend a club sanction, but the appellant can ask the second chamber for an order of no innovation, which it must answer within two days (article 47). The second chamber can confirm, revoke or change a sanction, even to increase it, and has 15 days from the filing to issue its sentence on a disaffiliation.

After the internal instances, the ANFP statutes send disputes to the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne (article 42.1) and allow ordinary courts only where ANFP, FIFA or CONMEBOL rules permit. San Marcos has already tried the Court of Appeals of Arica, which declared its protection action inadmissible on 9 October, and La Tercera reported that the club asked it to reconsider.

Earlier Cases and the Melipilla Precedents

The national press documents two earlier cases, both involving Deportes Melipilla, a club from the Santiago region. In December 2021 the first chamber expelled it over double contracts, and RedGol reported that the Court of Arbitration for Sport rejected its appeal in April 2022 after the second chamber had imposed relegation through a points deduction.

In January 2025 the first chamber disaffiliated Melipilla by 5 votes to 2 over allegedly false documents, in a complaint by Deportes Concepción. On 30 January the second chamber unanimously revoked the disaffiliation for lack of conviction that the documents were false, although a separate three-point deduction stayed.

What It Means for You

For US readers there is no direct exposure, because no US club, broadcaster or investor appears in the verdict or the complaints reviewed. The lesson is that in Chile a club’s filings to the ANFP financial control unit can carry league-ending consequences.

Fans following the final round, from Friday 30 October to Sunday 1 November, should treat any recalculated table as provisional until the written sentence and any appeal are decided. Wider context is collected on the Chile news hub, and an earlier piece covers Colo-Colo’s request to keep a nickname on its goalkeeper’s shirt.

What Is Not Known

The written sentence has not been issued, so it is not known which rule the majority applied, what evidence it used or whether article 87 changes the table. The club says it has not been told the grounds and will use every available legal instrument.

It is also not known whether the second chamber or a court will suspend the sanction before the final round, or what happens to the players. No official ANFP count of earlier disaffiliations was found, which leaves the Melipilla cases as the only confirmed benchmarks.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does disaffiliation mean in Chilean football?

It means a club loses its membership in the ANFP, the association that runs Chile’s professional leagues. It can return only by earning promotion to the lowest professional division and meeting the entry requirements.

Can San Marcos de Arica still appeal?

Yes, the club can appeal to the second chamber of the ANFP disciplinary tribunal within five business days of notification of the written sentence. That notification is due on Friday 30 October, according to the tribunal secretary.

What is Primera B in Chile?

Primera B is Chile’s second professional division, with 16 clubs in 2026. Under the 2026 rules two clubs are promoted, the champion and a playoff winner, and one is relegated.

Has a Chilean club been disaffiliated before?

The national press documents two Deportes Melipilla cases, an expulsion in December 2021 and a disaffiliation in January 2025. Both ended with a lighter outcome after appeal.

Does the ruling change the Primera B table?

That is unsettled. Article 87 of the league rules treats a sanctioned club as last with 3-0 defeats, but the published verdict mentions it only in one judge’s note, and outlets disagree on the effect.

World.content:

ZAMBIA · POLITICS

Key Facts — The country Zambia is a landlocked southern African democracy led by President Hakainde Hichilema, re-elected in August 2026.

— What happened Parliament approved the president’s plan to dissolve five ministries and create ten, the Zambia Daily Mail reported on Wednesday 28 October 2026.

— The big split Zambia splits energy ministry work into a Ministry of Electricity and a Ministry of Petroleum.

— Other changes Commerce, infrastructure, lands and youth portfolios are also reorganised, and a Ministry of Skills and Higher Education is created.

— Size of cabinet News Diggers reported that the government proposes to raise the number of ministries from 25 to 30.

— Who moved it Vice President Mutale Nalumango, the Leader of Government Business, moved the motion in the National Assembly.

— Still open The names of the new ministers and the exact date they take office have not been announced.

Zambia splits energy ministry in two after Parliament approved President Hakainde Hichilema’s plan to reorganise his government, the Zambia Daily Mail reported on 28 October. The old Ministry of Energy is replaced by separate Ministries of Electricity and Petroleum.

For US investors, miners and energy suppliers, the change creates separate government counterparts for power and for fuel in a major copper economy. President Hichilema won a second term in the August election.

What Parliament Approved in Lusaka

The National Assembly, Zambia’s single-chamber parliament in the capital Lusaka, approved a proposal to establish, merge and dissolve government ministries. The Zambia Daily Mail said a majority of lawmakers supported the motion.

Vice President Mutale Nalumango, who leads government business in the House, moved it, and Speaker Nelly Mutti put the question to members. The government says the aim is a more efficient state that delivers its Grow Zambia Agenda, its economic programme.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on Zambia Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Five Ministries Go and Ten Take Their Place

Five ministries are dissolved: Energy; Infrastructure, Housing and Urban Development; Commerce, Trade and Industry; Lands and Natural Resources; and Youth, Sport and Arts. Ten replace them, among them Trade and Export, Industry, Electricity, Petroleum, Housing, Lands, Skills and Higher Education, and Culture and Arts.

Nineteen ministries keep their names, including Finance and National Planning, Mines and Minerals Development, Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, and Defence. Nalumango said some duties will still move between ministries even where the name stays the same.

Why Electricity and Petroleum Get Their Own Ministries

Nalumango told the House that dedicated Electricity and Petroleum ministries are needed to answer changing energy demand and to support growth. She said an Electricity ministry is needed to look for innovative ways of generating, transmitting and supplying power.

When Zambia splits energy ministry duties, power generation and fuel supply get their own ministries. She also described culture and the arts as an economic opportunity that can draw tourists and create jobs.

How the Plan Reached the House

President Hichilema wrote to Parliament under Article 92(2)(d) of the constitution, which requires lawmakers to approve new, merged or dissolved ministries. The request came in a statement from Clayson Hamasaka, the president’s chief communications specialist, issued in Lusaka on Monday.

Jack Mwiimbu, the member for Monze East, backed the motion and called it non-controversial and in line with the Grow Zambia Agenda. News Diggers, an independent Lusaka paper, reported on Tuesday 27 October that the government wants to raise the number of ministries from 25 to 30.

What It Means for US Readers

Now that Zambia splits energy ministry work in two, American suppliers of mining gear, solar plants or fuel deal with two ministries instead of one. The government has not said which new ministry will handle licences, power-purchase agreements or fuel import rules.

The Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development keeps its name and its place in the cabinet. Investors tracking Zambia’s election result and second term can read it as a larger cabinet tied to the same Grow Zambia Agenda.

What Is Not Known

The government has not published which ministers will lead the ten new ministries or when they will be sworn in. The cost of running five more ministries has not been stated.

It is also unclear where the natural resources duties of the old Lands and Natural Resources ministry will go. Officials have not said how civil servants and budgets will be moved between the old and new ministries.

More: Zambia news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does it mean that Zambia splits energy ministry work?

After Zambia splits energy ministry duties, the Ministry of Energy no longer exists. Its work is divided between a Ministry of Electricity and a Ministry of Petroleum.

Who approved the changes?

Zambia’s National Assembly approved them on a motion from Vice President Mutale Nalumango. The constitution requires this approval before ministries can be created, merged or dissolved.

How many ministries will Zambia have?

News Diggers reported that the number would rise from 25 to 30. The Zambia Daily Mail listed five ministries dissolved and ten created.

Does the change affect copper mining rules?

The Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development keeps its name and its place in the cabinet. Vice President Nalumango said some functions will still move between ministries even where names stay the same.

When will the new ministers be named?

The government has not given a date. News Diggers reported that it wants to raise the number of ministries from 25 to 30.

Sources: Zambia Daily Mail, 28 October 2026; Zambia Monitor, 26 October 2026; News Diggers, 27 October 2026.

World.title: Mexico Senate Passes US$570B Revenue Law
World.content:
MEXICO · ECONOMY

Key Facts — What is happening Mexico’s Senate passed the 2027 revenue law on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, by 75 votes to 34.

— Why it matters The law sets Mexico’s 2027 income and borrowing limits, and exempts carmakers from a new tax-deduction cap.

— The numbers Income of 10.6 trillion pesos (US$570 billion); borrowing capped at 1.7 trillion pesos (US$91 billion).

— Who is who Morena, the governing party, and its allies backed it; the PAN, PRI and MC opposed it.

— What to watch Deputies must vote again on the income tax change; the spending bill is due by 15 November.

— Power Index Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 71.4 points (October 2026 edition).

— What it means for you Foreign visitors face a higher entry fee, 1,158 pesos (US$62) instead of 983 pesos (US$53).

Mexico’s Senate has passed next year’s revenue law. It adds no new taxes but caps borrowing and gives carmakers a tax break.

Mexico’s Senate approved the country’s 2027 revenue law on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, by 75 votes to 34. The law plans government income of 10.6 trillion pesos (about US$570 billion).

The Senate finished four days before its 31 October deadline. The bill now goes to President Claudia Sheinbaum for publication in the official gazette.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Mexico ranks 2nd of 14 with 71.4 points. Strongest pillar: economic relationships (90); weakest: state capacity & security (46). Alignment group: Hedging. Watch21 homicides per 100,000; organised crime at 7.7 of 10. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Who Is Who in Plain English

Revenue law (Ley de Ingresos): the yearly law that sets what the federal government expects to collect and may borrow; spending is a separate bill.

the yearly law that sets what the federal government expects to collect and may borrow; spending is a separate bill. Senate and Chamber of Deputies: the two houses of Mexico’s Congress; deputies passed the revenue law first, on 15 October.

the two houses of Mexico’s Congress; deputies passed the revenue law first, on 15 October. Morena: Sheinbaum’s governing party; with its allies, the Labor Party (PT) and the Green Party (PVEM), it holds a majority.

Sheinbaum’s governing party; with its allies, the Labor Party (PT) and the Green Party (PVEM), it holds a majority. PAN, PRI and Citizens’ Movement (MC): the opposition parties that voted against the law.

the opposition parties that voted against the law. ISR: the Mexican income tax law (Impuesto sobre la Renta), which the Senate changed.

What the Law Sets for 2027

The law counts on 10.6 trillion pesos (about US$570 billion) of income in 2027. Taxes make up about 6.26 trillion pesos (US$335 billion) of that.

It lets the government borrow up to 1.7 trillion pesos (about US$91 billion) at home. The version the deputies approved also allows borrowing abroad of up to US$13.5 billion, and the Senate left the law unchanged.

Lawmakers said the law adds no new taxes. It assumes economic growth of 1.5% to 2.5% in 2027.

The law also drops a cap of 300 million pesos (about US$16 million) on waiving fines for firms that settle overdue taxes. That lets very large taxpayers use the relief.

How the Senate Voted

Morena and its allies backed the law. The vote was 79 to 34 in general and 75 to 34 on the detailed articles.

The PAN, the PRI and Citizens’ Movement voted against. PAN senator Gina Campuzano questioned what results the borrowing has delivered.

PRI coordinator Manuel Añorve called the package a promissory note (pagaré) that Morena wants Mexicans to pay. Morena’s Manuel Huerta replied that 1.7 trillion pesos (US$91 billion) is a borrowing limit, not an amount the government must borrow.

The Carmaker Tax Break and Why One Law Goes Back

The Senate also changed a separate law, the income tax (ISR) reform. It exempts vehicle assembly and manufacturing companies from a new limit on tax deductions and losses.

Most reports say fuel stations and fuel distributors are exempt too. Morena’s Senate leader Ignacio Mier and Economy Committee chair Emmanuel Reyes proposed the change.

Because the Senate altered the text, the Chamber of Deputies must vote on the income tax reform again. The revenue law and the duties law do not need another vote.

The Senate also approved the Federal Duties Law, which sets government fees. It raises the fee foreign visitors pay to enter Mexico from 983 pesos (about US$53) to 1,158 pesos (about US$62).

What It Means for You

Travelers will pay about US$9 more to enter Mexico, a small rise next to most trip costs. The reports reviewed do not give the date the new fee starts.

Carmakers with plants in Mexico, a major supplier of vehicles to the United States, would avoid a new squeeze on deductions. The deputies still have to confirm the exemption.

Investors get a plan built on 1.5% to 2.5% growth, with the peso at 18.67 per dollar on 28 October. Borrowing is the pressure point, since opposition senators called the 1.7 trillion peso (US$91 billion) cap excessive.

Background is in the guide to US-Mexico relations, the report on how the deputies passed the law and the 2027 budget outlook. The large-firm tax reform, the guide to Mexico’s economy and the Mexico news hub add context.

What Is Not Known

Reports differ on whether fuel stations are exempt. They also differ on how a 50 million peso (about US$2.7 million) threshold in the deduction rule works.

The Senate’s own communiqué and gazette could not be opened, so the figures come from Mexican press accounts that agree. Single-source details, such as peso and inflation assumptions, were left out.

What Comes Next

The revenue law and the duties law go to the president for publication in the official gazette. The Chamber of Deputies must now vote again on the income tax reform.

The 2027 spending bill is next. Deputies are expected to take it up in committee in early November, with a floor vote by 15 November.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Mexico’s Senate approve?

The 2027 revenue law, by 75 votes to 34 on Tuesday, 27 October 2026, and the Federal Duties Law. It also changed the income tax law.

How much will Mexico collect and borrow in 2027?

The law plans income of 10.6 trillion pesos (about US$570 billion). Domestic borrowing is capped at 1.7 trillion pesos (about US$91 billion).

Does the law add new taxes?

Lawmakers said it adds none. It does tighten some business deductions, with an exemption for carmakers.

Why does one law go back to the deputies?

The Senate changed the income tax reform to exempt carmakers from a new deduction limit. A changed text must return to the chamber that passed it first.

Will foreign visitors pay more?

Yes, the entry fee for foreign visitors rises from 983 to 1,158 pesos (about US$53 to US$62). The start date was not given in the reports reviewed.

Sources: Senate of the Republic of Mexico; Chamber of Deputies of Mexico; Sin Embargo, 27 October; La Razón, 28 October; MVS Noticias, 27 October; NX Noticias, 27 October; SDP Noticias, 27 October; Excélsior, 15 October; exchange rate 18.67 pesos per US dollar, open.er-api.com, 28 October (all accessed 28 October 2026).

World.title: Costa Rica Pacific Business Park Faces Tests
World.content:
File photo, 2015. Aerial view of the Puntarenas peninsula and the Gulf of Nicoya on Costa Rica’s Pacific coast; the Pacific Business Park stands in Esparza, in the same province. (Photo: Mariordo (Mario Roberto Durán Ortíz), CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

COSTA RICA · REAL ESTATE

Key Facts The country Costa Rica is a Central American democracy whose state-owned Banco de Costa Rica owns a fund manager that runs US dollar real-estate funds for local savers.

Why it matters A state-owned bank group had to pay about US$89 million to repair a dollar fund hurt by a disputed 2020 purchase, which tests how far the regulator can go against a public bank.

Why now The purchase closed on Tuesday 27 October 2026, which starts the follow-up phase for investors, courts and the regulator.

What happened BCR SAFI bought the Pacific Business Park from a fund it manages, crediting the fund US$87.05 million plus US$2.31 million in legal costs, US$89.36 million in all.

The numbers The fund held US$378.08 million in assets and 1,505 investors at 31 March 2026, and the park was about 100% vacant.

What it means for you Anyone weighing Costa Rican funds or Pacific-coast logistics space gets a live case of regulatory enforcement, with court and criminal proceedings still open.

Still open What the bank group will do with the park, how the cash is used inside the fund, and when the lawsuit and the criminal case end.

Power Index Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 in Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 36.5 points (October 2026 edition).

BCR SAFI, the fund-management arm of state-owned Banco de Costa Rica (BCR), completed the purchase of the Pacific Business Park from a US dollar real-estate fund it manages on Tuesday 27 October, paying US$89.36 million in all. Of that, US$87.05 million was credited to the fund and US$2.31 million covered the legal costs of the transfer deed, according to the BCR SAFI filing (CHR-9250) on the securities regulator’s public register.

Diario Extra headlined US$89 million, Delfino.cr headlined US$87 million and La Nación headlined US$89.3 million, yet all three describe the same two line items, not rival prices. A companion explainer on how the deal works and who BCR SAFI is covers the mechanics, while this piece maps the decisions and dates ahead.

The fund is denominated in US dollars, held US$378.08 million in assets at 31 March 2026 and counted 1,505 investors, according to Moody’s Local Costa Rica, a local credit-rating agency. The questions now sit with Sugeval, the securities regulator, with the courts, with prosecutors and with a bank group that has to decide what to do with a vacant site on the Pacific side of the country.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Costa Rica ranks 9th of 14 with 36.5 points. Strongest pillar: state capacity & security (75); weakest: military means (0). Alignment group: Closer to Washington. WatchRating below investment grade (BB). See the full index, the business lens and the data →

Next Steps for the Pacific Business Park

The park now sits on the books of BCR SAFI and not inside the fund, and the bank group has not said what it will do with it. In August the group said it would define a plan after weighing the property’s features, location, size and potential, according to BCR’s press release of 18 August.

Any resale would start from a low base, since the last valuation booked for the park was US$24.24 million at 31 March 2026, against the US$70.8 million paid in February 2020. CR Hoy calculated in April that a sale near that value would leave a loss of about US$65 million over seven years.

File photo, 2013. The headquarters of Banco de Costa Rica, the state-owned bank that owns BCR SAFI, in San José. (Photo: Luciuskam, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons)

Moody’s Local noted in July that the park was about 100% vacant and could not be marketed because of a sanitary order, so it was producing no rent. In May 2024 the Ministry of Health had ordered seven of its warehouses closed after permits were not renewed, according to CR Hoy.

What Fund Investors Can Expect

The 1,505 investors in the BCR Non-Diversified Real Estate Investment Fund held units worth US$993.26 each at 31 March 2026, according to Moody’s Local. The park made up 50% of the fund’s leasable area and 87% of its empty space, so its exit removes half of the fund’s leasable space at once.

Sugeval’s order requires the money to go to paying the fund’s liabilities, cutting its debt and lowering interest costs, according to La Nación’s account of the resolution. Moody’s Local counted liabilities of US$128.11 million at 31 March 2026, 92% of them loans, with the grace period on the largest loan ending in June 2027.

The credit to the fund also covers financial costs and other items, according to La Nación, so US$87.05 million is not a price for the park alone. Against a book value of US$24.24 million in March the gap is about US$62.8 million, and how it feeds into unit values and payouts has not been published.

Moody’s Local rates the fund BBB.cr with a developing outlook, and said in July that removing the park could improve occupancy, debt levels and cash flow. It added that the rating could be confirmed or changed, up or down, once the process ends.

Courts, Prosecutors and the Regulator

BCR SAFI says it carried out the Sugeval order under protest and with full reservation of rights, without accepting that the contested acts were lawful, according to its filing. A lawsuit that BCR filed on 27 April 2026 against the Central Bank of Costa Rica over the Sugeval order is still pending in the administrative courts, the filing says.

The appeals tribunal for administrative disputes finally rejected the requests of BCR and BCR SAFI to suspend the order on 29 April and 10 August 2026, according to the filing. Those rulings dealt only with suspending the order while the main case proceeds, CR Hoy noted, so the underlying legal question is still undecided.

Separately, the Public Prosecutor’s Office has investigated the 2020 purchase since 2021 and searched properties in December 2025, according to Delfino.cr, which counts 16 search points. CR Hoy reported in April that 14 people appear as suspects in a case about suspected irregular overpricing and influence harming the public treasury.

An investigation is not a finding of guilt, El Observador stressed, and no trial date appeared in the sources reviewed. Sugeval said it will monitor the full execution of the action plan and make sure investors receive the maximum possible information, according to its press release quoted by La Nación.

Tenants and the Pacific Property Market

The park is a complex of warehouses in Caldera, Esparza, in Puntarenas province on the Pacific side, on a site of 540,400 square meters (about 134 acres), according to Delfino.cr. It had no tenants to lose at 31 March 2026, since Moody’s Local put it at about 100% vacant.

Almost all of the fund’s 134 tenants sit in its other properties, led by the Zona Franca El Coyol free-trade zone park at 32% of monthly rent, according to Moody’s Local. Without the park the rest of the fund shows occupancy in line with the market, CR Hoy reported in May, against 42.07% for the whole fund and an industry average of 72% in Moody’s Local data.

What It Means for You

For US investors and companies, the case shows that dollar funds in Costa Rica sit under a regulator that can order a state-owned bank group to repair investors, which it did over two years of appeals. No US company is named as a tenant or party in the filings and reports reviewed.

Moody’s Local indicates the site cannot be marketed while the sanitary order stands, so anyone considering Pacific-coast warehouse space should not count on it. Related Rio Times pages cover Costa Rica and who runs its economy, and nothing here is investment advice.

What Is Not Known

BCR has not said whether it will sell, lease or redevelop the park, and no buyer or tenant has been named. Whether the fire-safety and health permits that blocked leasing have been resolved is also not public.

How the US$87.05 million will be split between debt repayment and other uses inside the fund, and what that does to unit values and payouts, has not been published. The effect on the fund’s credit rating depends on a Moody’s Local review that has no announced date.

It is not known when the lawsuit or the criminal case will end, and no hearing, assembly or trial date appeared in the sources reviewed. The next fixed date on record is June 2027, when the grace period on the fund’s largest loan ends, according to Moody’s Local.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who bought Costa Rica’s Pacific Business Park?

BCR SAFI, the fund-management arm of state-owned Banco de Costa Rica, bought it on Tuesday 27 October. It acquired the park from the BCR real-estate fund it manages after an October 2024 order from the regulator Sugeval.

How much did BCR SAFI pay for the park?

The BCR SAFI filing totals US$89.36 million. That is US$87.05 million credited to the fund plus US$2.31 million in legal costs.

What happens to the fund’s investors now?

Sugeval’s order directs the money to paying the fund’s liabilities, cutting debt and lowering interest costs. The regulator says it will monitor the plan and give investors the maximum possible information.

Is the legal fight over?

The main lawsuit filed by BCR on 27 April 2026 is still pending. BCR SAFI paid under protest, with full reservation of its rights.

Is the criminal investigation closed?

The Ministerio Público has investigated the 2020 purchase since 2021 and searched properties in December 2025, according to Delfino.cr. An investigation is not a finding of guilt, and no trial date appeared in the sources reviewed.

Sources: SUGEVAL, hecho relevante CHR-9250 filed by BCR SAFI (entry 117257), 27 October 2026; Banco de Costa Rica, press release, 18 August 2026; Moody’s Local Costa Rica rating report on the BCR real-estate fund, 20 July 2026; Sugeval, mandate page; La Nación, 27 October 2026; Delfino.cr, 28 October 2026; Diario Extra, 27 October 2026; El Observador, 27 October 2026; La República, 27 October 2026; CR Hoy, 18 August 2026; CR Hoy, 18 August 2026 (valuation and appeals ruling); CR Hoy, 2 May 2026; CR Hoy, 6 April 2026; CR Hoy, 13 May 2024; La Nación, 29 November 2024.
