World.title: Croatian Campsites are the Most Expensive in Europe
World.content:
October the 27th, 2026 – Croatian campsites might be considered the most expensive in Europe, but the Germans still deem them the best. Here’s how much an average day costs.

For the ever-keen German campers, Germany itself is the most popular camping destination, while Croatia is the third most popular foreign destination, behind Italy and France, with the Netherlands in fifth place. Poslovni reports that Croatian campsites can expect continued strong demand from the German market throughout 2027, given that German campers give them the highest quality ratings in all of Europe, even though according to new research they are simultaneously the most expensive. This was highlighted by Uwe Frers, CEO of PiNCAMP, part of the German automobile club ADAC system.

German tourists, along with Slovenian and Austrian visitors, are the most numerous guests filling up Croatian campsites, and the German market is of particular importance for this segment, as well as for overall Croatian tourism. In a recent interview with Hina, Frers explained that ADAC’s digital tourism platform PiNCAMP also cooperates with the Dutch automobile club ANWB and the Swiss TCS.

“These auto clubs are among the largest in all of Europe, with a total of around 30 million members, many of whom are campers,” says Frers. At the recent Croatian Camping Congress, Frers presented one of their newer surveys on campers’ attitudes towards the quality and prices of campsites in 2026 and for 2027, conducted on the German and Dutch markets. For this purpose, they surveyed more than six thousand campers in two studies during the first three quarters of 2026.

around 25% of germans now go camping

The research showed that campers have positive attitudes and that demand from these two countries for Croatian campsites is growing. Demand from German campers is growing particularly strongly, for which Frers sees reasons in the rising number of camping vehicles in that country, from last year’s 1.7 million to this year’s 2 million, which is also a new record and, as he adds, “a great figure for the camping sector.” They also established that around 25 percent of Germans now go camping, which is a 19 percent increase compared to data from 2023. Frers also noted that a quarter of all camping vehicles in Europe are registered in Germany, followed by France with 19 percent, the United Kingdom with 13 percent, and the Netherlands with a 9 percent share.

interesting results for croatia and croatian camping

For Croatia specifically, he cites two interesting research results. The first is quality, which is the most important novelty, because campers gave it the best ratings. The second result is that Croatia is at the same time the most expensive camping destination. “In the past, we discussed how someone can be the most expensive and yet not the best. Now we can end such discussions, because Croatia has shown that it is the best in camping in terms of quality, so it is therefore justified that it also leads in price levels,” Frers believes.

He finds it interesting that Croatia has pursued a fairly aggressive pricing policy in recent years, but that this has now changed, because the average price increase in camping in Europe is around 8 percent, while Croatia with 7 percent is below that average. “So, being a leader in quality, while at the same time keeping price growth below the average, is the right tactic for surviving in this market,” Frers recommends. When asked about the average prices, he said that in Croatia it is €77 per day in a campsite, which is also the highest price among all countries, while the European average is around €50.

“In Europe, there are regions that are extremely cheap, as well as some very expensive ones. Croatia is clearly positioned in the luxury segment, and that position is further strengthened by its ‘leadership’ in quality, which is additionally confirmed in the research by campers stating that Croatian campsites offer good value for money,” says Frers.

However, he adds, in the research 56 percent of respondents said they had no opinion on this, which means they do not have a negative attitude either, while the remaining 44 percent are divided – half of them consider the Croatian camping offer acceptable and good, and the other half poor. “The fact that more than half of the respondents have no opinion at all I consider a good starting point for attracting new guests to Croatian campsites that should be utilised,” Frers stated.

croatia is the third most popular camping destination

For German campers, Germany itself is the most popular camping destination, while Croatia is the third most popular foreign destination, behind Italy and France, with the Netherlands in fifth place. Croatia is rated the best by the largest number of respondents (22 percent) in terms of price-quality ratio for camping, followed by Germany, Italy, Switzerland and Austria. In terms of quality, Croatia also occupies the leading position with the best average campsite rating of 3.9 stars, while the Netherlands, Luxembourg and France have 3.7 stars, Spain 3.6, and Italy 3.5. In terms of camping prices per day for 2027, Croatia leads with an average of €77, Switzerland is second with €65, followed by Italy with €64, Austria with €61 and the United Kingdom with €55.

World.title: Omiš Fire Claimed 6 Lives, Yet There’s No investigation Result Yet
World.content:
October the 27th, 2026 – The horrific Omiš fire has now tragically claimed six lives. Despite the severity of the disaster, there has still been no investigation result even after two months.

73 days have now passed since the major fire that broke out on the 13th of August in Lokva Rogoznica and spread down towards Omiš. Katarina Ergovic Arnaut reports for Index that the public still has no answer to the crucial question: how exactly this enormous fire started and who, if anyone, is responsible for it. In the meantime, the number of victims has risen to a horrendous six. Just two days ago, a 66-year-old woman who had been being treated in hospital since August for serious injuries sustained in the fire, died in hospital.

Despite the sheer scale of the tragedy, the police and the County State Attorney’s Office in Split have so far not publicly released the results of the investigation, nor have they announced whether the cause of the fire has been determined. It has also not been announced that anyone has been suspected or arrested in connection with its outbreak.

camera footage was examined and experts have been on the terrain taking samples

The investigation was launched immediately after the fire. The State Attorney’s Office (DORH) announced 71 days ago, on 15 August, that a crime scene investigation had been carried out at the place where the fire started in Lokva Rogoznica, involving the police, a fire and explosion protection inspector, and chemical-physical experts from the “Ivan Vučetić” Centre. Material samples were taken at the site where the fire broke out. Orders were also issued for the seizure of surveillance camera footage from the entire burned area, surveying of the terrain, and photographing of destroyed houses, other buildings and vehicles.

DORH stated at the time that the necessary expert examinations and other actions would be carried out in order to establish all the circumstances of the event. Over two months later, the results of these procedures have still not been presented to the public.

the fire directly affected around 1,000 hectares

According to the findings of the on-site investigation at the time, the fire broke out on the 13th of August around 20:00 in a heavily forested area next to the road in the wider Lokva Rogoznica area. Carried by strong winds, it spread quickly towards Omiš along a strip approximately 23 kilometres long and up to one and a half kilometres wide. Around 1,000 hectares of thick pine forest, grass and Dalmatian shrubs were burned. Numerous houses, business premises, plantations and vehicles were also claimed by the flames, and material damage in the multi millions was caused. Several dozen people were also injured to some extent or another in the fire.

The first victim, a seasonal worker from neighbouring Bosnia and Herzegovina, Dragana Antešević (34), tragically died during the fire itself. Later, retired firefighter Drago Lelas (79), Katica Nikolić (58), Ivana Kovačić (41), a 70-year-old man who was being treated at KBC Split, and the 66-year-old woman who died two days ago also succumbed to their injuries.

the question of responsibility

With each new victim, the importance of answering the question of how the fire started and whether anyone bears responsibility for the tragedy grows further. The question of the warning system’s response also remains open, because the SRUUK system was not activated during the fire. The system was introduced precisely so that citizens in crisis situations, such as major fires, floods, earthquakes or other immediate dangers, would receive timely warnings and instructions on how to protect themselves. The heartbroken families of the deceased and the public are therefore still waiting for the results of the investigation, as well as an answer to the question of whether all available mechanisms for warning the population were used on the night of the fire.

World.title: Minister: Economic recovery does not happen overnight
World.content:
Economic recovery will take a little longer for people to feel its effects, Minister of Economic Affairs and Industry Liina Vahtras (Reform) said on Tuesday, commenting on the latest consumer confidence survey.

Businesses believe the economy has improved this month, but consumers were more pessimistic, data from Statistics Estonia published on Tuesday shows.

Companies have held this view for some time, so the survey results were no surprise to the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications. The industrial sector is in its strongest position in four years.

"Of course, major negative events also took place four years ago, and confidence then plummeted. By now, we have climbed out of that hole. However, according to surveys, consumer economic confidence has fallen to its lowest level in six months," said Mario Lambing, chief analyst at the Ministry of Economic Affairs.

Since May, Statistics Estonia has conducted economic confidence surveys instead of the Estonian Institute of Economic Research, and the ministry comments on the results once a quarter.

Vahtras also commented on the results.

"Economic recovery and improvement simply take a little more time; they do not happen overnight. People will feel that things have actually improved for them. And the effects of the income tax reform implemented at the beginning of the year will simply be felt a little later," she said.

High motor fuel prices and the winter heating season have made people more cautious about the future. "If this winter is colder and heating bills rise, the government will discuss how to compensate both private consumers and businesses," the minister added.

Lambing said the change in survey provider has made consumers' opinions more pessimistic.

"One factor is indeed the change in survey provider, but a bigger change may have come from the fact that consumers were now surveyed online instead of by telephone, and these methods can produce different results, even if you ask exactly the same person exactly the same question," he said.

World.title: Estonian tennis player Ingrid Neel reaches Tokyo quarterfinals
World.content:
Estonian-American tennis player Ingrid Neel and her Mexican partner Giuliana Olmos opened the WTA tournament in Tokyo with a win and are through to the quarterfinals.

Neel and Olmos beat Shuko Aoyama of Japan and En Shuo Liang of Taiwan 4:6, 6:4, 10:8 in the first round of the women's doubles. In the deciding set they came back from 1:5 down, winning four points in a row from 3:6 and holding firm at the decisive moments.

In the quarterfinals they face Tereza Mihalikova (Slovakia) and Olivia Nicholls (Great Britain), who eliminated the third-seeded pair Erin Routliffe (New Zealand) and Aldila Sutjiadi (Indonesia) 6:2, 6:3.

Tokyo is hosting a WTA 500 singles event, where the top seed is world number one Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan. Rybakina, who recently won the equivalent-level tournament in China, had a first-round bye and next faces her compatriot, Yulia Putintseva.

Two of the four top seeds withdrew at the last moment — Poland's Maja Chwalinska and Switzerland's Belinda Bencic are not taking part. Diana Shnaider, Elise Mertens and home crowd favorite Naomi Osaka are however still in the Tokyo competition.

World.title: KAPO requests access to bank data register after shutdown
World.content:
KAPO has been blocked from accessing the register by the Justice Ministry for failing to implement a data tracker tool by the October 1 deadline, and the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) has been hit by the same block.

Palloson says the legislation permits KAPO to continue accessing the register without installing the tracker, at least in the case of national security matters.

"It has now become clear that the Police and Border Guard Board and KAPO have not established the necessary interfaces, which means that these agencies' access to the Enforcement Register and the e-arrest system must be closed. I ask the Center of Registers and Information Systems (RIK) to arrange the immediate technical shutdown of the services," Justice Ministry Deputy Secretary General Mari-Liis Mikli wrote in a letter to the RIK.

However, KAPO Director General Palloson says that, under the Code of Enforcement Procedure, the requirement for a technical solution — in this case a data tracker — does not apply to security authorities when performing tasks stipulated in the Security Authorities Act or conducting security vetting specified in the State Secrets and Classified Information of Foreign States Act.

"Consequently, we request continued access to the Enforcement Register and the e-arrest system for the performance of tasks stipulated in Section 6 of the Security Authorities Act and for conducting security vetting under the State Secrets and Classified Information of Foreign States Act," he wrote.

Palloson also specified which data KAPO wants its right to query restored: the existence of a bank account, account balance, account statement, persons authorized to use the account, who the beneficial owner of the account holder is, and whether a safe deposit box exists.

The KAPO director general confirmed that since October 1 his authority has not made any queries via the Enforcement Register as part of criminal proceedings, and has now also technically disabled the corresponding type of query.

"We also confirm that KAPO has taken measures to ensure the lawfulness of data processing and exercises sufficient oversight over it," Palloson noted.

The Enforcement Register (Estonian: Täitmisregister) is a state channel allowing authorities to query bank account data and place attachments. In 2025 Chancellor of Justice Ülle Madise found agencies had been accessing confidential bank data without the correct legal basis. The solution was the data tracker, which lets individuals see who has queried their data. Legislation putting this in place passed at the Riigikogu, with the installation deadline set at October 1. Other authorities initially blocked but now able to access the register, having installed the tracker, are the Tax and Customs Board (MTA) and the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), which combats money laundering.

World.title: Over 100 graves vandalized at Saaremaa cemetery
World.content:
More than 100 graves were found to have been damaged on Monday in a major act of vandalism at Kihelkonna cemetery on the island of Saaremaa.

Police have opened criminal proceedings into the vandalism and are seeking information about the perpetrators.

Margus Saar, who has worked as a cemetery caretaker for 21 years, was the first person to find the broken graves.

"The police have now established that 105 graves were damaged. Tombstones have been broken – knocked over and then shattered. Expensive granite grave lanterns have had their glass smashed, and flowers have also been damaged. I tend to think it happened on Sunday and that young people were responsible. That's what the footprints suggest," Saar said.

The Saaremaa municipal administration, which manages the municipality's cemeteries, will start to clean up the damage on Wednesday.

"The police have now initiated criminal proceedings under the section of the Penal Code concerning desecration of the memory of the deceased. The punishment for this is a fine or imprisonment. If minors are involved, the type of punishment remains exactly the same. This is the first time vandalism on such a scale has occurred here," said Minna Raun, regional group leader at Kuressaare police station.

World.title: Another poll shows Center more popular than Isamaa
World.content:
A third survey monitoring the popularity of Estonia's political parties shows the opposition Center Party has overtaken the opposition Isamaa Party for the first time since 2023.

Earlier this month, the same results were reflected in polls by Emor and Turu-uuringud, and the latest data from Norstat and the Ühiskonnauuringute Instituut confirm the change. Center's four-week average support has risen to 23.1 percent, while Isamaa's has fallen to 22.8 percent.

Center has risen to the top of the party ratings table, with its support increasing by 1.4 percentage points over the week and now standing at its highest level since August 2020.

Support for Isamaa fell by 1.2 percentage points over the week. This is the first time the party has lost the top spot since November 2023.

Support for the Social Democratic Party (SDE) has increased by 1.8 percentage points over the past four weeks to 16.5 percent, reaching its highest level since September 2024.

The top three are followed by EKRE (13.8 percent), Reform (12.3 percent) and Parempoolsed (6.4 percent).

Party ratings from Nortstat/ÜI: October 3-25, 2026. Source: Nortstat/ÜI

Support for coalition party Reform remains on a slight downward trend, with a fall of 1.7 percentage points over the past five weeks.

Support for the junior coalition partner Eesti 200 stood at 1.4 percent.

The Greens, ERK and Koos all polled below 1 percent.

The coalition parties were supported by a total of 13.7 percent of respondents, while the Riigikogu opposition parties were supported by 76.2 percent.

Based on calculations by political scientist Martin Mölder the Center Party would win 26 seats in the Riigikogu, Isamaa 25, SDE 18, EKRE 14, the Reform Party 12 and Parempoolsed six.

The latest aggregate results cover the polling period from September 28 to October 25, during which a total of 4,000 Estonian citizens of voting age were surveyed.

World.title: Karmen Turk: Why Estonia's gambling license is not attracting foreign operators
World.content:
Estonia has strengthened its regulations through economic and money laundering crises, but along with the rules, the procedural environment has also changed, no longer conforming to good practice but instead deterring international companies, attorney-at-law Karmen Turk writes.

No one is disputing that a gambling operator is required to combat money laundering. The law requires it. The question lies elsewhere: do Estonia's rules prevent money laundering, or do they primarily act as a barrier to new companies coming to Estonia? Unfortunately, experience over the past year points more towards the latter.

The recently amended Remote Gambling Tax Act has brought into focus international opportunities for financing Estonia's state budget and, in particular, sport and culture. The environment here could be attractive given the purpose of an Estonian license is simple: to bring tax revenue earned elsewhere into digitally advanced Estonia. International remote gambling operators will not be targeting Estonian players. Their customers are in other countries, around the world. An Estonian license, however, means that taxes on their activities are paid into Estonia and go towards financing our sports and culture. Every license brought into Estonia is thus a victory for Estonian culture and sports, yet without increasing gambling in Estonia. To achieve this goal, however, companies need to actually come to Estonia. But what is deterring companies today? The simple answer is: fear-driven regulation that diminishes the legal opportunities created in Estonia, because every applicant is treated primarily as a potential risk.

To explain in more detail, a gambling operating license is issued by the Tax and Customs Board (MTA), but it must first be approved by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU). The applicant must submit their internal anti-money laundering regulations, appoint a person who will communicate with the FIU (the so-called contact person), and submit documents concerning its owners and managers. Companies already operating must meet these requirements by January 1, 2027, at the latest. Gambling operators are now essentially treated in the same way as financial companies and cryptocurrency firms are. The purpose of stricter rules is understandable. The problem lies in how they get applied in practice.

The contact person must work in Estonia

Under current law, the contact person must be working on a permanent basis in Estonia. The FIU's training materials even state that "the entire department should be located in Estonia." In addition, the contact person must have suitable education, experience and an impeccable reputation, while the FIU must approve their appointment.

What does our regulation mean for an international company? Usually, the people responsible for its anti-money laundering controls work in the same location as its IT and payments teams would do, for example in Latvia, Italy or Malta. In order to obtain an Estonian license, however, it must find someone who works in Estonia, understands the risks of the gambling sector and passes the FIU's checks. The FIU has also indicated that one person may serve as a contact person for no more than two companies, and must have a replacement during vacation periods. In reality, consequently, one contact person is not sufficient; two experts meeting the same criteria are needed – but this is an over-regulation of the requirements. Estonia is small and there are few such specialists. This is as a result not merely a formality, but a real barrier to market entry.

Where the contact person sits says nothing about the quality of their work. The FIU's own updated guidelines do not mention location either. They require the contact person to report directly to the management board, to be competent and to have access to all the necessary information at all times. Even an entire department can serve as the contact person. None of these conditions depends on the country. On the contrary, actual knowledge and control are more effective when they are "close" to the operations themselves. According to the FIU's own data, the sector's real weakness is also the detection of suspicious transactions. In 2025, only about 14 percent of reports were related to genuine suspicions, while nearly 94 percent of all reports came from only about a tenth of all companies. This problem is solved by a good monitoring system and a skilled team, not by whether the contact person sits in Tallinn or in Rome. If a company's international team is stronger than an individual specialist who can be found in Estonia, the Estonian requirement may n fact weaken controls. This also raises a question of EU law. Companies with Estonian licenses often belong to groups managed in other EU countries and mainly serve foreign customers. The EU guarantees companies the right to operate and provide services in other member states. The European Court of Justice has allowed countries to restrict gambling, but only if the restriction has good grounds, genuinely helps achieve its objective, is applied consistently and does not go further than necessary. Estonia's location requirement is questionable in light of the last two conditions. First, it is not consistent: according to the FIU's guidelines, customers from other EU countries are considered lower risk, but a specialist working in another EU country is considered a risk. Second, less restrictive solutions exist. It would be sufficient for the contact person to be available at all times, communicate with the FIU in Estonian and ensure that the FIU has access to the data. In addition, a uniform EU anti-money laundering regulation will take effect on July 10, 2027. It is therefore appropriate to ask whether Estonia's additional requirements, which the EU does not demand, are even still necessary.

Documents must be in Estonian

The second obstacle is the language requirement. According to the experiences of companies, the FIU requires internal rules and other documents be in Estonian. It is natural that communication with the authority would take place in Estonian. However, an international company's internal rules are an everyday working tool. They are used by employees in various countries and so get written in a language that everyone understands. If a separate Estonian-language version has to be prepared for Estonia, two documents are created: one that is actually used at work and another that is shown to the authority. This contradicts the FIU's own objective, however. The FIU will check exactly whether the rules are actually being used or exist only on paper. The updated guidelines state that the rules must be understandable to employees and describe what the company actually does. In the case of customer documents, the guidelines themselves recommend avoiding translation if the original is in a comprehensible language, such as English. There is no requirement in the guidelines for internal rules to be in Estonian. The obligation to translate does nothing to help combat money laundering.

A procedure whose duration and outcome are unknown

In 2024, the Chancellor of Justice examined the FIU's licensing procedures and identified several problems. First, the FIU does not tell applicants when all their documents are in order. As a result, applicants do not know when the statutory 60-day deadline for making a decision starts. Second, in the course of an interview, an applicant may be advised to replace the contact person, an owner or a management board member, or to withdraw the application, but these interviews are not logged in the minutes. Based on the experiences of several companies from 2026, these interviews have gone on for hours, with three to four officials questioning one person all at the same time. For a company planning investments in Estonia, uncertainty of this kind is the worst possible signal. An official refusal can be challenged in court. However, if the outcome of the procedure depends on interviews that are not recorded in minutes, the company will simply choose another country where the procedure is clear and predictable.

Rules must be based on actual risks

The state fully knows what the sector's risks are. According to the national risk assessment, the money laundering risk posed by gambling operators is high because Estonian licenses are used mainly to serve foreign customers and business partners are often located abroad. The FIU focuses on the origin of funds, the use of front persons, the splitting of transactions and cryptocurrency. These are the right issues. But having the contact person live in Estonia or the rules written in Estonian does nothing to counter these risks. What is needed is good transaction monitoring, rapid information exchange and access to data for the FIU. The latter is already guaranteed by law, even when the server is located abroad.

The law itself requires proportionality: the extent of controls must correspond to the risk and be reasonable. The same should apply to the state when it decides what to require of a new market entrant. Penalties are already severe: a fine of up to €1 million can be imposed for violating the requirements for internal rules.

Estonia does not have to choose between strict anti-money laundering controls and an attractive license in order to regulate the market and generate tax revenue. But the success of controls must be measured by whether they stop suspicious money flows. Neither an office address in Tallinn nor the language of the documentation demonstrates this.

The author of this piece advises international gambling operators.

World.title: Almost 400 migrants detained in Estonia since July
World.content:
Since July, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) has detained 388 foreign nationals who arrived in Estonia without a legal basis after crossing the Belarusian border. Detentions in recent weeks have taken place exclusively in Tallinn.

As of Tuesday, 258 foreign nationals were being held at the detention center in Tallinn, while 148 people who entered the European Union via the Belarus-Latvia border have been handed over to Latvia.

"Each handover is essentially a logistical operation, the success of which requires verified information about the foreign nationals' routes, origins and intentions, as well as agreements between the authorities of both countries," said Indrek Aru, head of the border guard bureau at the PPA's Northern Prefecture.

Foreign nationals are transported back in groups.

Fifteen people are suspected of organizing illegal migration.

Medical attention

Detainees at the detention center have also sought medical attention due to health problems, including cold-like symptoms and skin rashes.

"Foreign nationals with high fevers were taken to West Tallinn Central Hospital, which provides healthcare services to the detention center. As of today, one foreign national remains hospitalized, and it is known that they will be able to return to the detention center in the coming days," Aru noted.

The hospital does not provide the detention center with detailed information about tests carried out or diagnoses.

"Due to personal data protection requirements, diagnoses are not disclosed to the detention center, but in the event of a health risk, the center's staff receive all the necessary information from medical professionals to immediately implement measures to limit the spread of disease, including isolation or quarantine," Aru said.

World.title: Tallinn mulling 1+1 and 2+1 lane options for Tulika tänav renovation
World.content:
Preliminary designs have been released for the renovation of Tulika tänav and the section of Paldiski maantee that intersects with it in Tallinn's Kristiine district, and the street will be rebuilt with either 1+1 or 2+1 traffic lanes.

Ahead of the renovation of Tulika tänav, which connects the Kristiine traffic junction and the Sõle intersection, Tallinn is considering two options: rebuilding the street with either 1+1 or 2+1 traffic lanes.

Both solutions will include new sidewalks, cycle paths and street greenery. A traffic study has been carried out to find a suitable solution, and the final choice will be made after assessing spatial possibilities and the needs of different modes of transport.

Tallinn Deputy Mayor Kristjan Järvan (Isamaa) said that he and Tallinn Deputy Mayor Joel Jesse (Center) prefer the 2+1 option.

"Our clear view is that this location cannot accommodate a 1+1 solution, and our firm preference is 1+2," he noted.

However, no decision has yet been made. "When making the final decision, we will naturally take residents' feedback into account," Järvan said.

The reconstruction will also include the renovation of water supply and sewerage facilities, the construction of a separate stormwater drainage system and improvements to street lighting.

Feedback on both options can be submitted until November 10.

World.title: Trump tamed after US midterms? Europe doubts it
World.content:
Brussels – President Donald Trump may be facing a political pounding at the US midterm elections next month — but in Europe expectations are low that a big Democrat win would change much.

From the battlefields of Ukraine to the boardrooms of Europe, Trump has sent multiple shockwaves across the continent since returning to power last year.

During a head-spinning 22 months, the mercurial leader has turned spectacularly on Kyiv, imposed tariffs on allies and threatened to take Greenland.

Ahead of the November 3 polls it looks like American voters could punish Trump’s Republican party and hand control of one or both of the US House of Representatives or Senate to the Democrats.

But while the hope may be that Trump could be reined in by a hostile Congress, multiple officials at the EU and NATO told AFP they doubt a big loss would muzzle him on the international stage.

“We don’t think the unpredictability is going to change,” said one senior EU diplomat.

Publicly the European Union is keeping its cards close to its chest.

“We will not comment on any elections in the EU or abroad. Let’s wait for those and we’ll see where it goes,” said European Commission spokeswoman Paula Pinho.

Behind closed doors as well, officials say that the midterms are not featuring much in the bloc’s internal discussions.

“I suspect because a) it is difficult to really predict the result, b) one wouldn’t want to get too high hopes for change and c) not sure how much even a Democratic wave would impact foreign policy issues,” said a second senior EU diplomat.

– Ukraine, tariffs –

Ahead of the midterms, Trump has rattled Europe by yet again lashing out at Ukraine and cosying up to Russia as Washington has renewed its push to end the fighting.

While a Democrat win could usher in a more vocal pro-Kyiv majority in Congress, the EU is not expecting US support for Ukraine to ramp up again.

Officials in Brussels say they are focused on plugging a 70-billion-euro hole in Kyiv’s finances next year.

And while they’re pushing other countries like Britain, Canada and Japan to do more, they are certainly not counting on the United States.

Meanwhile, there is equally little optimism for any major reversal on the tariffs Trump has slapped on Europe.

Diplomats and officials point out that it took months to get Democrat President Joe Biden to roll back tariffs on EU steel after Trump’s first term — and even then limitations remained.

In a recent poll from the Washington-based Council on Foreign Relations, only one quarter of Americans backed removing all the tariffs on the EU.

– US forces in Europe? –

At NATO the story is much the same.

European allies are nervously waiting for the results of a Pentagon review of US forces on the continent that looks set to be unveiled in December.

The widespread expectation is that it will see the United States scale back its deployments, although the hope is the cuts will not be too severe.

Multiple diplomats at NATO said they didn’t envision the midterms having an impact on the review.

While a changed Congress could see US lawmakers more outspoken in support of the alliance, the direction of travel is already set with Europe stepping up efforts to take more responsibility for its defence.

“Whatever the outcome, we’ll keep going,” said one European diplomat.

– Trump unleashed? –

There is also a nagging fear that things could get worse after the midterms.

If Republicans cling on it could embolden Trump, meanwhile if they lose, he could seek to distract from his woes at home by stirring up things abroad.

“We have a history in America of presidents who get in trouble domestically turning more to the international stage,” said Bruce Stokes, a visiting fellow at the German Marshall Fund think tank.

From an escalation in the Iran war to a more concerted push on Ukraine, there are numerous ways the White House can keep worrying Europe.

“Trump has demonstrated they can’t stand not to be the centre of attention,” said Stokes.

“If that means he needs to do more on the world stage, positively or negatively, that may be what ends up happening.”

World.title: Anthropic’s record IPO faces some big questions
World.content:
San Francisco – No startup has ever grown so fast. In five years, Anthropic has become an AI giant valued at $1 trillion, and it is now aiming for a record-breaking stock market debut.

But it faces three threats: rivals that are catching up, prices that are collapsing, and bills that keep climbing.

Anthropic spells out the risks in its Wall Street prospectus, published Monday.

The first is commoditization: “the degree of differentiation among advanced AI models may narrow,” the company warns.

The San Francisco-based firm also says “substantially all of our revenue” comes from its AI tools. Unlike Google or Meta, it has no advertising empire to fall back on if business takes a hit, and no cloud business like Microsoft’s or SpaceX’s.

Investors have already grown nervous. In mid-August, shareholders were floating a valuation of $2 trillion.

But quarter-on-quarter growth slowed from 145 percent in the second quarter to 45 percent in the third, cooling expectations to around $1.5 trillion.

– Cheap and open –

So-called open AI models, which anyone can download and modify, are close behind closed models such as Claude or ChatGPT, which are available only through their owners’ paid services.

The performance of open models trails by only about four months on average, according to research institute Epoch AI.

They include Kimi K3.1 Pro from Chinese company Moonshot, which costs half as much as Claude Opus 5.5, Anthropic’s current flagship.

And among paid models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google, none has stayed on top for long.

Anthropic also acknowledges it is holding itself back: its safety measures “could slow our capability gains relative to competitors that do not adopt similar constraints.”

Still, the company says each new version of Claude has boosted sales. More than 80 percent of its revenue last quarter came from models less than six months old.

– Prices collapsing –

When products look alike, prices fall. According to Morningstar, the price of having AI process the same amount of text, at the same level of performance, has dropped 97 percent, from $17 at the end of 2024 to 50 cents today.

Anthropic itself cut the price of Claude Opus by 20 percent in September, and OpenAI cut the price of one of its flagship models by a factor of five in July.

The effect is already visible at Vercel, a developer platform that routes requests across AI models.

In August, more than half of the text it handled was processed by open models, up from 13 percent in April.

Even so, Anthropic still captured nearly two-thirds of spending on the platform.

Even a 90 percent price cut would not shrink total spending on AI as long as usage keeps growing at its current pace, said Malik Ahmed Khan, a senior equity analyst at Morningstar.

– ‘Triple whammy’ –

Anthropic’s costs, by contrast, are largely locked in. To stay ahead, each new Claude model has to be bigger than the last, trained on more data using more computing power.

Since late 2025, the company has committed to paying at least $417 billion to rent chips and servers.

That is nearly 13 years of sales at its first-half 2026 pace, and the total could nearly double if cancellable or planned contracts are included.

These commitments are due no matter the state of its business, Anthropic warns.

The bet involves the entire industry: Google and Amazon are at once Anthropic’s shareholders, its suppliers and its resellers.

If AI turns out to be less profitable than expected, the International Monetary Fund fears a “triple whammy” from these intertwined investments: falling stock prices, debts that are harder to repay, and promised revenue that never materializes.

The independent research firm New Constructs called the listing “an unprecedented test of investor gullibility.”

To pay these bills, Anthropic is counting on money from the stock market, which is not unlimited.

SpaceX, Elon Musk’s rocket and AI company, raised record sums there in June, while Google and Meta, which are pouring fortunes into data centers, are also seeking fresh capital.

OpenAI, whose chief Sam Altman called a listing “ill-advised” this year, has chosen to wait until 2027, giving it time to see how Wall Street treats its big rival.

World.title: Tech stocks soar as SK hynix adds to rising AI confidence
World.content:
Hong Kong – Technology firms surged across Asia on Wednesday after blockbuster earnings from chip giant SK hynix helped boost optimism in the AI trade ahead of results from Wall Street titans Microsoft and Alphabet.

Oil prices rose as investors kept tabs on Israel’s election results, which could determine the future of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s war against Iran.

After a slight wobble this month in the tech realm caused by fresh worries about huge investment spending, profitability and company finances, AI-linked firms were back on the front foot.

SK hynix, which has been at the forefront of the chip boom, said Wednesday that third-quarter operating profit soared 632 percent to US$62.8 billion thanks to explosive demand for its advanced semiconductors.

The firm said it had now posted record revenue and operating profit for six straight quarters.

“While Wall Street argues over whether the AI arms race can keep financing itself, SK hynix has just reminded the market that somebody on the other side of all that capex is receiving the cheque,” wrote Stephen Innes at SPI Asset Management.

The reading added to optimism surrounding the sector after Anthropic, the mother company for Claude AI, said Monday in its IPO filing that first-half revenue surged about 1,300 percent and flagged heavy capital spending ahead.

That was followed Tuesday by Broadcom’s announcing jointly with Citi, Blackstone and Morgan Stanley a US$63 billion financing structure to build new capacity for Anthropic.

“The AI trade has undoubtedly received a healthy shot in the arm from Anthropic’s… filing, with its incredible revenue growth, improving compute economics and substantial commitments to future infrastructure investment reinforcing the longer-term opportunity across the AI supply chain,” said Pepperstone’s Chris Weston.

Shares in SK hynix soared almost nine percent Wednesday and South Korean rival Samsung, which reports Thursday, added more than eight percent. That pushed Seoul’s Kospi index up more than six percent.

Japan’s Nikkei 225 climbed more than one percent, with chipmaker Kioxia soaring more than 10 percent, while Advantest gained three percent and Tokyo Electron four percent.

Taipei was pulled sharply higher thanks to chipmaker TSMC’s strong performance, while Hong Kong, Shanghai, Sydney, Singapore and Wellington were also well up.

The gains tracked advances in New York, where the Nasdaq added more than one percent.

Microsoft and Alphabet are due to report later in the day, while Amazon, Apple and Intel follow on Thursday.

However, traders are also awaiting the Federal Reserve’s policy decision Wednesday.

While it is expected to stand pat after last month’s hike, its post-meeting statement and comments from boss Kevin Warsh will be pored over for clues about its future plans. Markets expect a hike in December.

Crude prices jumped more than one percent as results from Israel’s general election rolled in.

While polls appeared to show Netanyahu’s governing Likud and the opposition neck and neck, the prime minister vowed to form a new coalition, adding that he could work with US President Donald Trump to eliminate the “existential threat” posed by Iran.

His comments came after opposition candidate Gadi Eisenkot said the country had chosen change and that he would seek to form a new administration.

World.title: Billionaire Ambani’s Jio to debut after record India IPO
World.content:
Mumbai – India’s Jio Platforms makes its stock market debut on Wednesday after a record-breaking IPO, capping billionaire owner Mukesh Ambani’s years-long drive to diversify his conglomerate beyond oil refining.

Jio Platforms, which houses the country’s biggest wireless operator and is the digital services arm of Ambani’s Reliance Industries, raised about $3.2 billion at 1,119 rupees ($11.76) per share in India’s biggest-ever initial public offering.

The listing, one of the year’s most anticipated, attracted robust demand last week, with investors applying for more than 22 times the shares on offer.

In the run-up to its Mumbai debut, grey market platforms showed a premium of around 22 percent for Jio shares, although experts caution that such unofficial indicators can be unreliable predictors of early trading.

Nevertheless, most analysts expect decent listing gains despite a weak year for Indian equities.

Jio has a “proven execution record” and will see its cash generation “strengthening as the 5G investment cycle winds down”, analysts at financial services firm Emkay Global said in a note, calling the company “the digital engine of India”.

Launched a decade ago, Jio’s wireless service disrupted the market with steep discounts, rapidly winning customers from rivals Bharti Airtel and Vodafone.

With over 530 million subscribers, the firm currently makes most of its money from telecoms, but has expanded in recent years into digital services and artificial intelligence.

Experts say Jio is key to Reliance’s strategy to move beyond oil and underpins its future technology ambitions.

Local media have reported how it is considering a low Earth orbit satellite constellation to provide internet services from space — a venture that would see it compete with Musk’s Starlink, which has been trying for years to launch in India.

Musk accused unnamed Indian “oligarchs” this month of preventing Starlink’s rollout in the country, and referred to the Reliance chairman as “Prime Minister Ambani” and the “real boss of India”.

Reliance responded by noting that it had never “feared competition” and welcomed offerings from rivals in satellite communications, including Starlink.

World.title: US Fed expected to hold rates steady ahead of key midterm elections
World.content:
Washington – The US Federal Reserve will announce a decision on setting interest rates on Wednesday, with markets expecting the central bank to hold steady days ahead of crucial midterm elections, despite surging inflation.

The Fed will announce the decision of the 12 voting members of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) at 2:00 pm local time (1800 GMT) on Wednesday, with a press conference by Chairman Kevin Warsh to follow.

Policymakers voted at their last meeting in September to raise interest rates to a range between 3.75 and 4.00 percent — the first hike in three years — to tackle inflation.

The Fed has missed its long-term two-percent target for inflation for more than five years, with households and businesses battered by sustained price increases.

US President Donald Trump’s war on Iran, launched in late February, has sent energy prices skyrocketing and fueled domestic inflation, alongside his wide-ranging tariff policies.

Prices have also been driven by an investment boom in artificial intelligence (AI) technology and the build-out of huge data centers to support it.

The Fed’s decision comes six days ahead of the November 3 midterm elections, in which the Democratic Party seeks to wrest control of both houses of Congress from Trump’s Republicans.

Trump’s handling of the economy has been a key issue throughout the campaign, with working-class households across the country struggling to make ends meet despite largely stable overall economic growth.

US consumer inflation came in hotter than expected in September, clocking in at 3.7 percent, edging back towards a three-year high established in May.

Still, key policymakers at the Fed — including Chair Warsh — have signaled that they did not see an urgency to raise rates again immediately.

Speaking in Bangkok earlier this month, Warsh said that US economic conditions had “broadly conformed” to policymakers’ expectations, fueling speculation that the Fed may pause at the October meeting.

Wendy Edelberg, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, told AFP that all the signs pointed to a hold.

“I would be very surprised if they raised interest rates just for starters so close to the election, but also given that so many of them have signaled that they’re happy for a pause,” she said.

– ‘Don’t understand the logic’ –

For Edelberg, however, a decision to hold after raising rates in September would potentially be contradictory, given the labor market — the Fed’s other mandate — has been largely stable.

“In terms of the economics of it, I don’t totally understand the logic,” she said.

“If there was a reason to raise interest rates at the last meeting, I think that there’s just as compelling of an economic reason to raise interest rates at this meeting.”

The Fed has a dual mandate to maintain maximum employment while keeping inflation to its long-term target.

It achieves this goal largely using one tool: the economy’s key interest rate. Raising rates tends to cool inflation but can also dampen economic activity; lowering them can spur economic activity but also fuel inflation.

The US unemployment rate has been largely stable around 4.2 percent over the last year, with job growth mostly in positive territory — albeit driven by a few sectors.

Loretta Mester, former head of the Cleveland Fed, agreed that current economic conditions gave policymakers an opportunity to press ahead with rate hikes now.

“Take advantage of the situation you’re in today, which is pretty clear evidence of stability in the labor market, and clear evidence that inflation is still too high,” she said.

“Move, given that you know you want to be moving more, take the advantage of this meeting.”

Mester, who took part in FOMC meetings during her tenure at the Fed, insisted that the committee did not “take into account any kind of political issues” when it debated monetary policy.

– Attacks on Fed –

Still, Trump has loomed large over the Fed since he returned to power last year.

In his second term, he has led an unprecedented assault on the Fed’s independence, pursuing criminal charges against Warsh’s predecessor Jay Powell and attempting to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook as he demanded lower interest rates.

While the probe against Powell was dropped to smooth the way for Warsh’s Senate confirmation, the White House has recently renewed its drive to fire Cook — despite a Supreme Court decision that batted back an earlier attempt.

“I don’t think it’s going to stop because I think it’s in the nature of this administration to continue those attacks,” said Mester.

World.title: Meta, Snap head to trial in another case about social media’s harms
World.content:
San Francisco – Jury selection is expected to begin on Wednesday in Los Angeles for another landmark trial about the alleged harms of social media on young users, with Meta and, for the first time, Snap as defendants.

Thousands of lawsuits have been filed in recent years in local, state and federal courtrooms across the country with various claims about alleged harms to children and teenagers caused by social media companies.

The cases — the first of which went to trial earlier this year in Los Angeles — have taken twists and turns.

Meta and YouTube lost the first so-called bellwether case earlier this year, when a jury found them collectively liable for harming a young user known by the initials KGM, and ordered the tech companies to pay a combined $6 million penalty.

Meta said at the time that they “respectfully disagree” with the verdict.

Snap and TikTok settled with KGM ahead of that trial.

Months later, Snap, TikTok and YouTube settled another case that was set to go to trial in August; that plaintiff, known as RKC, then withdrew their remaining claims against Meta, allowing the Instagram and Facebook maker to avoid trial without a settlement.

TikTok and YouTube were previously named as defendants in the new case but both companies reached settlement agreements with the plaintiffs, known by their initials SJ and KDB, before the start of the trial, their lawyers said.

Meta reached a settlement agreement with one of the plaintiffs, SJ, but not KDB, according to their lawyers.

A California state judge consolidated both cases into a single trial.

If no additional settlements are reached before opening statements kick off on November 4, the new trial will move forward with both Meta and Snap as defendants.

Star witnesses are expected to testify beginning mid-November including Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Instagram chief Adam Mosseri, and Snap CEO Evan Spiegel.

Earlier this month, a New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in a case where the company was found liable for deceiving users in the state about how their data was used in a case related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

A New Mexico jury previously found the social media giant liable for harms to children, leading to a combined penalty of $942 million.

In August, Meta agreed to pay more than $18 billion in penalties, in addition to making changes to Instagram and Facebook for teens, when it settled with 52 attorneys general several days into a trial held in California.

Part of that settlement hinged on YouTube and TikTok making similar changes to their own products, such as limiting daily screentime.

– ‘Addictive and problematic’ –

As regulators around the world grapple with reining in, or even banning, social media use for teens, American lawsuits have focused on allegations of addictive design and deceptive practices by social media companies.

Next month, lawyers for the two plaintiffs in Los Angeles — SJ and KDB — will argue that their clients were exposed to “addictive and problematic” social media apps when they started using them at 13 and 15, respectively, according to court documents.

SJ, a teen in Illinois, began to use Snapchat, the app created by Snap, compulsively and subsequently experienced mental health issues, an eating disorder and self harm, her lawyers claim.

KDB, now an 18-years-old from Mississippi, similarly developed compulsive use of both Meta and Snap, leading to worsening mental and physical health, according to her lawyers.

Meta has previously denied such claims.

“We will not back away from defending ourselves against baseless lawsuits,” Meta told AFP in July.

Snap intends to argue that it is different from other apps like Meta’s Instagram and Facebook because of Snapchat’s focus on primarily being a messaging platform.

“We believe the evidence will support that we have put our community first, and that these allegations fundamentally misrepresent the plaintiffs’ experiences on Snapchat and how our platform was designed,” a Snap spokesperson said in a statement.

World.title: Palestinian protest leader says movement reshaping US politics
World.content:
New York – Mahmoud Khalil, who became the face of resistance to President Donald Trump’s crackdown on pro-Palestinian student activism, believes the movement has succeeded by shifting public perception and encouraging a generation of leaders ready to question views about Israel.

“The American public is finally changing, is finally looking at the Palestinian as an equal human,” the 31-year-old said in an interview with AFP one week before crucial midterm elections — and just as Israel held its own election.

Khalil rose to prominence when he helped lead demonstrations at New York’s Columbia University, the epicenter of protests against the war in Gaza that swept US campuses in 2024.

At the height of Trump’s crackdown, immigration authorities responded by detaining Khalil — a permanent US resident born in a Palestinian refugee camp in Syria — for three months without criminal charge, making him miss the birth of his first child.

But despite the personal toll — recounted in his memoir “No Land to Stand On: Notes from Detention” — Khalil credited Palestinian advocacy with helping to transform public opinion in the United States, where polls show historic growth in support for Palestinians.

“This gives me hope,” he said in his New York apartment.

“Also, we can see on the ground that we have more progressive candidates being elected into Congress and positions of power.”

Khalil pointed to Abdul El-Sayed, a Muslim running for US Senate in the key state of Michigan, as well as pro-Palestinian New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who was elected last year.

Both men are also notably critics of Israel — a move away from the traditional defense of the US ally among both Republicans and Democrats.

– ‘Work not done yet’ –

Khalil said that Trump sought to “chill” free speech on Palestinian rights with his arrest — which the president celebrated in a social media post, saying it was the first of many to come.

“The Trump administration tried to dehumanize me for my advocacy for Palestine, for my opposition to the genocide in Gaza,” he said.

“It was clear to me that this administration just wanted to make an example out of me, so people wouldn’t speak out for Palestine.”

The Trump administration says it is fighting anti-Semitism and illegal immigration, using both arguments to justify everything from controversial detentions of activists to defunding elite universities where pro-Palestinian protests took place.

Khalil said that strategy backfired.

“The fact that the president of the United States came after me, a random student, means that I was doing something right,” he added.

– ‘Such cruelty’ –

Khalil’s ordeal also exposed him to conditions in a Louisiana jail he likened to torture, describing constant fluorescent light, cold, and poor food.

“I never imagined that such cruelty is happening on US soil,” Khalil said of the deportation drive led by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

“I came to a country that supposedly champions liberty, justice, rule of law, only to be shocked when I entered these detention centers that all my rights were left outside,” he said.

Khalil has been free for well over a year but the Trump administration is still pushing for his deportation even as he raises his son, now aged 18 months, in New York with his wife.

It’s an emotional cost that is hard to bear.

“A big part of my fight is like fighting for normalcy,” he said. “To go back to being the young father who would go to the park with his son and wife, and no one would bother them.”

But Khalil is also defiant.

“My fight is not only about whether I get to stay in this country. It is about whether you know people in this country can speak their minds.

“Whether I am in or outside the United States, I’m committed to advocate for the rights of the Palestinian people,” he said.

World.title: Palestinian activist Khalil returns to Columbia after US detention
World.content:
New York – Mahmoud Khalil, a figurehead of Gaza war protests in the United States, returned Tuesday to Columbia University for the first time since his 2025 arrest under President Donald Trump’s crackdown on pro-Palestinian activists.

The 31-year-old told AFP his presence for an event on his new memoir, attended by around 100 people, was a “victory,” as he accused Columbia of seeking “to erase me, to erase any Palestinian voices on campus.”

He has slammed the Ivy League institution for its response to the 2024 student demonstrations, which included allowing New York police to clear protesters from its Manhattan campus in a heavy-handed operation.

Columbia said at the time the protests were a safety threat.

Khalil has also accused the university of failing to protect him from harassment ahead of his arrest by US immigration authorities and three-month detention without criminal charge, before his release in June 2025.

“Columbia could have been an example for how to have difficult conversations on campus, how to respond to such a protest, how to be aligned with human rights and with international law,” Khalil told AFP in an interview.

“They chose the total opposite. They chose brutality. They chose repression,” he said.

Some Jewish groups on social media had opposed Khalil’s return. A spokesperson for Columbia said the college is “committed to rigorous debate, inquiry, and respectful dialogue across differing perspectives.”

“Columbia supports the right of faculty members to organize academic events. An invitation to speak does not signify university endorsement of a speaker’s views,” they said in a statement carried by US media.

World.title: 'We don't want a fight': Delhi traders' body writes to Rahul Gandhi again over November 1 rally
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A Delhi traders' body on Wednesday wrote another letter to Congress leader

, urging him to postpone the INDIA bloc's November 1 rally at Ramlila Maidan until after Diwali over fears that the gathering could disrupt business in several major markets.

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI), which has raised concerns about the rally's impact on festive sales, also sought a 20-minute meeting with Gandhi to explain why traders want the event deferred.

In the letter, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal said representatives of 20 markets wanted an opportunity to put forward their concerns about the rally, which is expected to draw around 10 lakh people.

"We don't want a fight; we want dialogue. Rahul ji himself says that he listens to everyone, listens to the voice of small traders.

So, we traders from 20 markets are asking him for 20 minutes. This will be the beauty of democracy," Goyal said.

The traders' body also proposed that it would withdraw its protest if Gandhi could convince its representatives that the rally would bring more customers and boost business. However, if traders were able to convince him that the event would result in losses, they wanted him to agree to postpone it until after Diwali.





Wednesday's letter was the second sent by CTI to Gandhi within four days. The organisation had first approached the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha on October 24, seeking postponement of the rally to prevent disruptions during one of the busiest periods for Delhi's markets.

According to CTI, at least 20 markets within a 1-5 km radius of Ramlila Maidan could be affected by the expected turnout.

The markets include Chandni Chowk, Bhagirath Palace, Khari Baoli, Sadar Bazar, Chawri Bazar, Kashmere Gate, Nabi Karim, Karol Bagh, Ajmeri Gate and Daryaganj.

Nai Sarak, Kinari Bazar, Dariba Kalan, Fatehpuri, Naya Bazar, Filmistan, Paharganj, Gaffar Market, Jama Masjid-Meena Bazar and Lajpat Rai Market are also among the commercial areas identified by the traders' body.

The concerns come as the INDIA bloc prepares for a major show of strength in the national capital over alleged "vote chori" and irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

World.title: ‘BJP wins through foul means’: Akhilesh alleges MLC poll fraud, warns of 2027 defeat
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party supremo

on Wednesday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of electoral malpractice in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council (MLC) elections, alleging that irregularities during counting were part of a conspiracy to defeat SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi.

In a post on X, Akhilesh alleged that BJP leaders, their associates and officials had colluded to manipulate the counting process. He claimed that the alleged treatment of Tripathi had angered teachers and members of his community, and vowed that the SP would fight "injustice and harassment."

"The corrupt BJP leaders, their conspiratorial associates and complicit officials have stooped to every possible low to win the MLC elections.

The conspiracy to defeat Dr Sanjayan Tripathi has been exposed before everyone. The reason for defeating Dr Sanjayan Tripathi through vote-counting irregularities is not merely that he is an SP candidate; the main reason behind it is âHaata nahi bhaataâ (he is not acceptable to them).

In matters of politics, the BJP has sunk to the lowest depths. After such massive fraud, the public has realised that the BJP has, in fact, lost every seat," he wrote.





"BJP leaders win not through votes, but through foul means," former UP CM added.

Targeting the BJP over its alleged treatment of teachers, the SP chief said the incident had left a deep impression on Tripathi's community and teachers across the state.

âThe way Sanjayan Tripathi has been harassed is being witnessed by his entire community. Neither his community nor any teacher in the state will forget Dr. Tripathi's tears,â the SP chief said, alleging that teachers had received nothing but humiliation from the BJP government.

Akhilesh also linked the controversy to the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections, claiming that teachers would remember the alleged mistreatment when they vote.

âEvery teacher will always remember the despicable conspiracy to make teachers do the unwanted task of collecting fodder, and will fulfil their âguru resolveâ by defeating the BJP in the 2027 assembly elections,â he wrote.

Taking another swipe at the ruling party, Akhilesh said its alleged electoral tactics would not succeed across the state.

"The BJP's â400 BCâ (a pun on char sau beesi, meaning fraud or deceit) will not work across all 403 seats," he further said.

Reiterating his support for Tripathi, the SP chief added, "We stand with Sanjayan Tripathi and against every injustice and act of harassment inflicted upon him and his community. We stand united against the BJP and will continue to do so."

SP candidates allege irregularities in MLC counting

The remarks came amid allegations of irregularities during the counting of votes for the Gorakhpur-Faizabad Division Teachers' constituency.

SP candidate Sanjayan Tripathi and independent candidate Rajeev Yadav boycotted the counting process, accusing administrative officials and the election observer of favouring the BJP candidate.

Speaking to news agency ANI, Tripathi alleged that the counting trend changed abruptly after the first three rounds, when independent candidate Rajeev Yadav was leading by around 450 votes.

âWe have boycotted the vote-counting process. Everything was proceeding smoothly for the first three rounds of counting; independent candidate Rajiv Yadav was leading by approximately 450 votes.

Suddenly, the counting began to shift entirely in favour of the BJP candidate; the trend changed abruptly, making it appear as though the outcome had been predetermined. Consequently, we decided to boycott the process,â Tripathi said.

He also alleged police misconduct and claimed that the authorities were determined to ensure the ruling party's candidate won.

A day earlier, Akhilesh had urged Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to take immediate cognisance of the alleged irregularities and ensure transparency in the counting process.

He had accused officials of delaying the announcement of round-wise results and warned that the SP would launch a movement and file a case against the Election Commission if any foul play was detected.

Similar allegations were raised by SP candidate Danish Akhtar over the results in the Bareilly-Moradabad Teachers' constituency. Akhtar alleged irregularities in the electoral rolls and voting process, claiming that 30 per cent of the names on the electoral roll were fraudulent.

He also accused the Election Commission of failing to act despite receiving evidence and repeated representations.

SP claims lead in Lucknow constituency

Meanwhile, in Lucknow, Ram Singh Rana, an SP agent for party candidate Kanti Singh, claimed on Wednesday that the party was maintaining its lead during counting. He alleged that BJP candidate Avnish Singh had repeatedly attempted to disrupt the process.

âWe have been steadily increasing our lead since yesterday, and it continues to grow.

The opposition candidate from the BJP made several attempts to misuse power, but the Samajwadi youth did not bow down; they stood firm and remained unafraid--even when there were lathi-charges during the night, and chairs were smashed,â Rana said.

Rana alleged that the opposition had tried to halt the counting process four or five times and that SP workers had faced harassment throughout the night.

"The opposition tried to halt the process four or five times, but no one gave in or felt intimidated.

We have maintained our momentum and are moving toward victory. We faced harassment all night long. The opposition candidate, Avnish Singh, tried to stop the process five times, but we did not back down," Rana said.

World.title: Delhi to Haridwar in 90 minutes? What Nitin Gadkari said
World.content:
The journey from Delhi to Haridwar may soon become significantly shorter, with a new road project scheduled to open next month, union road hransport and Highways minister

said on Tuesday. Once operational, the route could bring travel time down to around 90 minutes.

Speaking at the Confederation of Indian Industryâs (CII) National Conference on âHighways of Indiaâs Future: Smart, Safe and Sustainableâ, Gadkari said the expansion of the countryâs road network was making religious destinations more accessible while supporting tourism and job creation.

Pointing to the recently opened Delhi-Dehradun corridor, the minister said the journey between the two cities, which earlier took about seven hours, could now be completed in roughly two hours.

He said the upcoming Delhi-Haridwar project would further improve access to one of the countryâs prominent pilgrimage destinations, according to ET.

Gadkari also cited road development work in Ayodhya and Maharashtra, including the Pandharpur Palkhi Marg projects, which are intended to make journeys easier for devotees. He said infrastructure development was being undertaken across regions, with roads, tunnels and bridges being built in the Northeast, Jammu and Kashmir and other parts of the country.





Expressways to open up new economic opportunities

Gadkari said greenfield expressways could bring regions with limited economic opportunities closer to major business centres, helping expand development beyond established urban hubs.

The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, he said, would improve access for rural areas, aspirational districts and tribal regions. In Haryana, the project is expected to benefit aspirational districts, while Alwar, Dausa, Sawai Madhopur and Bundi in Rajasthan are among the areas that could gain from improved road links.

He also pointed to Ratlam and Jhabua in Madhya Pradesh and Dahod in Gujarat, highlighting the potential for better connectivity to encourage economic activity in tribal districts.

Stressing the importance of the Delhi-Mumbai route, Gadkari said stronger links between the national capital and Mumbai were crucial, given the latterâs position as the countryâs economic hub.

World.title: Prayagraj’s cultural, literary legacy celebrated at JNU festival
World.content:
NEW DELHI: From its centuries-old traditions of learning and literature to its cultural and spiritual identity, Prayagrajâs legacy took centre stage at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), where over 450 people with connections to the city gathered for âPrayag Utsav 2026â.

Organised by Shankh Initiatives as part of âPrayag-Delhi Sangam 2026â, the festival brought together academics, writers, artists, professionals and former residents of Prayagraj living in Delhi-NCR. The event, held at JNUâs Convention Centre, featured discussions on the cityâs intellectual history, literary contributions and contemporary cultural identity.

Addressing the valedictory session, Uttar Pradesh cabinet minister Nand Gopal Gupta âNandiâ said Prayagrajâs identity extended beyond its geographical boundaries, connecting people through shared memories and traditions.

Referring to the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and the traditionally revered Saraswati, he said the cityâs spiritual and intellectual heritage continued to influence generations. He also acknowledged the efforts of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and UP chief minister Yogi Adityanath in promoting Indiaâs cultural heritage.

Former UP minister Siddharth Nath Singh, who inaugurated the festival, said such initiatives helped connect Prayagrajâs literary and cultural traditions with contemporary academic discourse.





He emphasised the importance of engaging younger generations with their cultural roots.

Professor Anand Shankar Singh, principal of Iswar Saran Degree College, described Prayagrajâs intellectual heritage as a living tradition that continued to shape contemporary thought.

World.title: 'Process becomes punishment in our system': Ex-SC judge Sanjay Kaul on Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam bail pleas
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former

judge Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said that the period before conviction or acquittal has become a "punishment" in India, commenting on the denial of bail to Umar Khalid and

. He said that prolonged legal proceedings can themselves become a form of punishment and that bail should generally be the norm.

In an interview with news agency ANI, Kaul said he had generally taken a liberal view on bail, but acknowledged that certain laws explicitly restrict the granting of bail in specific cases.

"I have taken a generally very liberal view on bail. I feel the bail cannot be the punishment. The conviction is the punishment. In our system, unfortunately, the pre-conviction or acquittal period itself becomes a punishment. The process becomes a punishment," former Supreme Court judge said.

Kaul said several judges had raised concerns about the issue. He also referred to a judgment written by Justice Sundaresh, with whom he had dealt with the question of bail and the principles governing custody.

"And many judges have been writing and talking about it. In fact, I, sitting with Justice Sundaresh, had dealt elaborately with the bail itself, trying to say, why are you people under custody? Justice Sundaresh wrote the judgment.





He's, to my mind, a liberal judge on this. And we tried to lay down norms, etc., which were already in existence, but trying to, you know, until this case. So in most cases, our view is, that bail should be the norm.

But there are certain acts which prohibit bail," said Kaul.

Kaul has co-authored an upcoming memoir, Without Fear or Favour, with Jay Vinayak Ojha. The book is scheduled for release on October 31.

Khalid and Imam are accused under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) in connection with an alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

According to the prosecution, the violence left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.

The riots broke out amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019, and the proposed National Register of Citizens.

On January 5 this year, the Supreme Court denied bail to Khalid and Imam in the case related to the alleged conspiracy behind the 2020 riots. In its judgment, the court observed that the two accused stood on a "qualitatively different footing" in terms of the prosecution's case and the evidence against them.

In September, the Delhi high court had also rejected their bail pleas. The case stems from FIR 59/2020, registered by the Delhi Police Special Cell to investigate the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 northeast Delhi riots.

âMet him only a couple of timesâ: Justice Kaul on Saurav Das

Meanwhile, former Supreme Court judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul also clarified his association with Cockroach Janta Party activist Saurav Das, saying he had met him only a couple of times when Das was working as a journalist and had advised him to "taper down a little" in his language.

Justice Kaul told news agency ANI that a photograph of him with Das, taken at a Diwali gathering about a year ago, was being used to suggest that he shared a particular ideology.

"So, it was one year ago. He was not even in the news then," Justice Kaul said, explaining how the meeting came about.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"He was a journalist, maybe met me a couple of times. He was insistent that I must, at Diwali time, come. I was going somewhere else.

I said, 'Okay, I'll drop in for ten minutes.' I told my wife, 'Have a cup of coffee, I'll drop in for ten minutes, and then we'll go.' That's all that happened," he said.

Asked whether he had mentored Das at any point, Justice Kaul denied doing so, while acknowledging that he had advised the activist on his choice of words.

"I was not mentoring him, but once or twice he met me, I told him that, I will always tell you to taper down a little in your language," he said.

Justice Kaul added that differences in language and expression across generations could sometimes cause discomfort, particularly among those accustomed to more civil forms of conversation.

on Wednesday accused the Modi government of allowing the

World.title: Centre deputes a high-level team to investigate death of Cheetah, caused by firearm pellet injuries, in Madhya Pradesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday deputed a high-level team to investigation the death of a 19-month-old male Cheetah of Kuno National Park, Madhya Pradesh, caused by firearm pellet injuries.

The team has been tasked with undertaking a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death of the Cheetah, examining all available evidence and coordinating closely with the Madhya Pradesh forest department to ensure strict and swift action in the matter.

The 19-month-old radio-collared male cheetah, an offspring of Namibia-born Cheetah Nirva, was found injured on Oct 25 in the territorial forests of Morena, outside the protected area of Kuno National Park.

Preliminary medical examinations corroborated multiple internal injuries associated with the firearm pellets.

The incident, the first reported casualty of a shooting since PM Narendra Modi launched Project Cheetah at Kuno in Sept, 2022, is being viewed quite seriously at the Centre, given the critical importance of Project Cheetah and the need to ensure the highest standards of protection for the reintroduced population of the Big Cat.





âAs reported by the MP forest department, the injured cheetah was rescued from the Sheopur Territorial Forest Division the same day and provided intensive veterinary care and emergency surgery at the veterinary facility in Jabalpur. During the surgery, five firearm pellets were recovered from its body. Despite the medical intervention, the Cheetah succumbed to its injuries on Oct 27,â said the Union environment ministry in a statement.

It said, âThe state govt has already constituted a Special Task Force (STF), comprising forest and police officers, to investigate the incident. The central team deputed by the Union environment ministry would work in coordination with the state machinery. It would also examine the implementation of security protocols, as well as monitoring and protection measures being undertaken to avoid any such incident in future.
